title: Milwaukee by Night
description: Milwaukee, late autumn 1991, after Psychomachia and a failed Sabbat infiltration. Four realms (Waking with Underground levels, Dreaming, Shadowlands, Near Umbra), Kindred domains, ~330 places and ~150 characters.

approx.name: Source gives the area; exact spot placed

waking.name: Waking
waking.date: Autumn 1991, the nights after the Prince’s fall
waking.banner: No Prince · the Sabbat beaten back · Velez still at large
waking.credit: Base map drawn from Milwaukee’s 1991 street grid and shoreline · positions approximate

levels.name: Underground
levels.banner: The Warrens · the Rat Market · things in the tunnels
levels.credit: The sewers, the brewery caves and the Deep Tunnel (built 1986–1993) are real; everything living in them is improvised

dream.name: Dreaming
dream.banner: Nine Kithain · three freeholds · no court
dream.credit: The Dreaming keeps relationships before distances · dotted threads tie places to their mortal anchors

shadow.name: Shadowlands
shadow.banner: One Citadel · newly dead in the streets
shadow.credit: The Shadowlands remember what the living city has torn down · all wraith lore improvised

umbra.name: Umbra
umbra.banner: Three clans, one of them nearly gone · a poisoned forest
umbra.credit: The Penumbra mirrors the city’s spirit, not its streets · every zone, spirit and Garou here is improvised on the book’s Lupine lore

mecca.name: MECCA
mecca.sub: Milwaukee Exposition & Convention Center and Arena
mecca.html:
A sky-walk of enclosed catwalks joins MECCA to the Hyatt Regency, the Arena, the Auditorium and the Reuss Federal Plaza, so that an Elder can cross the whole complex without touching the street or seeing it.

Security is the ghoul Raoul, a former karate champion, and his team of heavily armed mortal guards. Gracis feeds Raoul and calls him a wonderful deterrent against "undesirables". The Anarchs found ways past the ordinary guards years ago; they have not found a way past Raoul.
mecca.brief:
The Milwaukee Exposition & Convention Center and Arena: the Versailles of Kindred Milwaukee. Red carpet, crystal chandeliers, flowerbeds out front and extra police patrols to keep the poor away. The Council of Elders meets here, and several Elders keep havens in the complex.

Every neonate is brought here once to be presented. Anarchs who try to raid it never get far past the lobby.

notes.title: On your first visit
notes.html: You are expected to be awed. The Elders want you to feel how much there is to lose, and slightly excited to be allowed near it.

notes.title: Below the carpet
notes.html: The complex sits on the Council's steam tunnels. Somewhere down there is a boiler room that has been turned into a cell, and Raoul's people take turns guarding it.

hyatt.name: Hyatt Regency
hyatt.html: Carna's favourite haven is here as well, so in Council terms the Toreador and Tremere seats sleep under one roof and can reach the Council chamber without going outside. The staff of the upper floors are well paid not to remember guests.
hyatt.src: Milwaukee by Night, p. 22; Lucina p. 48; Carna p. 53
hyatt.brief: A grand hotel at 333 W Kilbourn Avenue, joined to MECCA by the sky-walk. Elders keep rooms here: Lucina has a permanent suite on the 16th floor, as everyone knows.

arena.name: Milwaukee Arena
arena.html: The Arena is the busiest part of the complex and the easiest to enter. Raoul's guards concentrate on the corridors that lead from it to the Council's rooms.
arena.brief: Part of the sky-walked MECCA complex, between the Auditorium and the Hyatt: hockey, concerts and conventions by night, crowds big enough to feed in.

auditorium.name: Milwaukee Auditorium
auditorium.html:
Concerts are the Council's favourite negotiating venue: the members can reach each other, and the music covers every word. Before a big vote you can see the Councillors whispering and passing notes between their boxes.

The Anarchs resent being shut out. The Elders misread that anger as hatred of music and art, which has led to a good deal of misunderstanding among the Undead.
auditorium.brief: Where the Symphony Orchestra plays. A concert here is a pleasure reserved for the most powerful Elders and the members of the Council; lesser Kindred are not welcome in the private boxes.

reuss.name: H. Reuss Federal Plaza
reuss.html: The federal guards keep the building quiet at night, which suits the Elders. The F.B.I. agents who have been poking around Milwaukee this year keep their files elsewhere, but nobody on the Council likes having federal offices at the end of their corridor.
reuss.alias: A federal building on the sky-walk
reuss.aliasText: The sky-walk ends at a federal office building. Elders use the corridor; you have not been invited to.
reuss.brief: The H. Reuss Federal Plaza, the southern end of the sky-walk: federal offices by day, a sheltered corridor for Elders by night.

journal.name: Milwaukee Journal building
journal.html: The Elders' control of the press is easy from so close. Merik had an arrangement to read tomorrow's edition a day early, and the Council has quietly kept it. Whoever holds the editor will decide how the autumn's "Vampire Murderer" and "Milwaukee Dragon" stories are remembered.
journal.brief: The Milwaukee Journal building, directly across the street from MECCA. Every Kindred in the city enjoys the joke: the greatest newspaper story of all time sleeps across the street, and the editors never notice.

notes.title: Under the presses
notes.html: The Nosferatu keep their rumour archive in the old pneumatic-post vault beneath the building, and listen to the telephone lines from there.

police.name: Police Administration Building
police.html: With the Prince dead, the department is a prize. Lucina wants the administration for an anti-gang crusade; Jason means to keep it out of everyone's hands; Gracis is after the detectives who used to answer to Parovich. Lieutenant James Wilks of homicide works out of here.
police.src: Milwaukee by Night, p. 24; The Pawns pp. 70–71
police.brief: The Police Administration Building, two blocks from MECCA: one of the two great ironies of the city. The Elders are the city's worst criminals, and the police live next door.

notes.title: Masterless detectives
notes.html: Parovich owned the detective bureau. Since his exposure his informants there have no master, and they are frightened people with badges.

notes.title: Wilks knows
notes.html: Lieutenant Wilks knows what Kindred are. He has kept silent so far.

library.name: Milwaukee Public Library
library.html: The first-floor occult section is written by charlatans and checked out by the curious. In the second basement, among old unreadable books that nobody has borrowed for years, is a shelf that no longer appears in the card catalogue.
library.brief: The Milwaukee Public Library, three blocks from MECCA and across from the fire department headquarters: an Elder haunt. Messages are left inside books, and the recipient is told which title to borrow through a harmless remark: "I have been reading about ancient Norwegian tools lately. Fascinating."

notes.title: The second basement
notes.html: A careful search of several nights turns up genuine magical tomes more than six hundred years old. A Tremere would pay dearly for them, and so would the Chapel's archivist.

firehq.name: Fire Department headquarters
firehq.html: Gracis used to control the department. When his men set fire to Hrothulf's haven, the trucks took two hours to arrive. Hrothulf took the brigade for himself and has kept it ever since.
firehq.src: Milwaukee by Night, p. 23; The Fire Department p. 70
firehq.brief: Fire Department headquarters, across the street from the Library. Kindred fear fire, so whoever owns the brigade matters. Everyone knows it belongs to Hrothulf.

notes.title: The last resort
notes.html: If he were ever truly cornered, Hrothulf could make every hose in the city fail and let Milwaukee burn.

museum.name: Milwaukee Public Museum
museum.html: The Toreador value the achievements of mortals and do not understand Akawa's fury at all. The exhibit is still up, and the night guards have been doubled. The Brothers have not forgotten it.
museum.brief: The Milwaukee Public Museum by MacArthur Square. It used to be a Kindred favourite, until it put American Indian bones on display. Akawa's Blood Brothers have attacked it several times, and Lucina's Toreador have retaliated.

cityhall.name: City Hall
cityhall.html: Whoever holds the mayor can fire the police and fire chiefs, and so instantly makes enemies of everyone who owns them. Gracis is weighing it. A losing Elder might grab it as a last resort and turn the whole game over.
cityhall.src: Milwaukee by Night, Downtown map #1; The Mayor p. 71
cityhall.brief: City Hall, east of the river. Merik owned the mayor's office. Nobody has claimed it since he died.

pabst.name: Pabst Theater
pabst.html: The Toreador treat it as part of Lucina's Theatre District. Opening nights are an unofficial Elysium.
pabst.brief: The Pabst Theater on East Wells Street, beside City Hall: gilt, velvet and a good stage for the city's gilded diplomacy.

pac.name: Performing Arts Center
pac.html: Late at night Anarchs break in to put on mocking shows of their own on the empty stage. The Toreador consider this the worst thing that happens in the city.
pac.brief: The Performing Arts Center on the river. Kindred of every kind come to its functions. The Council holds diplomacy sessions during performances.

merikpent.name: Merik’s penthouse (sealed)
merikpent.html: By the end it held dried blood, dead flowers stapled to the walls and a drained aquarium. The Council has not decided what to do with it, or with the vessels, who were moved somewhere quieter.
merikpent.src: Milwaukee by Night, Fire and Blood pp. 83–84; The Unmasking p. 114
merikpent.aliasText: The late Prince lived at the top of a downtown tower. The penthouse has been sealed since he died.
merikpent.brief: Terence Merik's private palace at the top of an East Town tower: plush rugs, spiced blood in crystal goblets and a herd of green-eyed vessels in the back rooms. Sealed by the Council since his death.

notes.title: The ambush
notes.html: Merik's old Nosferatu servant Demetri hid an ambush of ghouls in the penthouse with Obfuscate, for guests the Prince did not want to leave.

stmary.name: Old St. Mary’s Church
stmary.html: The Inquisition meets here to make plans and share what it has learned about Vampires and Werewolves. Merik's standing order was to leave it alone, in the hope that the Inquisition would find nothing in Milwaukee and go away. Nobody has repealed the order, and nobody is sure it still holds.
stmary.brief: Old St. Mary's Church, near the river on the east side. It looks like an ordinary church. In its basement the Society of Leopold keeps a secret base, and the Kindred know it.

notes.title: Merik’s rule
notes.html: Leave the Inquisition alone. Do not give them anything to find.

mac.name: Milwaukee Athletic Club
mac.html: The members are young, attractive and very fit. They can lose more blood without harm, and their strong hearts make it flow faster. Hunting here means crossing the Union's streets, which is part of the thrill.
mac.brief: The Milwaukee Athletic Club, in the middle of Union turf and a favourite hunting ground anyway.

artmuseum.name: Milwaukee Art Museum & War Memorial
artmuseum.html: Elders who do not want to be overheard by the Blood Brothers meet here, and there have been several secret Elder meetings in the building about that gang. The museum now takes its best works down at night and posts guards, but guards can be Dominated.
artmuseum.brief: The Milwaukee Art Museum and War Memorial beside Veterans Park. The Toreador visit often. Turk's Union keeps breaking in to deface the collection.

unionboat.name: The Union’s riverboat
unionboat.html: Turk believes the water makes it safe from fire, which he fears beyond reason. The park's homeless are the Union's herd, so its members rarely go into a fight short of blood.
unionboat.brief: A broken-down riverboat moored on the Veterans Park shore, its bright banners hanging limp and grey. It is the Union's base, and everyone knows Turk sleeps there.

crucible-mp.name: Missing Persons
crucible-mp.html: You will never hear alternative music here. Kindred who hunt at Missing Persons blend in and feed unnoticed, and many of them think of the crowd as a bloated, senseless herd.
crucible-mp.brief: "Persons" to its regulars: several hundred people every night, top-40 hits and a crowd that never gets too wild. The easiest feeding in the Crucible.

crucible-dp.name: Deadman’s Party
crucible-dp.html: Akawa's boys own the back booth. Since his disappearance the mood here is ugly, and strangers who ask about him are asked to step outside.
crucible-dp.brief: Neo-punk, avant-garde noise and the most outlandish drinks known to man. A Blood Brothers hangout; the police have been called more than once.

crucible-an.name: Arabian Nights
crucible-an.html: Elders who find modern music offensive come here. It is very hard to find a bar that plays any older music, so they settle for something soft, simple, a little boring and, above all, not loud.
crucible-an.brief: Across the street from Deadman's Party and its opposite: desert murals, slow dance music and a quiet room. A place to take a date, or find one, if you have money.

crucible-pc.name: Peaches and Cream
crucible-pc.html: The constant sexual tension makes it the easiest hunting ground in the Crucible for anyone who feeds by seduction.
crucible-pc.brief: A singles bar and a meat market for the young, bored and rich. One-night stands start here every night.

crucible-sb.name: Soldier Boy
crucible-sb.html: The regulars know one another, so it is a poor place to meet strangers. Some Kindred who were soldiers in life come only for the atmosphere.
crucible-sb.brief: A reservists' bar with camouflage netting on the walls and old war trophies hanging side by side: bayonets, rifle clips, dud grenades, Civil War cannonballs. The dance floor is tiny.

crucible-hs.name: Howler & Starscape
crucible-hs.html: The bouncers are bribable and the bathrooms are large. Toreador neonates who want to be seen hunt here.
crucible-hs.brief: Two high-class dance clubs with $10–20 covers and gorgeous floors of black steel and mirrors under coloured lights. Loud top-40; nobody comes for the music.

marqint.name: Marquette Interchange
marqint.html: Union gangers hop onto I-794, slip past the Blood Brother lines and climb down into one of the courtyards; the Brothers arrive and battle is joined. The police never patrol it and the homeless cannot get in without a car, so nobody sees.
marqint.brief: Where I-94 meets I-794 and I-43, small concrete courtyards are trapped between the ramps. More Anarch battles are fought here than anywhere else in the city.

mafia.name: The Don’s table, Third Ward
mafia.html: That Elder is Gracis. He uses Mafia money for bribes and for mortal hitmen whose job is to scare his rivals rather than kill them.
mafia.aliasText: Elders say the old Italian Third Ward still belongs to "the family", and that one of the Council owns the family.
mafia.brief: The Don of Milwaukee's organised crime keeps his table in a restaurant in the old Italian Third Ward. Everyone assumes an Elder holds his leash.

notes.title: Chicago’s captains
notes.html: Capone of Chicago has quietly bought influence with some of the Don's captains.

notes.title: The pipeline
notes.html: Whoever thinks to use the family's drug pipeline could leash every street gang in the city.

h-gracis.name: Gracis’s villa
h-gracis.html: Quaint and respectable outside, gaudy modern plastic within. Mafia soldiers watch the street; the house has been attacked by Hrothulf's people more than once and has never fallen.
h-gracis.src: Milwaukee by Night, Gracis p. 56; Scene 14 p. 107
h-gracis.aliasText: Gracis is said to live in a fine old house on the water north of downtown.
h-gracis.brief: A fine 19th-century house on the riverbank north of downtown, the old north end of Kilbourntown. Gracis's haven since he ruled that town.

h-scott.name: Sir Edward Scott’s flat
h-scott.html: It was his favourite of several homes. Nobody has dared claim it, and Jade Riley has not come to see it.
h-scott.brief: Sir Edward Scott's small, elegant flat on the east side near the lake, in the thick of Union turf, where the Black Prince was always welcome. It stands empty now. Anarchs still leave empty bottles and flowers by the door.

h-jason.name: Jason’s tenement penthouse
h-jason.html: Petitioners who bring him questions about Council business are received here, one at a time, and always kept waiting until his watch says otherwise.
h-jason.brief: A run-down little tenement in Walker's Point. Behind one drab door is a grand penthouse; guests are shocked when it opens. Jason's haven.

h-esau.name: Esau’s condo
h-esau.html: From here Esau coaches Turk and the Union against the Blood Brothers. Turk calls him "the man".
h-esau.brief: An expensive condominium just north of downtown, home of an old, hairy Malkavian called Esau.

notes.title: One mind
notes.html: The condo and the Greendale mansion belong to the same Kindred. Esau is Jacob.

h-jacob.name: Jacob’s mansion
h-jacob.sub: Greendale, the edge of Kindred land
h-jacob.html: He gives very good advice. People who take it tend to end up fighting someone he says is his mad brother.
h-jacob.brief: A distinguished mansion at the very edge of Kindred-controlled territory in Greendale, where a fatherly old Malkavian called Jacob receives anyone who has a grievance.

notes.title: One mind
notes.html: Jacob and Esau are the same Kindred. Two homes, one mind, and a war that never ends.

h-parovich.name: Parovich’s mansion (sealed)
h-parovich.html: For years it was scheduled for demolition, and Parovich kept pulling strings to save it. Sabbat messengers came and went unnoticed. The search found letters to Guillem Velez, a map of the tunnels and an empty coffin. Raul, his last childe, still haunts the steps.
h-parovich.src: Milwaukee by Night, Parovich p. 44; Raul p. 46
h-parovich.brief: The condemned 19th-century mansion of the Nosferatu traitor Parovich, among the decaying Highland Boulevard mansions of Concordia. After his exposure the Council searched it and boarded it up.

notes.title: Broken from inside
notes.html: The passage that once linked the cellar to the Warrens was bricked up by the Council. The bricks have since been pushed out from the tunnel side.

h-anastasia.name: Anastasia’s steam tunnel
h-anastasia.html: She moves between empty cellars and storm drains. Kristian visits once a week and always brings her something nice.
h-anastasia.alias: A steam tunnel under a high school
h-anastasia.brief: A dry utility room in the steam tunnels under Washington High School, as far from the hissing electrical gear as possible. Anastasia lives here with a little zoo of stray cats.

h-kristian.name: Kristian’s borrowed basement
h-kristian.html: From here he hid his brother and sisters from Parovich and plotted their sire's fall. Someone else got there first.
h-kristian.brief: The basement of a house in Lincoln Village owned by an elderly couple who can barely get around upstairs and never notice their guest. Kristian's haven.

h-barth.name: Barth’s apartment
h-barth.html: He fears the Union will try to diablerize him for his blood and has been asking around for bodyguards. Raul sleeps on his couch some days.
h-barth.aliasText: Derik Dark lives somewhere in East Downtown. Half the Kindred in the city have his address; the other half have his frequency.
h-barth.brief: Barth's middle-class apartment in East Downtown. Every weeknight from 10 p.m. to 2 a.m. he broadcasts as "Derik Dark" on WBIT.

h-louis.name: Louis Detonas’s apartment
h-louis.sub: Rugs like grass, a chandelier like stars
h-louis.html: He receives only those who dress properly. Toreador neonates come here to be noticed and leave feeling underdressed.
h-louis.alias: An elegant apartment by the cathedral
h-louis.aliasText: The Toreador sculptor lives near Cathedral Square. Neonates who are invited come back talking about the carpets.
h-louis.brief: Louis Detonas's spacious downtown apartment by Cathedral Square: rugs like grass, a chandelier like the stars, sculpture in every room.

notes.title: He lied for Gracis
notes.html: In the late Prince's last weeks, Louis told the Mask what Gracis wanted them to hear about Hrothulf.

h-victor.name: Victor’s hidden havens
h-victor.html: Victor kept several havens, all well hidden in very rich areas. After his death the Chapel cleaned out most of them, but not all.
h-victor.alias: A house among the Lake Drive mansions
h-victor.brief: One of Victor's hidden havens, among the Lake Drive mansions of Shorewood, just past the last Kindred patrol.

notes.title: The safe
notes.html: There are still Vienna papers in a safe here that the Chapel never found.

h-mortius.name: Dr. Mortius’s haunted house
h-mortius.html: His ghoul retainers are skilled fighters and die often, defending him from the Lupine who prowl around the null zone.
h-mortius.aliasText: Mortals swear there is a haunted house near Marquette. Kindred who ask about it are told to stop asking.
h-mortius.brief: A house near Marquette that mortals swear is haunted, and keep away from. Dr. Mortius, a Tremere scholar, lives here and does not like to be disturbed.

notes.title: Haunted House
notes.html: The haunting is a ritual the Tremere banned as a danger to the Masquerade. Mortius learned it before the ban.

h-hrothulf.name: Hrothulf’s house
h-hrothulf.html: The door is patched over bullet holes from Gracis's latest attack, and the basement vault is full of traps. The Lupine have learned to avoid it.
h-hrothulf.src: Milwaukee by Night, Hrothulf p. 57; Scene 17 p. 112
h-hrothulf.aliasText: Hrothulf lives alone somewhere past the Anubi line, and even the Lupine leave his house alone.
h-hrothulf.brief: A modest two-storey suburban house solidly in the Outlands, in Elm Grove, its neighbours demolished for yard space. Hrothulf lives here alone.

h-badr.name: Badr-al-Budur’s condominium
h-badr.html: Anarchs hire her to kill Elders and Elders hire her to kill Anarchs. With the Prince dead, business is about to boom.
h-badr.aliasText: Everyone knows someone who knows how to reach the Assamite. Nobody admits to knowing where she sleeps.
h-badr.brief: A small condominium near the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee. Badr-al-Budur travels the Northwest on contracts but always returns here.

h-decker.name: Decker’s motel
h-decker.html: He keeps no regular haven, fearing the Lupine would find it. Julia Calvin sleeps beside him.
h-decker.src: Milwaukee by Night, Decker p. 37; Julia p. 39
h-decker.alias: A cheap motel near Good Hope
h-decker.aliasText: Decker keeps no haven. He sleeps wherever the patrol ends.
h-decker.brief: A cheap motel on 76th Street just below Good Hope Road, on the Anubi's own patrol line. Mark Decker sleeps in the windowless bathroom.

h-thomas.name: Thomas’s borrowed bedrooms
h-thomas.html: The girls think he is a runaway. He has never fed on any of them.
h-thomas.alias: Borrowed bedrooms on the North Shore
h-thomas.brief: Thomas Gerhieren sleeps in the homes of rich teenage girls from the Outlands high schools in Fox Point and River Hills, whenever their parents are travelling.

h-milo.name: The lakeshore drains
h-milo.html: Milo never sleeps in the same place twice, but he keeps coming back here. On cold nights the pipe breathes.
h-milo.aliasText: Milo says something woke in a drain down by the lake. Everyone has heard the story. Nobody has gone to look.
h-milo.brief: A storm outfall below the North Point bluff. Milo says this is where IT found him: something in a drain pipe that chased him and told him it would eat every Kindred in the city, one by one.

notes.title: IT is real
notes.html: Something really did follow Milo out of these drains. The dead would call it a Spectre.

parkcounty.name: Milwaukee County Stadium
parkcounty.html: Lucina and Hrothulf both keep season box seats, and both pretend not to notice the other.
parkcounty.brief: Milwaukee County Stadium, home of the Brewers. The crowds are big enough to hide enemies from one another, so fights here are rare. The Elders sit in the boxes; the Anarchs sit in the bleachers.

sprecher.name: Sprecher Brewery
sprecher.html: They know the night security guard, whom they have Dominated into submission, and practically walk in through the front gate.
sprecher.brief: Sprecher Brewery on West Oregon Street. After a good ball game the Blood Brothers party here until dawn, with their own music and sometimes their own lighting. The fermenting wort smells wonderful to the dead.

zoo.name: Milwaukee County Zoo
zoo.html: Anarchs dare each other to sample the blood of the most disgusting animals on offer (the water buffalo, for instance).
zoo.brief: The Milwaukee County Zoo at the I-45/I-94 interchange. Not officially Elysium, but the Kindred have agreed not to fight here. Even Elders come in the early hours, after the cleaning crews have gone, to see the animals and relax.

notes.title: The custom
notes.html: No fighting at the Zoo.

medical.name: Milwaukee Regional Medical Complex
medical.html: The danger that someone will come down to restock is half the fun.
medical.brief: The Milwaukee Regional Medical Complex. Anarchs sneak into the refrigerated blood bank just after the nurses have drawn what the emergency room expects to need, and feast, giggling.

notes.title: Upstairs
notes.html: One of the Council keeps a haven in the upper office floors of the complex.

wmpark.name: West Milwaukee Park
wmpark.html: Several failed peace talks between Lucina and Akawa took place here, with Akawa hidden and speaking through one of the Blood Brothers. Ken Elliot's, Country Gardens and Grenadier's are close by, and Kindred sometimes sit in them for the sake of the view of the park.
wmpark.brief: West Milwaukee Park: neutral ground. Kindred throw parties here and meet enemies here safely. On the rare nights the Elders must parley with the Anarchs, they do it here.

notes.title: The custom
notes.html: Enemies may meet here safely.

southgate.name: Southgate Shopping Mall
southgate.html: The security is the result of strings the Elders have pulled to keep the mall free of riff-raff and Anarchs. Several very expensive shops survive almost entirely on Elder custom, and some Elders hold business meetings in the corridors.
southgate.brief: The Southgate Shopping Mall, open until midnight on weekends and patrolled by a great deal of security. Elders shop here rather than rob closed shops; the Anarchs stay away.

hilton.name: Airport Hilton
hilton.html: Both reasons are lies. The Council knows the Anarchs might risk an attack on a visiting official downtown, and a guest out here is easier to watch. Nothing the Milwaukee Kindred want hidden is anywhere near the Hilton.
hilton.brief: The Hilton by Mitchell airport. Visiting Kindred dignitaries and Camarilla officials are lodged here, supposedly because it has the finest rooms in town and makes departure easy.

mitchell.name: General Mitchell International
mitchell.html: Gracis's spies log every arrival. Parovich's network did the same until his exposure; it is being checked and purged, and not all of its people have been found.
mitchell.brief: General Mitchell International: the city's real front door. Every road and railway passes through Lupine country, so most Kindred arrive by a short night flight. Council members meet visiting dignitaries here.

timmerman.name: Lawrence J. Timmerman Airport
timmerman.html: The Anarchs know it well and pick up friends and new allies here. Quietly, some Elders do the same.
timmerman.brief: Lawrence J. Timmerman Airport, on the far side of the city and dangerously close to the Outlands. Few Kindred use it, which means few watch it.

amtrak.name: Milwaukee Road depot (Amtrak)
amtrak.html: For money or a large favour, a sealed car will carry a Vampire through Lupine country unseen and unsmelled.
amtrak.aliasText: The trains run through Lupine country. Kindred who take them arrange something special first.
amtrak.brief: The Milwaukee Road depot. The railways are largely run by the Kindred of Chicago.

port.name: Port of Milwaukee
port.html: Few use it, which makes it the cleverest way in. If Decker ever sealed the city, somebody else would have to watch the ports.
port.aliasText: Some Kindred come by ship. It is slow, but no wolf swims that far.
port.brief: The Port of Milwaukee on Jones Island. Sea travel is safe from the Lupine but slow, and a Vampire must stay out of the sun for days.

fair.name: State Fair Park
fair.html: The Brothers use the grandstand for initiations: a new member runs the track while the gang throws whatever comes to hand.
fair.brief: State Fair Park, deep in Blood Brother country. Its empty grounds and barns make a quiet off-season rumble site.

graceland.name: Graceland Cemetery
graceland.html: The Elders no longer dare come this far from downtown: the Anarchs might interfere. The Anarchs have taken the custom over and spend hours learning every headstone, so they will know the ground when their turn comes.
graceland.brief: Graceland Cemetery, just south of Good Hope Road: one of the famous dueling grounds. In the early 1900s the Elders settled their quarrels here. Now the Anarchs fight their own duels here instead.

army.name: U.S. Army Reserve Center
army.html: Nobody knows whether the F.B.I. knows about Vampires, and nobody wants to help them find out. The base is not heavily secured, but it is a military base: fences, barbed wire and guards.
army.brief: The U.S. Army Reserve Center. Merik declared it off limits, and whoever rules next will probably keep it that way: the F.B.I. has run an operation from here for months.

notes.title: The Prince’s rule
notes.html: Off limits. Stay away from the Reserve Center.

jungleman.name: Jungleman
jungleman.html: He also buys blood from Anarchs who are short of money. Where he came from and what he is doing in Milwaukee remain a mystery.
jungleman.brief: A small dance bar on West Townsend Street beside Wanderers Rest Cemetery, owned by the ghoul Vrasks. Everyone knows what he sells: he will kill anybody, or so he says, for enough Kindred blood to keep himself immortal.

notes.title: His master
notes.html: Vrasks's original master is still in the city and secretly backs him.

mountmary.name: Mount Mary College
mountmary.html: The Church is a feminist order that wants to take the world back to the days before a patriarchal God. Its members worship nature, and seven or eight of them have real talent for witchcraft.
mountmary.alias: A small college in the north-west
mountmary.aliasText: Kindred avoid Mount Mary College. Nobody explains why.
mountmary.brief: Mount Mary College, a small college that does creditable work in the humanities. The Kindred avoid it: it is the source of a women's occult society called the Church of Isis.

notes.title: Mortius’s dowsers
notes.html: Dr. Mortius uses the Church's witches to search the city for the magical disturbance without risking himself. The other Tremere would be appalled.

notes.title: The Lupine connection
notes.html: The order makes frequent trips into the wilds. Rumour ties it to the Lupine, and Mortius would very much like to know whether that is true.

brynwood.name: Brynwood Country Club
brynwood.html: The Anubi sweep the eleventh hole every night. They have still lost Kindred here.
brynwood.brief: One of the largest country clubs along Good Hope Road. Its fairways and tree lines are perfect ambush cover for the Lupine.

tripoli.name: Tripoli Country Club
tripoli.html: Its clubhouse has been closed early every night since the summer; the members have been told it is about bears.
tripoli.brief: The other great country club on Good Hope Road. Anarchs "doing Good Hope" floor it past here.

joanarc.name: St. Joan of Arc Chapel
joanarc.html: A mage had it moved to the centre of the zone so that he could study the anomaly. The Lupine killed him.
joanarc.src: Milwaukee by Night, History p. 13; Downtown map #10
joanarc.alias: A small stone chapel at Marquette
joanarc.aliasText: There is a medieval chapel in the middle of Marquette. Thaumaturgists talk about it in the same breath as the null zone.
joanarc.brief: St. Joan of Arc Chapel, a 15th-century French chapel moved stone by stone to the Marquette campus in the 1960s. It stands at the heart of the null zone.

notes.title: Usla’s totems
notes.html: Under the chapel lie the Talon of the Eagle and the Eye of the Coyote, the halves of two Lupine totems, stolen by the outcast Usla three centuries ago and reshaped as his own hand and left eye. Whoever recovers them becomes nearly unbeatable and is hunted by every Lupine alive.

notes.title: The Chapel’s ritual
notes.html: The Tremere have placed four anchors around the city whose diagonals cross exactly over this chapel.

marquette.name: Marquette University
marquette.html: It is not truly dead: there is too much magic here, and it drowns out spells. Several independent Kindred have discovered it as well as the Tremere, and most Kindred with an interest in Thaumaturgy know about it. Tremere, Lupine and Anarchs all prowl the campus.
marquette.aliasText: Magic does not work at Marquette. Every Tremere in the city knows it, and some of them say so.
marquette.brief: Marquette University, a few harmless cults and a "dead" zone for magic that covers nearly the whole campus and peaks around the central plaza. Thaumaturgy simply fails here.

notes.title: An Inquisitor on the faculty
notes.html: A member of the Society of Leopold teaches here.

sinai.name: Mount Sinai Medical Center
sinai.sub: Northern edge of the null zone
sinai.html: Kindred who feed here at night find their Thaumaturgy failing on the south side of the building and working again on the north.
sinai.brief: Mount Sinai Medical Center. The null zone reaches north past the hospital.

childrens.name: Old Children’s Hospital
childrens.sub: Western edge of the null zone
childrens.html: The Tremere have mapped the zone's edge here street by street.
childrens.alias: An old hospital on Wisconsin Avenue
childrens.brief: The old Children's Hospital on Wisconsin Avenue, the western edge of the null zone.

foresthome.name: Forest Home Cemetery
foresthome.html: The dueling grounds are scattered across the city, usually cemeteries where the police can be steered away. The Graves charge a toll to anyone who wants to use this one.
foresthome.src: Milwaukee by Night, History p. 14 (“scattered across the city”)
foresthome.brief: Forest Home Cemetery, the grandest Victorian cemetery in the city: one of the dueling grounds of the Elder war of 1901–06, isolated enough that friends cannot hide nearby. The Graves, a minor Caitiff gang, haunt it.

calvary.name: Calvary Cemetery
calvary.html: Nobody ever collected. The Brothers hold a wake here for Scott on the first Friday of every month, and do not say whether it is for him or against him.
calvary.brief: Calvary Cemetery on the hill above Bluemound Road, another dueling ground. Sir Edward Scott and Akawa nearly killed each other here more than once; Kindred laid bets on every bout.

g-scorpions.name: Scorpions turf
g-scorpions.html: The Brothers feed on them now and then, and the Scorpions have started to notice that their missing members come home pale.
g-scorpions.src: Milwaukee by Night, War of Tribes p. 87
g-scorpions.brief: Turf of the Scorpions, a dangerous and violent mortal gang next to Blood Brother territory. They jeer at strangers at red lights but will not attack unless provoked.

g-disp.name: The Dispossessed
g-disp.html: One of the minor Caitiff gangs that Gracis and Lucina, and Parovich before them, courted as a counterweight to Akawa. They took the money and did nothing.
g-disp.alias: A Caitiff gang in the rail yards
g-disp.brief: The Dispossessed: two Caitiff and six mortals in the Menomonee Valley rail yards.

g-dark.name: The Darkboys
g-dark.html: No threat to anyone yet. With Akawa gone, they have started talking as if they might become one.
g-dark.alias: A Caitiff crew on the south side
g-dark.brief: The Darkboys: one Caitiff, two ghouls and four mortals around Clarke Square on the near south side.

g-war.name: Warlords
g-war.html: Their leader bought a charm from the tattoo parlour in Bay View before the invasion and has not taken it off since.
g-war.alias: A Caitiff gang on Teutonia Avenue
g-war.brief: The Warlords: one Vampire and four ghouls along Teutonia Avenue on the north side.

lup-cave.name: The Mouse pack’s cave
lup-cave.html: This autumn the Mouse pack riddled a Kindred car with machine-gun fire on Route 43 and threw the survivors into this cave. Horatio's Coyote broke the Mouse pack's hold and let them go.
lup-cave.src: Milwaukee by Night, A Midnight Moon pp. 99–106
lup-cave.brief: A cave with a three-foot entrance in the Milwaukee River ravines near Mequon, off a dark stretch of Route 43 north. The Mouse pack used it as a den.

notes.title: The Justicar
notes.html: At the back of the cave lay the fresh remains of the Justicar who should have come to investigate the Vampire Murders.

lup-coyote.name: Coyote rendezvous
lup-coyote.html: The pack is Red Talons, wolves to the bone, with exactly as much humanity as the job requires. Horatio plans even when he seems to be talking.
lup-coyote.brief: The quarry country past Menomonee Falls, where the Coyote pack gathers. Horatio Sims, its leader, takes human shape only to negotiate.

notes.title: What Horatio wants
notes.html: All he needs is the Kindred distracted long enough to hold Marquette and dig.

lup-eagle.name: Eagle staging ground
lup-eagle.html: The pack is almost entirely Wendigo. If the Anubi falter even once, the Eagle will push into the inner city; three or four would get through and die there, but Kindred losses would be severe. This autumn the blighted woods keep them home.
lup-eagle.brief: The Root River woods of Franklin, where the Eagle pack stages its raids on the city, roughly once a week.

notes.title: Seven Fires
notes.html: The pack has kin among the city's Native Americans and secretly owns the Seven Fires casino.

lup-usla.name: Where Usla went into the lake
lup-usla.html: Lupines have converged on the area ever since without knowing why.
lup-usla.brief: The lakeshore where, the Lupine say, the dying Usla crawled into Lake Michigan three centuries ago and was never seen again.

hist-1674.name: Manhanawaukee-Seepe
hist-1674.html: Among them was a scout called Petre Dubois, who vanished every dawn and married into the Chippewa.
hist-1674.aliasText: Kindred history in Milwaukee is older than the city. Elders say it began with the Jesuits.
hist-1674.brief: Manhanawaukee-Seepe, the tribal gathering place where the rivers meet. In 1674 Père Marquette's party camped here.

notes.title: Petre Dubois
notes.html: Petre Dubois was Hrothulf. He later Embraced his Chippewa wife, Chiclena, and her war against the Menominee brought the outcast Lupine Usla here.

hist-juneau.name: Juneautown (1818)
hist-juneau.html: He drew French Kindred down from Canada, and for a decade or two Juneautown was the most civilised Kindred settlement west of Detroit.
hist-juneau.brief: Juneautown, Solomon Juneau's settlement east of the river, founded in 1818. Hrothulf moved in early, dominated its leaders and became its Prince.

hist-kilbourn.name: Kilbourntown (1834)
hist-kilbourn.html: Their war of assassins left almost every other Kindred in the area dead by 1840. Kilbourntown once aimed a loaded cannon across the river at Juneautown, though it never fired. In 1845 Gracis staged the riot that brought the bridges down, and a Nosferatu Justicar finally forced a truce.
hist-kilbourn.brief: Kilbourntown, Byron Kilbourn's town west of the river, founded in 1834, already had a Prince: Gracis Nostinus, Hrothulf's blood-brother and sworn enemy.

hist-1900.name: New Year’s Eve, 1900
hist-1900.html: How the border watch failed has never been explained. Mark Decker had warned the Council beforehand. The palace site has been lost; this marker is symbolic.
hist-1900.brief: New Year's Eve, 1900: the night the Lupine got into the city. Prince Erik Pointene died defending his palace, and Terence Merik led the counter-attack that saved Kindred Milwaukee and made his name.

notes.title: Who opened the border
notes.html: Some of the old Anubi believe someone inside the city let the watch fail on purpose. They have never been able to prove whom it served.

ps-house.name: Ruins of Merik’s hilltop house
ps-house.sub: Where the Prince met Final Death
ps-house.html: The house had a basement dungeon. A police lieutenant was held there and walked out of the fire alive.
ps-house.src: Milwaukee by Night, Dreams of Madness pp. 118–123
ps-house.alias: A burned house above the Menomonee
ps-house.aliasText: The Prince died when his house on a hill above the river burned. The fire trucks took their time.
ps-house.brief: The ruins of Terence Merik's hilltop house on the bluffs above the Menomonee River Parkway, at the very edge of the Outlands. The Prince met his Final Death here when it burned this October.

notes.title: The dungeon
notes.html: Merik drugged and chained the Mask in the dungeon here, and held Lieutenant Wilks as well. The Mask destroyed him in the burning house, and Wilks ran to meet the fire trucks and kept his silence.

ps-roof.name: Lisa Urgen’s rooftop trap
ps-roof.html: This autumn the Inquisitor Lisa Urgen trapped a group of Kindred on its roof with a flamethrower and ten minutes until sunrise. They got away.
ps-roof.src: Milwaukee by Night, War of Tribes pp. 95–96
ps-roof.alias: A burnt-out hotel on the lake
ps-roof.brief: An abandoned lakeside hotel on the Bay View shore, gutted by fire years ago: fish wallpaper and carved dolphins.

ps-lot.name: The abandoned factory lot
ps-lot.html: The Union struck on the Prince's orders, though none of them could tell you so.
ps-lot.src: Milwaukee by Night, War of Tribes p. 88
ps-lot.brief: A lot behind an abandoned factory in the Menomonee Valley, where the Union ambushed the Blood Brothers this autumn: motorcycle jousts among broken glass.

notes.title: Dominated
notes.html: The Union had been under Merik's Domination and Blood Bond for years.

ps-scene.name: Fresh murder scene
ps-scene.html: The killings stopped when the Prince died. The Council's story is that a rogue Kindred was responsible and that the matter has been settled.
ps-scene.brief: Near Brady Street, where one of the "Vampire Murderer" victims was found this autumn. The Journal put four drained bodies on its front page, and the Masquerade has not recovered.

notes.title: The killer
notes.html: The Vampire Murderer was Prince Merik himself.

notes.title: A watcher
notes.html: At one of the scenes a Lupine was seen slipping away to report to the Union.

f-hearth.name: The Last Hearth storefront
f-hearth.sub: Marta’s alterations shop, near Mitchell Street
f-hearth.html: Most months the Spare Chair Supper is held here. The absentee landlord is weighing a better-paying tenant; he is an ordinary man, not anyone's pawn.
f-hearth.alias: An alterations shop near Mitchell Street
f-hearth.brief: A rented storefront near Mitchell Street where Marta takes in alterations and cooks community suppers: a cluttered tailoring counter with a back kitchen.

notes.title: The Last Hearth
notes.html: This is the waking face of the Last Hearth, the changeling freehold of the city.

f-counter.name: Juneau Avenue bascule bridge
f-counter.html: A troll called Oren Voss keeps a small private refuge beside the machinery.
f-counter.src: Unclaimed City p. 9, 19 (bridge chosen for play)
f-counter.brief: The Juneau Avenue bascule bridge, on the old Chestnut Street site where the bridges came down in 1845. City bridge tenders do their ordinary work here.

notes.title: The Counterweight
notes.html: Oren's refuge is the Counterweight, a changeling freehold whose road still demands a white flag.

f-shop.name: Leon’s repair shop
f-shop.sub: A rented bay in the Menomonee Valley
f-shop.html: It counts as a place of power only while people are inventing in it. It is not a freehold.
f-shop.alias: A repair shop in the Menomonee Valley
f-shop.brief: A rented repair bay in the Menomonee Valley: audio gear and industrial controls on the benches, a tram prototype under a tarp, and a brass dog that is not his. Leon Mercer works here.

f-hall.name: Riverwest practice hall
f-hall.sub: Where the Standing Ovation opens most reliably
f-hall.html: She has cancelled two rehearsals here since the applause started continuing after the room emptied.
f-hall.brief: A neighbourhood hall in Riverwest with folding chairs, a piano missing two keys and the best acoustics Nina Salazar can afford.

f-pabst.name: 100 East Wisconsin
f-pabst.html: Everything that survived of the Hall of the Copper Hart survives only in the Dreaming, where the Unbuilt Stair still begins.
f-pabst.brief: A new office tower, finished in 1989, where the Pabst Building rose over the old city from 1891 to 1981. There are no ruins here.

f-domes.name: Mitchell Park Domes
f-domes.html: One of the gardeners, Arthur Saye, draws impossible gardens on the backs of discarded forms.
f-domes.aliasText: The three glass domes in Mitchell Park hold a jungle, a desert and a garden. Kindred like them in winter.
f-domes.brief: The Mitchell Park Domes: three glass domes holding a rain forest, a desert and a seasonal show garden through the Wisconsin winter.

notes.title: The Glass Orchard
notes.html: The Domes anchor the Glass Orchard, a realm of the Dreaming.

f-celia.name: Celia’s rented room
f-celia.sub: Beginner cello lessons, Lower East Side
f-celia.html: The rent comes out of the last of her savings.
f-celia.alias: A rented room on the Lower East Side
f-celia.brief: A second-floor room on the Lower East Side with a music stand, a patched coat on the door and a letter to a sponsor that never gets posted. Celia Ashdown gives beginner cello lessons here.

f-ruth.name: Ruth’s kitchen table
f-ruth.html: She runs courier and driving jobs from the phone on the wall.
f-ruth.alias: A kitchen table in Sherman Park
f-ruth.brief: Ruth Bell's kitchen in Sherman Park: bus schedules under a glass tabletop, a road atlas worn soft, coffee for anyone who wants to argue about the best way to a real destination.

f-kit.name: Kinnickinnic Avenue junk shops
f-kit.html: Kit Navarro's bicycle is usually chained outside, freshly repaired by Oren.
f-kit.brief: Secondhand stores and Saturday tables on Kinnickinnic Avenue, where abandoned futures are sold cheap: an instrument after two bad lessons, a half-sewn costume, a child's outdated map.

f-bjorn.name: Inner Harbor docks
f-bjorn.html: In the locker, wrapped in a fisherman's sweater, is the only working scale-light lantern anyone in the city knows of.
f-bjorn.brief: Irregular dock work and repairs on the Inner Harbor. Bjorn Halvorsen keeps a locker here.

f-ivory.name: Ivory’s high school
f-ivory.html: She dislikes the place and leans on its routine to stay steady.
f-ivory.brief: A north-side public high school: bells, hall passes and assignments with a comprehensible end. A grumpy girl called Ivory sits in the back row.

notes.title: The last overseer
notes.html: None of her classmates suspects that the girl in the back row is the last overseer of the Michigan Pocket.

f-lola.name: Lola Wendt’s apartment
f-lola.sub: Playbills, newsletters, and a leaking basement
f-lola.html: She holds a duplicated 1980 supper invitation that puts two supposedly unrelated incidents on the same night.
f-lola.brief: Lola Wendt's apartment: playbills, newsletters and a leaking basement. Right now she mostly needs boxes and two people with a car.

f-eddie.name: Eddie Rusk’s ghost club
f-eddie.sub: Back room of a south-side bowling alley
f-eddie.html: A newer member has started publishing names and addresses without consent, and Eddie has to choose between the club and the people it says it protects.
f-eddie.alias: The back room of a bowling alley
f-eddie.brief: The back room of a south-side bowling alley, where Eddie Rusk's amateur ghost club investigates hauntings over pitchers of beer.

f-warren.name: A door left unforced
f-warren.sub: Mortal approach to the Low Candle Way
f-warren.html: Being seen here exposes someone's movements. It does not give the observer a road anywhere else.
f-warren.alias: A service door under the Wisconsin Avenue bridge
f-warren.brief: A service door under the Wisconsin Avenue bridge that leads into the old Nosferatu warrens. Nobody forces it.

notes.title: The arrangement
notes.html: The sluagh and the Nosferatu once shared the work of the Michigan Pocket. That ended when Parovich went over to the Sabbat; Ivory's arrangement with individual Nosferatu may now be no bigger than this door staying unforced.

c-jade-floor.name: Jade Riley’s floor
c-jade-floor.sub: A whole storey of an office tower on East Michigan Street
c-jade-floor.html: It was bought through a shell company of her grandsire's. A library, a gym and a reception hall where nobody has yet been received. The lights go on and off every evening.
c-jade-floor.brief: The new Brujah Primogen's official haven: the entire twentieth floor of a glass tower on East Michigan Street. Everyone knows the address; that is the point.

notes.title: Timers
notes.html: The floor is empty. The lights run on timers. Jade Riley has not slept here since the fight at the fish plant.

c-macy-house.name: Macy Carver’s house
c-macy-house.html: The house is inside the Anubi patrol zone.
c-macy-house.brief: A small suburban house in Wauwatosa with peeling blue paint, bought with Macy Carver's trust fund: protest posters, stacks of zines, a windowless basement behind a reinforced door.

notes.title: Jade sleeps here
notes.html: This is where the Brujah Primogen really sleeps. Decker knows exactly who is staying here.

c-rusty.name: The Rusty Nail
c-rusty.sub: Punk basement where Jamie Robinson sings
c-rusty.html: Union Anarchs and Blood Brothers come to the same shows and pretend not to see each other. Macy Carver finds half her counterculture contacts in the crowd.
c-rusty.brief: A cramped Riverwest basement club: sticky floor, a home-built stage and the best sound in town. Jamie Robinson's band, the Rust Saints, plays here.

notes.title: The custom
notes.html: Nobody starts anything during the set.

c-gas-lot.name: The lot where the gas station stood
c-gas-lot.sub: The Robinson family station on Highway 41
c-gas-lot.brief: An empty pad on Highway 41 where the Robinson family's gas station stood for thirty years, until it was condemned for a widening. One morning the demolition crew found no foundations, no pumps and no fuel stains.

notes.title: Where it went
notes.html: Ivory carried the station off to the Michigan Pocket. Jamie knows where it went and does not know how he feels about it.

c-chapel.name: The Chapel
c-chapel.sub: Tremere chantry · a brewer’s mansion on Highland Boulevard
c-chapel.html: The chantry's researchers work and sleep here. Since Victor's death this autumn the link to Vienna is a formality, and the Chapel draws on unorthodox resources more freely every week. Luke Newman runs its security for now and keeps a visitors' log.
c-chapel.brief: The Chapel: the Tremere chantry in an old beer baron's mansion on Highland Boulevard ("Sauerkraut Boulevard"), a few blocks west of the edge of the null zone. No Tremere comes to Milwaukee without Vienna's leave.

notes.title: Who really runs it
notes.html: Carna heads the Tremere on paper. In practice Dr. Mortius sets the Chapel's work.

c-victor-death.name: The Chapel’s east wing
c-victor-death.html: A Lupine of the Mouse pack, already twisted by the Wyrm, walked through the wards as if they were not there. Newman has rebuilt the defences and will not say what let the creature in.

notes.title: From inside
notes.html: The wards were weakened from inside. Jesselin found a way in through Haberman's social correspondence and slipped Drake the "key".

c-victor-death.aliasText: Somebody died inside the Chapel this autumn. The Tremere are not discussing it.
c-victor-death.brief: The east wing of the Chapel, sealed since Victor, Vienna's watchdog in Milwaukee, was killed in his own laboratory this autumn.

c-isis.name: Temple of the Church of Isis
c-isis.sub: An esoteric church on Brady Street
c-isis.html: This is the city temple of the Church of Isis. Its inner circle drinks blood and keeps the Chapel's secrets.
c-isis.alias: An incense shop on Brady Street
c-isis.brief: Above an incense shop on Brady Street: a room with blue walls, sistrums and a copy of Isis nursing Horus. To its congregation it is a neo-Egyptian fellowship with Thursday meditations.

notes.title: Ghouls
notes.html: Two of the inner circle, Kayla and Arianna, are ghouls. Kayla serves Jade Riley and Dr. Mortius at once.

c-uwm.name: University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee
c-uwm.sub: Where Arianna studies and Doctor Fire teaches
c-uwm.html: An Egyptology student called Arianna runs between lectures and somewhere she does not discuss. One floor down, in the archaeology department, teaches a professor with burn scars on his hands.
c-uwm.brief: The University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee campus in the city's north-east corner. Students, late lectures and a lot of easy vessels.

notes.title: Doctor Fire
notes.html: The archaeology professor is "Doctor Fire", the brains of a small group of vampire hunters.

c-711.name: The empty corner
c-711.html: A former night clerk comes back here every night without knowing why, a couple of cab drivers have an address in their logs that does not exist, and a soda distributor keeps billing a customer nobody can find.
c-711.brief: A weedy lot at Wisconsin Avenue and 25th Street that looks untouched for decades. There was a 7-Eleven here. Probably.

notes.title: What happened
notes.html: Annalena stopped here while fleeing the Gloaming Keep, and that was the last thing that ever happened to the store. The Mists wiped it from nearly everyone's memory.

c-warehouses.name: The railside warehouses
c-warehouses.html: Dragos Dalca kept his workshops here. Behind Warehouse No. 7 a ramp wide enough for a truck leads down into the underground, hidden by little more than a wall. The Council has put a grate and two ghouls on it.
c-warehouses.aliasText: The Sabbat came up through Cudahy. Nobody goes into the railside warehouses now.
c-warehouses.brief: Rusting sheds between the railway and the meatpacking plant in Cudahy. During the invasion the Sabbat's creatures came out of here, and the Camarilla has guarded the place ever since.

c-breach1.name: Masquerade breach No. 1
c-breach1.sub: A dragon on the late news
c-breach1.html: The Nosferatu and Gracis's people are still hunting down copies. "The Milwaukee Dragon" has become an urban legend and a talk-radio staple. The thing on the tape was Dragos Dalca, the Sabbat's Tzimisce elder.
c-breach1.brief: Masquerade breach No. 1. A late-news crew filming a car crash on Kinnickinnic Avenue caught something huge, winged and scaled chasing three running figures over the rooftops. The tape aired once.

c-breach2.name: Masquerade breach No. 2 · the fish plant
c-breach2.html: Dragos took his raw material here: off the conveyors, and from the homeless his servants trucked in from under the viaducts. The plant is closed and still cordoned off. Pieces of things that were neither fish nor human were found in the wreckage.
c-breach2.brief: Masquerade breach No. 2: Lakeside Fish Processing. In front of hundreds of witnesses on the neighbouring piers, the Camarilla fought the Sabbat's creatures here, and Jade Riley killed the Sabbat's dragon, Dragos Dalca, with her bare hands. Officially, an ammonia explosion.

c-viaduct.name: The camp under the viaduct
c-viaduct.html: They were taken to the fish plant. Some came back in a form nobody here talks about.
c-viaduct.aliasText: The homeless under the viaduct say people were taken all autumn. Nobody listened.
c-viaduct.brief: Tents and barrel fires under the freeway viaduct. All autumn people vanished from here, two or three at a time, and nobody cared except the homeless themselves.

c-guillem-church.name: St. Jude’s, closed
c-guillem-church.html: The Camarilla found it empty. Velez left a day before the raid.
c-guillem-church.alias: A closed church in Walker’s Point
c-guillem-church.aliasText: The Camarilla raided a church in Walker's Point during the invasion and found it empty.
c-guillem-church.brief: St. Jude's, a boarded-up church in Walker's Point. The Sabbat commander Guillem Velez ran the infiltration from here: city maps on the sacristy walls, the stains of a Vaulderie on the altar.

notes.title: Someone warned him
notes.html: Velez was warned of the raid. The warning came from someone on the Camarilla side.

c-guillem-boat.name: The yacht Santa Eulàlia
c-guillem-boat.html: Guillem Velez sleeps here some days. He never spends more than two days running anywhere.
c-guillem-boat.alias: A yacht in the McKinley marina
c-guillem-boat.brief: A decommissioned yacht under a borrowed name, the Santa Eulàlia, at the McKinley moorings. The hold is blacked out and the portholes painted over from inside.

c-maximus-shop.name: Charms & Needles
c-maximus-shop.sub: Maximus McKenzie’s tattoo parlour · Bay View
c-maximus-shop.html: The shop is shut and the sign is gone. Maximus vanished when the Sabbat invasion failed, and the Council would like a word. Some of his charms are still around their owners' necks.
c-maximus-shop.alias: A tattoo parlour in Bay View
c-maximus-shop.aliasText: Half the Caitiff in the city wore a charm from a Bay View tattoo shop before the invasion. The shop is shut and the tattooist is gone.
c-maximus-shop.brief: Charms & Needles, Maximus McKenzie's tattoo parlour in Bay View, with a shelf of amulets in the window. Through the back door he sold Union Caitiff and Anarchs cheap blood-magic charms: wards, silencers, "luck in a fight".

notes.title: Sabbat blood
notes.html: Every piece was made with Sabbat blood and tied its owner to Maximus a little. He was a Tremere of House Goratrix.

c-jesselin.name: A suite at the Pfister
c-jesselin.html: She is never seen at lunch itself, only at the coffee afterwards.
c-jesselin.aliasText: The Pfister is the city's oldest grand hotel. Its top floor has a new long-term guest.
c-jesselin.brief: The Pfister, the city's oldest grand hotel. A new patroness of the opera, "Miss Lascelles", keeps a suite on the top floor and lunches with a city councilman's wife.

notes.title: Jesselin
notes.html: "Miss Lascelles" is Jesselin, a sorceress of House Goratrix, the Sabbat's Tremere. A copper scrying bowl stands in her bathroom and a mirror draped in black velvet in her wardrobe.

c-ethan.name: Ethan Stone’s roost
c-ethan.sub: The roof of a grain elevator · Menomonee Valley
c-ethan.html: Ethan Stone keeps his bows and bundles of arrows here and sleeps in an empty grain bin.
c-ethan.alias: A grain elevator in the valley
c-ethan.brief: A concrete grain elevator above the Menomonee Valley. From the roof there is a clear shot over half of Blood Brother turf.

c-dominique.name: Dominique’s flat
c-dominique.html: There is still a black scorch on the kitchen ceiling. The neighbours think a frying pan exploded.
c-dominique.aliasText: A Kindred who went to check on a Blood Brothers errand-boy in Riverwest did not come back.
c-dominique.brief: The fourth floor of a shabby public housing block in Riverwest. A Camarilla vampire died in this kitchen, burned down by a kid called Dominique with a lighter and a can of air freshener.

c-gunther.name: Gunther’s boathouse
c-gunther.html: Merik granted him the river in the 1930s. Nobody has had the nerve to ask whether the grant died with the Prince.
c-gunther.aliasText: An old Gangrel lives on the river above the North Avenue dam. He was here before the city had a name.
c-gunther.brief: An old boathouse on the pond above the North Avenue dam: upturned boats, nets and the smell of pipe smoke and wet fur. Gunther has lived on this water since the city was Kilbourntown.

notes.title: A visitor
notes.html: Sometimes Mercer comes here: the last Garou of the Mouse pack.

c-soraya.name: The house that isn’t there
c-soraya.html: There is no electricity, gas or water; at night the windows burn with candles. The Kiasyd Soraya lives here with her mad sire.
c-soraya.brief: A large old manor of chimneys, gables and ivy on Yankee Hill, a few blocks from downtown, on a spot no city map shows. Passers-by turn aside before they reach the wall and do not remember turning.

notes.title: Sideways
notes.html: A rare marriage of Dominate and Umbral mysticism folds the house a few blocks "sideways" from the street.

c-hunters.name: Wolfgang’s garage
c-hunters.sub: The hunters’ hideout and armoury · West Allis
c-hunters.html: Under a false floor in the inspection pit: stakes, jugs of gasoline, a crossbow, two Scandinavian-forged swords and a crate of Doctor Fire's books. Pinned over the invoices is a map of the city's havens, wrong in places and right in the worst ones.
c-hunters.brief: A two-bay garage in West Allis: Wolfgang's auto repair. Oil, invoices, a radio playing polka.

notes.title: A well-wisher
notes.html: Sometimes someone leaves a dried flower on a car hood, or a child's drawing with a hint in it. The hunters think they have a secret well-wisher. They are right: Ivory helps them.

c-casino.name: Seven Fires Bingo & Casino
c-casino.sub: Secretly owned by the Eagle pack
c-casino.html: The casino pays for lawyers and land and buys influence with community councils.
c-casino.alias: A bingo hall on the south side
c-casino.brief: Seven Fires Bingo & Casino: a loud hall of bingo and slot machines on the south side. The owners of record are Native American families of the city.

notes.title: The real owner
notes.html: The Eagle pack of Lupines owns it. It gives the Wendigo a place to meet people without leaving their own.

c-mercer.name: The telephone exchange
c-mercer.sub: Where Mercer works the night shift
c-mercer.html: He listens to the city down the wires.
c-mercer.brief: A brick telephone-company building full of switching frames. A night technician called Mercer works here.

notes.title: The last Mouse
notes.html: Mercer is the last Garou of the Mouse pack.

c-blight.name: The blighted groves
c-blight.sub: Defiled places of power in the Root River woods
c-blight.html: Things crawl up out of the ground here at night. The Eagle pack of Lupines fights them every night, which is why it was not watching the city when the Sabbat came in.
c-blight.alias: Dying groves in the Root River woods
c-blight.brief: Old groves in the Root River woods where the undergrowth is dying and the creeks smell of copper.

notes.title: Who poisoned them
notes.html: Maximus McKenzie and Jesselin of House Goratrix poisoned these places of power with blood magic, so that Banes would keep the Lupine busy.

c-anchor-e.name: Anchor East · the North Point Water Tower
c-anchor-e.html: Inside the shaft, ringed around the standpipe under the lamp-room, someone has mounted a coil of copper antennae.
c-anchor-e.brief: The Gothic North Point Water Tower of 1873 on the Lake Park bluff.

notes.title: Anchor East
notes.html: It is one of the four anchors of the Chapel's ritual. The tower holds water, water holds reflections, and the lake is the biggest mirror in the city: this anchor "looks" at the null zone through water.

notes.title: Truce ground
notes.html: The tower stands on the ground of the Lake Park Truce. The Lupine would call this a provocation.

c-anchor-s.name: Anchor South · the roof of the Hotel Warszawa
c-anchor-s.html: From the roof you can see the dome of St. Josaphat's, built from another city's stones, and the Allen-Bradley clock the neighbourhood calls the Polish Moon.
c-anchor-s.brief: A tired old hotel on Lincoln Avenue in the Polish district, with a neon crown on its roof and a new TV aerial beside it.

notes.title: Anchor South
notes.html: The "TV aerial" is one of the four anchors of the Chapel's ritual. It draws on the "reassembled" holiness of the basilica and on a clock that tells its own time.

c-anchor-w.name: Anchor West · the mound in the Root River woods
c-anchor-w.sub: Deep in the parkway forest, south-west
c-anchor-w.html: A tripod wrapped in willow withies stands on top of it.
c-anchor-w.alias: A mound in the Root River woods
c-anchor-w.brief: A slumped mound in a clearing among old oaks deep in the Root River parkway, on no survey.

notes.title: Anchor West
notes.html: One of the four anchors of the Chapel's ritual. The Lupine would call it a sacrilege, and they fight Banes a few miles south of it every night. The mound remembers the people who lived here before the city, and perhaps it remembers Usla.

c-anchor-n.name: Anchor North · the relay mast above Lincoln Creek
c-anchor-n.sub: A disused radio mast on the north side
c-anchor-n.html: Someone has hung a new copper-wound antenna at the top.
c-anchor-n.alias: A relay mast above Lincoln Creek
c-anchor-n.brief: An abandoned radio relay mast over the Lincoln Creek parkway on the north side.

notes.title: Anchor North
notes.html: One of the four anchors of the Chapel's ritual. The creek has refused to die, buried in culverts and resurfacing again and again, and the anchor borrows that stubbornness to keep the ring from collapsing.

c-ritual-core.name: The ritual’s target: expose the null zone
c-ritual-core.html: When all four anchors are tuned, the Chapel's ritual should "turn the null zone inside out" and show what keeps it dead. The Tremere think they will find a source.
c-ritual-core.brief: The point over the Marquette campus where the diagonals of four distant antennae cross: St. Joan of Arc Chapel.

notes.title: Two totems
notes.html: The Tremere do not know that halves of two Lupine totems lie under the chapel. The ritual will wake the Coyote and the Eagle at the same moment.

d-hearth.name: The Last Hearth
d-hearth.sub: Working freehold · a long brick bakehouse
d-hearth.html: Its balefire lives in a shallow coal pan inside the stove, and its strength depends on freely shared practical work: teaching, repair, cooking, cleaning. Paying Marta to do everything does not sustain it. A guest who takes a real share of the work can ask for one honest hearing before being refused shelter. It supports a small circle, not all seventeen of the city's Kithain, and ordinary food still has to be bought.

notes.title: The custom
notes.html: Never draw cold iron inside an offered refuge.

notes.title: The kettle
notes.html: The landlord is due on the night a chimerical kettle is shouting the name of someone who needs help. Marta needs three people; everyone assumes she can do all three things herself.

d-hearth.alias: The back kitchen of an alterations shop
d-hearth.brief: The Last Hearth: a long brick bakehouse with a copper stove, a communal table and cupboards labelled in handwriting accumulated over generations. A modest working freehold.

d-counter.name: The Counterweight
d-counter.sub: Working freehold · a gatehouse hung on chains
d-counter.html: Three pallets, an ironless tool cupboard and a shelf of thermoses. It welcomes travellers for a night; it cannot become a dormitory without changing what sustains it. Oren's door is valuable because it gives a dependable return from two otherwise unreliable routes.

notes.title: Broken promises
notes.html: The damaged weight contains broken promises. They can be removed only after the current obligations they match are honestly settled or renegotiated.

notes.title: A token
notes.html: A stranded chimera has presented a valid old admission token. Admitting it is possible; protecting it from what pursues it will make tomorrow's crossing uncertain.

d-counter.alias: A room beside the bridge machinery
d-counter.brief: The Counterweight: a stone gatehouse hung by chains over a channel full of discarded destinations. Its balefire hangs in a bronze cage on the great weight that raises the dream-bridge, and sinks close to the dark water whenever the bridge opens.

d-keep.name: The Gloaming Keep · outer court
d-keep.html: The public story is that she found an unclaimed ruin and made it habitable. The Keep keeps a deeper reserve of Glamour than either public refuge, almost all of it committed to the private wards, and an edible chimerical garden.
d-keep.alias: A door at the end of the warrens
d-keep.brief: The Gloaming Keep: Ivory's secluded holding, made from the broken architecture of the Copper Hart joined to the old sluagh chambers. Its approach lies inside the Nosferatu warrens; the final threshold is hers.

d-wards.name: The private wards
d-wards.html: The patients' care involves observation, safe periods of ordinary routine, personal anchors and carefully chosen contact. None of the city's treasures replaces that work.
d-wards.brief: The private wards of the Gloaming Keep.

notes.title: Eight survivors
notes.html: Eight changelings presumed dead in 1981 live here in Bedlam. Their refuge drifted out of step with earthly time: they lived months of disordered confinement across five mortal years before Ivory found them.

d-index.name: The Unfinished Index
d-index.html: To enter, return an unfinished work of your own to a shelf where it belongs in the dreaming reflection of the basement stacks, and state the question that stopped you; a ladder descends from above. To travel upward, ask a harder question rather than climbing harder. It holds interrupted investigations, unpublished local writing, rejected municipal schemes and forgotten annotations. It is not omniscient. A reader must honestly advance one abandoned task before borrowing another.

notes.title: Useful discoveries
notes.html: Somewhere in the stacks are the original words of Oren's oath, a repair diagram that could make Leon's tram work without the Glass, and Alisande's unfinished speech proposing reforms to her own court.

d-index.alias: A shelf in the library’s second basement
d-index.brief: The Unfinished Index: bookshelves drifting through a great vaulted gulf beneath the Central Library, desks hanging at different angles, lamps on chains attached to nothing. Half-written letters nest under the desks like swallows.

d-stacks.name: The inner stacks
d-stacks.html: Following a shelf because it holds the answer you want, rather than the work you borrowed, separates companions into different lines of inquiry. Agree on a meeting question before splitting up.
d-stacks.brief: The inner stacks of the Unfinished Index: unstable, shifting shelving drawn toward related questions.

d-ward.name: The Crownless Ward
d-ward.sub: Overgrown towers, blue-lit windows, perpetual late afternoon
d-ward.html: Each blue window holds a place someone might still make: a workshop, a schoolroom, a rehearsal hall, a home. A window goes dark when its room is stripped for parts or declared worthless, and brightens when people start something equivalent in the mortal city. Three buildings are worth saving: the Hall of Borrowed Voices, the West Foundry and the House with Enough Bedrooms. None is a freehold yet. Saving every tower is beyond nine people.

notes.title: The live problem
notes.html: The Surveyor of Necessary Losses offers to make one building safe in exchange for the permanent destruction of three others. Saving every tower is beyond nine people.

d-ward.brief: The Crownless Ward: great towers in perpetual late afternoon, vines over carved walls, birds wheeling between them and blue light in windows above streets that remember feet better than names. A composite realm made of demolished buildings and ambitions whose inhabitants never arrived.

d-ruins.name: The distant ruins
d-ruins.sub: Where the Ward forgets its address
d-ruins.html: Old stairs still lead to floors that no longer exist. The Waiting Platform is out here.
d-ruins.brief: The distant ruins, where the Crownless Ward forgets its address.

d-seat.name: The Far Guest’s Seat
d-seat.sub: A black mountain on the starlit lake
d-seat.html: A great dragon lived here long before the current fae's records; it came from elsewhere and eventually left the Earth. Its lair was a place of audience as well as a hoard, and it still rewards ventures freely undertaken and resists commands imposed on someone else's journey. The dragon's absence is real: there is no dragon under the floor. Most of the gold and the great weapons left with it.

notes.title: The petitions
notes.html: The mountain has begun accepting petitions in the dragon's name. It cannot grant them, and each one adds a step to the Listening Stair.

d-seat.brief: The Far Guest's Seat: a black mountain rising like a blade out of Lake Michigan, under constellations that look like departure routes. There is no such island on the mortal lake.

d-arrivals.name: Hall of Arrivals
d-arrivals.html: What remains of the hoard is here: an empty bell frame, small navigation tools, containers of unfamiliar seeds and gifts whose meanings have been lost.
d-arrivals.brief: The Hall of Arrivals: stone niches sized for gifts, some of them offered by beings much larger than people.

d-stair.name: The Listening Stair
d-stair.sub: Repeats your purpose back to you
d-stair.brief: The Listening Stair repeats a visitor's declared purpose until they can tell it apart from someone else's expectation.

d-winter.name: The Winter Orchard
d-winter.html: The last fruit ripens only for someone who has found a hunger they cannot name.
d-winter.brief: The Winter Orchard grows pale fruit in warm snow.

d-departure.name: The Departure Room
d-departure.html: The road is severed and cannot be followed.
d-departure.brief: The Departure Room overlooks the road the dragon used to leave.

d-orchard.name: The Glass Orchard
d-orchard.sub: Seasonal glade · three vast glass fruits
d-orchard.html: A guide must respect each environment's rhythm; forcing every plant to bloom at once produces brilliant colour and then an exhausted silence. Arthur Saye and a flock of glasshouse swifts look after it. Bjorn comes for the flavours; Nina brings exhausted collaborators who need to want something again.

notes.title: Mountain seeds
notes.html: Seeds carried from the Far Guest's mountain are germinating among ordinary ambitions. People sketch houses that could only stand underwater, or rehearse music that needs a voice they do not have.

d-orchard.brief: The Glass Orchard: three vast glass fruits enclosing a rain forest, a desert and a garden where the seasons turn around a single path. A seasonal glade anchored in the Mitchell Park Domes, sustained by human curiosity.

d-third.name: The Third Shift
d-third.sub: Workshop realm · the factory after the foreman leaves
d-third.html: Its productive hours are limited. If nobody rests, the benches lengthen, the exit moves away and a whole night disappears into "one more adjustment". A brewery worker once dreamed a copper whale into it.

notes.title: COMPLETION
notes.html: Leon's line has acquired an immaculate timetable that nobody wrote. Its last stop is called COMPLETION, and Ruth says no working transport system has such a destination.

d-third.brief: The Third Shift: a factory after the foreman has left, when every worker can try the improvement management would never approve. Lathes sing counterpoint, chalk equations move between benches and small brass creatures carry scraps to projects that might need them.

d-ovation.name: The Standing Ovation
d-ovation.html: The stage grants the pleasure of being heard. Repeating a familiar success makes the exit curtains heavier; new, awkward work opens them. Nobody in the seats can tell you anything reliable about the real people whose faces they wear.
d-ovation.brief: The Standing Ovation: a shallow wooden stage facing seats filled by audiences who nearly came. Some are absent parents, some future admirers, some borrowed from the performer's assumptions.

notes.title: The Encore
notes.html: The Encore wants Nina's neighbourhood performance to happen here for ever.

d-wolfeye.name: The Country of the Wolf’s Eye
d-wolfeye.sub: Border distortion over the Marquette zone
d-wolfeye.html: Ruth travels around it. Leon thinks the interference could teach him something about the tram; Oren thinks his proposed test is not nearly far enough away. A changeling who enters may see a warning in familiar imagery, which is an interpretation at the border and not proof of anything.

notes.title: A lost notebook
notes.html: One of Hester Ames's research notebooks has been lost at the edge of the zone.

d-wolfeye.brief: The Country of the Wolf's Eye: over the Marquette null zone the Dreaming is not empty but overfull. Shadows choose different directions, carved animals seem alert and a small cantrip can gain an unintended audience.

d-borrowed.name: Hall of Borrowed Voices
d-borrowed.brief: The Hall of Borrowed Voices, a chamber of the Crownless Ward that Celia wants to relight as a public rehearsal and meeting hall.

d-foundry.name: The West Foundry
d-foundry.html: Miss Tuesday has found the component Leon is missing here.
d-foundry.brief: The West Foundry in the Crownless Ward, where Leon can recover dream-machinery.

d-bedrooms.name: The House with Enough Bedrooms
d-bedrooms.brief: The House with Enough Bedrooms: a many-storeyed house in the Crownless Ward whose occupants must share decisions about hospitality.

d-blueroom.name: Kit’s blue-lit room
d-blueroom.brief: A blue-lit room in the Crownless Ward, claimed on a ticket Kit carries.

notes.title: Custodian
notes.html: The ticket names Kit custodian, not owner.

d-platform.name: The Waiting Platform
d-platform.sub: Echo of the demolished Everett Street depot
d-platform.html: Reaching it needs an actual invitation from a named destination outside Milwaukee. Ruth wants to secure a real host at the other end and test a short outward stretch.
d-platform.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, pp. 9, 23; improv placement
d-platform.brief: The Waiting Platform: an abandoned intercity dream-station, the echo of the demolished Everett Street depot. The timetable shows emotionally persuasive departures that cannot carry a living traveller home.

d-lanternthreshold.name: The Lantern Wake landing
d-lanternthreshold.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, p. 22; improv placement
d-lanternthreshold.alias: A sheltered spot on the lakefront
d-lanternthreshold.brief: The Lantern Wake landing: a sheltered lakefront threshold where crossings to the Far Guest's Seat begin.

d-pabstecho.name: The Copper Hart’s stair-foot
d-pabstecho.html: The Hall of the Copper Hart stood above the old city here, with an antlered weathercock of a stag climbing above the smoke. The building was demolished in 1981, in the same spring as the war's last night.
d-pabstecho.alias: The foot of a stair downtown
d-pabstecho.brief: The dream-reflection of the old Pabst site, where the Unbuilt Stair begins.

d-eastecho.name: Eastern downtown echoes
d-eastecho.sub: Far bank of the White Flag Crossing
d-eastecho.brief: Eastern downtown echoes: the far bank of the White Flag Crossing.

c-quire.name: Mrs. Quire
c-quire.brief: Mrs. Quire at her desk in the Unfinished Index.

c-rent.name: The Rent Collector
c-rent.brief: The Rent Collector on its rounds of the Crownless Ward.

c-surveyor.name: The Surveyor of Necessary Losses
c-surveyor.brief: The Surveyor of Necessary Losses, measuring something in the Ward.

c-tollman.name: The Tollman of Two Banks
c-tollman.brief: The Tollman of Two Banks, under the White Flag Crossing.

c-usher.name: The Ashen Usher
c-usher.brief: The Ashen Usher in the Hall of Arrivals.

c-tuesday.name: Miss Tuesday
