c-tuesday.brief: Miss Tuesday, the brass hound, who wanders wherever a tool is missed.

c-encore.name: The Encore
c-encore.brief: The Encore, on the stage of the Standing Ovation.

c-swifts.name: Glasshouse swifts
c-swifts.brief: A flock of glasshouse swifts that helps keep the Glass Orchard.

c-whale.name: The copper whale
c-whale.brief: A small copper whale dreamed into the Third Shift by a brewery worker. It feeds on steam and is furious when called a fish.

c-knock.name: The Knock-under-the-Bridge
c-knock.html: She enchants her trainees so they can meet it on controlled ground, with escape routes and an abort signal she enforces. The danger is a hunter assuming that an unrelated encounter follows the same rules.
c-knock.brief: The Knock-under-the-Bridge, one of Ivory's training chimera.

c-coat.name: The Coat on the Last Bus
c-coat.sub: Ivory’s training chimera · rides the route
c-coat.alias: A coat on the last bus
c-coat.brief: The Coat on the Last Bus, one of Ivory's training chimera. It rides the route.

c-lantern.name: The Lantern in the Drain
c-lantern.brief: The Lantern in the Drain, one of Ivory's training chimera.

c-staircase.name: A staircase of people
c-staircase.sub: County Stadium on a good night
c-staircase.html: It has nothing to do with who owns the boxes.
c-staircase.brief: On a good night at County Stadium the crowd briefly makes a chimerical staircase of people giving a stranger a better view.

w-ribbon.name: June’s mended ribbon
w-ribbon.sub: Found outside the Keep’s outer approach
w-ribbon.html: Marta recognises it: she made it for June before the war.
w-ribbon.brief: A mended ribbon, found outside the outer approach of the Keep.

notes.title: How it got out
notes.html: It was carried out with discarded fabric. It proves an old object survived; it does not reveal eight living people.

t-bell.name: The Bell of the Last Transfer
t-bell.html: Properly repaired, it could call a stranded passenger with a valid punched ticket back to the last legitimate stop on its one restored route. It cannot recover the dead or overrule a closed freehold.
t-bell.brief: The Bell of the Last Transfer: a brass tram bell on Leon's test vehicle.

notes.title: Before repair
notes.html: Wired to the Glass shard, it recognises wartime stops, and is a hazard rather than a rescue.

t-glass.name: A shard of the Glass of the Second Door
t-glass.html: The Glass could alter a limited set of prepared thresholds so that a convincing false escape replaced a real destination. One shard is in Leon's prototype; the other pieces are unaccounted for. Destroying it does not harm Ivory's patients or any freehold.
t-glass.brief: A shard of the Glass of the Second Door, broken in 1981.

t-key.name: The Key of a Borrowed Room
t-key.html: The guest must leave a practical improvement: a repaired latch, swept stairs, an honest inventory. Using it again without improvement brings the Rent Collector.
t-key.brief: The Key of a Borrowed Room: a small tarnished key on Kit's claim ticket. It opens one unoccupied, unclaimed room in the Crownless Ward for a night of shelter.

t-thimble.name: Marta’s Mending Thimble
t-thimble.html: A garment mended patiently for a particular willing person can carry one vivid comforting memory into an enchanted experience. It does not compel calm or cure Bedlam. Marta lends it to competent learners and refuses commissions made without the wearer's knowledge.
t-thimble.brief: Marta's Mending Thimble, copper, polished almost smooth.

t-pennant.name: The White Pennant
t-pennant.html: It guarantees that the Tollman will hear the bearer out before refusing the White Flag Crossing, if they declare their peaceful purpose honestly. A hearing, not agreement. Using it to set up ambushes destroys it.
t-pennant.brief: The White Pennant, an old strip of sailcloth kept by Oren.

t-lamp.name: The Scale-Light Lantern
t-lamp.html: It reveals the Lantern Wake and a small circle of reliable water around the boat, if the pilot follows the agreed chart. It is charged by completing a journey freely promised to someone else. One charge, one passage.
t-lamp.alias: A lamp with a scale shutter
t-lamp.brief: The Scale-Light Lantern: a lamp with a translucent dragon-scale shutter, carried by Bjorn.

notes.title: A loan
notes.html: The Ashen Usher recognises it as a loan from an older visitor, and wants the terms renewed.

t-fruit.name: The Fruit That Has No Name
t-fruit.html: Shared willingly by two people, it lets each convey one sensation the other has never known. The mountain grows no second fruit until both act on what they learned.
t-fruit.brief: The Fruit That Has No Name: a single pale fruit in the Winter Orchard, visible only when ripe.

s-citadel.name: The Exposition Hall
s-citadel.sub: Citadel of the Hierarchy · relic of the 1881 Exposition Building
s-citadel.html: In the Shadowlands the old hall still stands, all iron trusses and dusty bunting, and it is Milwaukee’s Citadel. Anacreon Konrad Vollmer keeps his court on the balcony where the 1881 opening speeches were made. Below him, in the living world, the Kindred Council whispers through Symphony nights. The Hierarchy has been listening for decades.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: The Reapers want Merik’s victims brought here before the Renegades of Bay View or the free wraiths of Walnut Street reach them. The Anacreon wants it done quietly, because the Chicago Necropolis has started asking why Milwaukee’s harvests run so thin.

s-citadel.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.
s-citadel.brief: The great Industrial Exposition Building burned in 1905, and the Auditorium was raised on its ashes.

s-pabst.name: The Pabst Building
s-pabst.html: Hierarchy Monitors keep a lamp in the cupola to watch for Maelstrom weather over the lake. Nobody goes above the fourteenth floor. Doors there open onto stairwells that loop back on themselves, and the wraiths call it the False Floor.

notes.title: Storyteller
notes.html: The False Floor is what remains, on the death side, of the fae War of False Doors in 1981. The Glass of the Second Door scarred the relic as surely as it scarred the Dreaming. A sluagh might recognise the pattern. A Monitor never will.

s-pabst.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.
s-pabst.brief: Demolished ten years ago, the tower stands again on this side of the Shroud, ash-grey and whole, taller than anything around it.

s-plankinton.name: Plankinton House
s-plankinton.html: Mr. Penny keeps the ledgers at the old front desk and charges a toll in memories for anything he cannot price in coin.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: A bundle of relic letters from the Third Ward fire of 1892 has come up for auction. Three separate wraiths claim the same grandmother wrote them.

s-plankinton.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.
s-plankinton.brief: The grand hotel came down in 1980 to make room for the new Grand Avenue mall. Its relic lobby is the city’s market for soul-coin, favours and Stygian goods.

s-newhall.name: The Newhall House ruin
s-newhall.html: The relic is a blackened shell that is always smouldering. Most of the dead moved on or were Reaped long ago. Something else has kept the fire going.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: Every January the ruin flares. This year the smoke is drifting toward Old St. Mary’s, and the Inquisition cell in the basement has begun to dream of burning rooms.

s-newhall.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.
s-newhall.brief: In January 1883 the Newhall House burned in the night and more than seventy people died. Many were servant girls trapped on the upper floors.

s-depot.name: The Everett Street depot
s-depot.html: Harbingers ride it with sealed dispatches. In the Dreaming, the fae know the same spot as the Waiting Platform, and neither side has noticed the other yet.
s-depot.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.
s-depot.brief: The Milwaukee Road’s great depot was torn down in 1965. Its relic platforms serve the Hearse Train, the Hierarchy’s overland line to the Chicago Necropolis.

s-bronzeville.name: Walnut Street
s-bronzeville.sub: Relic Bronzeville · the free wraiths’ quarter
s-bronzeville.html: In the Shadowlands it is all still there: the barbershops, the churches, the clubs where the music ran till dawn. Its dead and its memories hold it together. Lorraine Hollis keeps the peace. The Hierarchy has no garrison here and has learned not to send one.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: Lorraine is sheltering a newly dead woman the Reapers want. The woman hasn’t told anyone how she died, and her Shadow keeps answering for her.

s-bronzeville.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.
s-bronzeville.brief: Milwaukee’s Black business and entertainment district along Walnut Street was cut apart by urban renewal and the North-South Freeway in the 1950s and ’60s.

s-soldiers.name: The Soldiers Home
s-soldiers.sub: Grim Legion garrison · Wood National Cemetery
s-soldiers.html: Sergeant Reinholt drills them at dusk on a parade ground that the living know as lawn.
s-soldiers.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.
s-soldiers.brief: Veterans of four wars lie in the national cemetery around the old Soldiers Home. The Grim Legion, for those who died by violence, keeps its Milwaukee garrison in the relic barracks.

s-forest.name: Forest Home chapel
s-forest.sub: The Pardoner’s seat · end of the Funeral Road
s-forest.html: Father Anselm hears confessions here and pares Shadows back with Castigation.
s-forest.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.
s-forest.brief: The Victorian cemetery where Milwaukee’s brewers and mayors are buried. Its chapel is the Hierarchy’s registry of the dead, where every Reaped soul is entered in a book that is never quite finished.

s-county.name: The County Grounds
s-county.html: Every coffin raised breaks a Fetter. The Penitent Legion, keeper of those who died in madness and despair, is losing wraiths it has guarded for ninety years.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: Matron Grau wants the excavation slowed. The living crew wants to finish by winter. A wraith who can make one archaeologist feel watched could buy her a week. The Anacreon has forbidden it.

s-county.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.
s-county.brief: For a century the county’s poor, insane and unclaimed were buried here in unmarked rows. In 1991 construction near the medical complex turned up the first graves, and archaeologists are now lifting them one by one.

s-baymill.name: The Rolling Mill
s-baymill.html: The relic mill is a cold furnace hall where the Strikers’ Circle meets. They are Renegades who see the Hierarchy as one more set of owners. Joe Mazur leads them.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: The Circle wants Merik’s newly dead before the Reapers get them. Joe says it is to free them. The Anacreon says it is to recruit them. Both are partly right.

s-baymill.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.
s-baymill.brief: On 5 May 1886, striking workers marching for the eight-hour day were fired on by the state militia outside the Bay View rolling mills, and seven people died.

s-elgin.name: The Lady Elgin landing
s-elgin.html: Many were Third Ward Irish of Milwaukee’s Union Guard. Her relic still sails. The Emerald Legion, keeper of the accidentally dead, runs her as the ferry across the Sea of Shadows toward Chicago. She docks here at the harbor mouth on foggy nights.
s-elgin.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.
s-elgin.brief: On 8 September 1860 the excursion steamer Lady Elgin sank off the Illinois shore with roughly three hundred people aboard.

s-police.name: The Broadway station
s-police.html: Their relic station house still answers calls. The Ninth Watch, a squad sworn to the Grim Legion, walks a beat no living patrolman can see, and they are very interested in whoever has been draining people in Juneau Park.
s-police.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.
s-police.brief: In November 1917 a bomb carried into the old Central Police Station exploded and killed nine officers and a civilian.

s-joan.name: The Pyre Circle
s-joan.sub: Heretics · St. Joan of Arc Chapel
s-joan.html: Sister Clotilde’s heretics believe it, and they believe Joan crossed over and passed beyond, into Transcendence. They gather around the stone to pray their way after her. Over the Marquette anomaly the Shroud behaves strangely, sometimes thick as felt and sometimes gone. Some nights their prayers seem to be answered.

notes.title: Storyteller
notes.html: What answers is not Joan. It is the overabundance of magic around Usla’s buried totems, leaking through. The Circle’s “visions” are a Lupine relic dreaming.

s-joan.brief: Legend says one stone in the chapel is cold because Joan of Arc kissed it before she died.

s-forge.name: The Tannery Forge
s-forge.html: The smoke from the forge never quite leaves the valley.

notes.title: Storyteller
notes.html: Hilde has quietly asked the Reapers to send her any wraith “too damaged to keep”. She has been told Merik’s victims may fit that description.

s-forge.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.
s-forge.brief: The valley’s old tanneries and packing houses left deep relics full of vats and hooks. Hilde Brauer’s Artificers forge Stygian steel, chains and soul-coin here for the Citadel.

s-masquers.name: The Pabst Theater
s-masquers.html: Colette Duval’s Masquers rehearse there between living performances, learning the faces they will wear on errands for the Citadel.
s-masquers.brief: The theatre is no relic, since it still stands in the living world, but the Shroud is thin in its gallery.

s-bench.name: The bench in Juneau Park
s-bench.html: They do not understand why the police tape is gone, or why the lake has turned grey.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: The Reapers, the Strikers’ Circle and Lorraine Hollis all want to reach them first, for different reasons. One of the couple is already listening to a voice that sounds exactly like her own.

s-bench.brief: Merik’s frenzy began here: a couple kissing on a park bench on the way home from a movie. They woke on this side still holding hands, bound to the bench and to each other.

s-four.name: The four from the headline
s-four.sub: Fetters scattered across the Lower East Side
s-four.html: Each is Fettered to something different: a stairwell, a newspaper box, a borrowed coat, a voice on the WBIT late show. Two have already been Reaped. Two are hiding.
s-four.brief: “Vampire Murderer Kills Four.” Their bodies were left where they would be found. Their wraiths are less tidy.

s-ashes.name: The burned house on the hill
s-ashes.html: They prowl the relic of the house, which burns more completely on this side, and wait for the Prince to come home. He won’t. Destroyed Kindred leave no wraith, and nothing that was Merik has crossed.
s-ashes.brief: Several of Merik’s ghouls died in the fire. Three woke in the Shadowlands still craving vitae that no longer exists for them.

s-hollow.name: The Interchange Hollow
s-hollow.html: The Anarch rumbles fought here every month feed it a little. Wraiths cross the bridges above it quickly and do not look down.
s-hollow.brief: The freeway interchange erased blocks of homes. In the Shadowlands the concrete courtyards between the ramps are open wounds: a Nihil spirals down past the Shroud into the Tempest.

s-drain.name: What Milo met
s-drain.html: Nobody believes him. He is right. A Spectre nests in the outfall: a Doppelganger whose Shadow devoured it decades ago, now fat on despair and drawn to the cold, borrowed lives of vampires. Ivory’s training chimera, the Lantern in the Drain, works just upstream. She has noticed the water tastes wrong.
s-drain.brief: Milo the Malkavian swears something in the drain pipes by the lake woke up, chased him, and promised to eat every Kindred in the city, one by one.

s-tempest.name: The Sea of Shadows
s-tempest.html: The Lady Elgin crosses it. The Ice Road runs over it in winter. Everything else that sails it is hunting.
s-tempest.brief: Past the breakwaters the Shroud gives way to the Sea of Shadows, the lake’s death-side twin, rolling grey and endless under Maelstrom weather.

u-spire.name: The Spire of 100 East
u-spire.sub: Pattern-Spider nest over the lost Pabst
u-spire.html: Underneath lies the empty footprint of the old Pabst Building, the one place downtown the spiders won’t spin. The fae and the dead both have reasons for that. The spiders don’t.
u-spire.brief: The new glass tower is, in the Umbra, a single enormous crystal still being grown. Eight-Count, overseer of the downtown Pattern Spiders, nests at the top.

u-tallest.name: The Tallest Thing
u-tallest.sub: Spirit of the city’s tallest tower
u-tallest.html: It sees the whole Penumbra from its roof and will tell you what it sees for a compliment it has not heard before.
u-tallest.brief: The great bank tower on East Wisconsin Avenue has the spirit of a proud civil servant. It is the tallest thing in the state and it knows it.

u-clockwork.name: The Clockwork Heart
u-clockwork.html: Since Merik died, the clerks have noticed someone is missing from the mayor’s strings, and they are deeply uneasy about who will pick them up.
u-clockwork.brief: City Hall’s Umbral reflection is a ticking brass heart where Ledgerlings file the city’s permits and Weaver-clerks argue precedent.

u-inkwell.name: The Inkwell
u-inkwell.html: It trades rumours with spirits all over the city and printed the “Vampire Murderer” headline in the Umbra a full night before the mortal paper did.
u-inkwell.brief: A spirit of news: ink-black, many-handed and always on deadline. It is mostly Weaver but has a Wyld streak for a good story.

u-static.name: Static
u-static.html: It sent squad cars after the Mask during Psychomachia for the fun of it. Decker’s friendly patrolmen have noticed their radios go bad whenever Lupines are near.
u-static.brief: A crackling Bane that lives in the dispatch frequencies, feeding on panic and wrong addresses.

u-coldrooms.name: The Cold Rooms
u-coldrooms.sub: MECCA and the Hyatt, where the Elders sleep
u-coldrooms.html: Garou can read the Kindred’s whole downtown in this taint like a map. The Pattern Spiders spin around it and never through it.
u-coldrooms.brief: In the Umbra, vampires leave a stain. The rooms where the Elders sleep and meet show as voids: cold, grey and lightly Wyrm-tainted, where spirits refuse to go.

u-skyweb.name: The Skywalk Web
u-skyweb.brief: The skywalk is a great woven tube of Weaver silk in the Umbra, used by Weaver-messengers. A spirit can travel from the Hyatt to the Federal Plaza without touching the Penumbra floor.

u-wound.name: The Wound of Two Totems
u-wound.sub: Under St. Joan of Arc Chapel
u-wound.html: Spirits who come too close start to argue with themselves. Whoever lifts the relics will have the Wounded Eagle and Coyote’s Grin standing on either side of them, both demanding their piece back.

notes.title: Storyteller
notes.html: Neither totem can take back its part alone, because Usla bound the two relics together when he shaped them into one body. Returning them takes Coyote and Eagle acting together, the one thing the two clans have not done in three hundred years.

u-wound.brief: The buried hand and eye of Usla, once the Talon of the Eagle and the Eye of the Coyote, burn in the Penumbra like two coals in a split hearth.

u-stormcrows.name: The Storm-Crows
u-stormcrows.html: They always deliver it twice, once to each side.
u-stormcrows.brief: Small black spirits born from the storm itself. They fly in double flocks, one cawing for the Eagle and one for the Coyote, and will carry a message anywhere in the city for a mouthful of Gnosis.

u-eyewatch.name: The Eye in the Cloud
u-eyewatch.html: Anyone it fixes on hears a joke in their own voice about something they have kept secret.
u-eyewatch.brief: A vast amber eye opens in the clouds over the campus on overcast nights. It is the Coyote’s missing sight, looking for itself.

u-talonrake.name: The Raking Talon
u-talonrake.sub: The Eagle’s missing claw, in the storm
u-talonrake.html: Spirits that fly too high here come down in pieces.
u-talonrake.brief: On the south side of the storm, red light tears the sky in four parallel lines. It is the Talon clawing for its owner.

u-mortiuswards.name: Mortius’s wards
u-mortiuswards.html: Since Victor died and nobody from Vienna watches the Chapel, there are three times as many threads and the glyphs are darker. The Storm-Crows have learned to pull them, and soon one of them will pull the wrong one.
u-mortiuswards.brief: Dr. Mortius cannot reach the Umbra, but his Thaumaturgy leaves glyph-threads at the zone’s north edge to record what passes.

u-gambrinus.name: The Hall of Gambrinus
u-gambrinus.html: He will trade almost anything for a reason to believe he will last.
u-gambrinus.brief: A smoky banqueting hall of carved oak and copper with the old king on his barrel-throne. Gambrinus is generous, sentimental and frightened: his brewery is losing money and he can feel it in his joints.

u-copperqueen.name: The Copper Queen’s Court
u-copperqueen.sub: Spirit-queen of the State Street brewery
u-copperqueen.html: Garou of all three clans have been seen here on the same night, at different tables.
u-copperqueen.brief: The busiest neutral ground in the city’s Umbra, a bright, roaring beer hall. Spirits of every allegiance drink side by side because nobody dares break the Queen’s peace.

u-widow.name: The Widow of the Vats
u-widow.brief: A tall, faded spirit in a copper-buttoned apron, polishing empty kettles. She knows every old recipe in Milwaukee and will give one away to anyone who promises to brew it somewhere.

u-upstart.name: The Upstart
u-upstart.sub: Spirit of the little Walker’s Point brewery
u-upstart.html: The Blood Brothers party in its hall, and it likes them. Gambrinus finds it charming. The Copper Queen hasn’t noticed it yet.
u-upstart.brief: A young, cocky craft-brewery spirit, barely five years old, that thinks it can take on the giants.

u-ironhorse.name: The Iron Horse
u-ironhorse.html: It loved the wolf who rode with them. Akawa is gone now, and every night the Horse tears up and down the city’s avenues looking for him.
u-ironhorse.brief: A thunder-voiced stallion of chrome and engine, its mane a plume of exhaust. It loves speed, loud men and open roads, and was proud that its children carried the Blood Brothers.

u-chromepack.name: The Chrome Pack
u-chromepack.html: Anyone who comes off can expect to be laughed at for a month.
u-chromepack.brief: A howling pack of motorcycle-spirits that run the Penumbra’s avenues at night. Garou Ragabash ride them for fun.

u-tallow.name: Tallow
u-tallow.html: It is old, patient and very hard to kill, because the valley keeps feeding it.
u-tallow.brief: A slow, enormous Bane of fat and steam that seeps through the valley, reducing everything it touches into simpler, hungrier things.

u-tannin.name: The Tannin Pits
u-tannin.sub: Where hides were cured, and worse
u-tannin.brief: Bubbling pits of black-brown liquor where the Tannin Twins, two Banes joined at the hip, cure anything thrown in until it can never rot or grow again.

u-herd.name: The Stockyard Herd
u-herd.html: Lupus-born Garou can’t stand to hear them. Lately something has been driving them out of the valley at dusk.
u-herd.brief: Terrified herd-spirits, the memory of a century of animals driven to slaughter, stampeding through the smoke.

u-sabbatpact.name: Parovich’s legacy
u-sabbatpact.sub: The Sabbat’s remnants keep feeding the Wyrm
u-sabbatpact.html: He fed blood to Gnaw, a rage-Bane, and Gnaw rode the Eagle’s raiders and made their raids wilder. Parovich was exposed and destroyed, but the bargain outlived him. The scattered remnants of Guillem Velez’s Sabbat found his old offerings and keep feeding Gnaw, no longer so that the Lupines break the city, but so that the Garou are too busy to look for Velez.
u-sabbatpact.brief: Parovich learned what the rest of the Kindred never knew: the Banes of the Rendering will bargain.

u-compost.name: Grandmother Compost
u-compost.html: She has outlived three Garou septs and expects to outlive these.
u-compost.brief: An immense, unhurried spirit of rot and renewal, wrapped in steam and earthworms. She takes in the city’s filth and gives back green, and she is the only spirit the Wyrm, the Weaver and the Wyld all treat with respect.

u-foggate.name: The Fog Gate
u-foggate.sub: Where the lake fog comes ashore
u-foggate.html: Fog-spirits carry messages from Greatwater to anyone they find awake on the shore.
u-foggate.brief: At the harbor mouth the great lake fogs, the Grey Coming, enter the city’s Umbra like a slow army.

u-kkspirit.name: Kinnickinnic, in chains
u-kkspirit.html: It cannot rise and it cannot rest. It begs every passing Garou to break one band, just one. Each broken band floods a few blocks of the South Side’s Penumbra.
u-kkspirit.brief: A river spirit of muddy water and willow roots, bound in grey concrete bands from bank to bank.

u-warden.name: The Concrete Warden
u-warden.html: It believes absolutely that it saves lives, and it may be right.
u-warden.brief: A square, tireless Weaver spirit that patrols the channel and pours new concrete over every crack.

u-kkmouth.name: Where the chains begin
u-kkmouth.html: Spirits come here to watch it breathe.
u-kkmouth.brief: At the mouth of the channel the bands end and the river spills free into the harbor in a burst of green light.

u-polishmoon.name: The Polish Moon
u-polishmoon.sub: The four-faced clock and its Lune court
u-polishmoon.html: The Moonkeeper holds court on the clock face and enforces every oath sworn beneath it. A Garou who wants to swear something that will hold comes here.
u-polishmoon.brief: The great clock tower is, in the Umbra, a second moon that never wanes, ringed by Lunes who dance in silver silks.

u-reassembled.name: The Reassembled
u-reassembled.sub: The basilica built from another city’s stones
u-reassembled.html: Its spirit is a patient patchwork giant who remembers being something else and loves being this. It shelters spirits who have lost their homes.
u-reassembled.brief: The South Side’s great basilica was raised in 1901 from the salvaged stone of a demolished Chicago building.

u-bazaar.name: The Mitchell Street Bazaar
u-bazaar.html: Mouse Garou come here to buy talens. Marta Kaczmarek’s Hearth is just down the street on the Dreaming side, and the Bazaar’s spirits can smell it as warm bread from another world.
u-bazaar.brief: Under the shop signs of the old commercial street, small spirits trade favours, fetishes, gossip and Gnosis by the thimbleful.

u-kosciuszko.name: Kosciuszko’s Watch
u-kosciuszko.sub: The park statue and its sentinel spirit
u-kosciuszko.html: It has a soldier’s courtesy and a soldier’s grudges.
u-kosciuszko.brief: The general’s statue in the park has a spirit that stands guard over the neighbourhood and challenges any Bane that crosses the Ward.

u-treaty.name: The Treaty Green
u-treaty.sub: Where the three clans may meet
u-treaty.html: The Lake Breeze witnesses every word and carries a report of any broken truce to every caern in the city.
u-treaty.brief: A circle of lawn above the ravines where the Lake Park Truce holds. Any Garou may call a moot here; any who come are safe while they stay on the Green.

u-lighthouse.name: North Point Light
u-lighthouse.html: When the bridges are open its beam sweeps; when one is broken the beam stutters, and the Lunes come to see why.
u-lighthouse.brief: The old lighthouse burns in the Umbra with a silver flame that lights every moon bridge in the city.

u-ravinekids.name: The Ravine Children
u-ravinekids.sub: Wyld spirits of the park ravines
u-ravinekids.brief: Small, giggling Wyld spirits of creeks, leaf-litter and rope swings. They obey the paths as a game and break the rule whenever they think nobody is looking.

u-greatwater.name: Greatwater
u-greatwater.html: It has never taken a side in the city’s wars, and every Garou Theurge in Milwaukee has tried at least once to change that.
u-greatwater.brief: Not a person but a presence: a vast, cold, patient intelligence under the waves. It speaks in fog, ice and storm.

u-usla.name: The Drowned Thief
u-usla.html: He can tell the truth of the theft. He wants to be asked.
u-usla.brief: When Usla crawled into the lake to die, Greatwater kept him. His spirit lies in the cold dark offshore, chained by his own shame, a broken Garou of the old days who stole two totems’ strength to save a people who were not his.

u-alewives.name: The Thousand Alewives
u-alewives.sub: A swarm-spirit of the lake’s die-offs
u-alewives.brief: In the 1960s, dead alewives washed up on Milwaukee’s beaches in their millions. Their memory is a shimmering swarm-spirit, silver and mournful, that circles the southern shore and remembers every spill and every poison poured into the lake.

u-avoided.name: The Avoided Water
u-avoided.sub: A place offshore that spirits steer around
u-avoided.html: The Garou don’t know why. The fae would call it the Far Guest’s Seat; on this side there is only the gap.
u-avoided.brief: There is a stretch of open water east of the harbor that every lake-spirit steers around, as though something very large once sat there and might come back.

u-wrecks.name: The Wreck-Choir
u-wrecks.html: Sailors who hear it in the waking world feel suddenly homesick.
u-wrecks.brief: Schooners, steamers and ore boats lie on the lake floor, and their spirits sing to each other in the dark: a slow choir of bells, fog-horns and timbers.

u-icemother.name: Ice-Mother’s Remnant
u-icemother.sub: The glacier that never fully left
u-icemother.html: In hard winters she stirs, and the Ice Road on the death side freezes in sympathy.
u-icemother.brief: Far out in the Deep Umbra of the lake lies a blue-white memory of the ice sheet that carved it: Ice-Mother, mostly asleep.

u-breeze.name: The Lake Breeze
u-breeze.sub: The spirit that cools the shore
u-breeze.html: It witnesses the Lake Park Truce and keeps the shore calm. It does not like the Lupine raiders who use its beaches, but it has never once refused them passage.
u-breeze.brief: A brisk, cheerful, slightly smug air-spirit, known to every Milwaukeean from the weather report: cooler by the lake.

u-bonfire.name: Bradford Beach bonfires
u-bonfire.html: Wake one early and it will burn very bright and very briefly for you.
u-bonfire.brief: Small fire-spirits born from a century of summer beach fires, banked for the autumn and dreaming of July.

u-southbluff.name: Grant Park’s wild bluff
u-southbluff.brief: Steep wooded ravines down to the lake, the last wild shore in the county. In the Umbra the Eagle clan’s raiders come ashore here after swimming north along the coast, and the Lake Breeze cools their Rage just enough to keep them hidden.

u-rendezvous.name: The rendezvous boat
u-rendezvous.sub: Where the Mouse meet the Union
u-rendezvous.html: The Mouse pack’s messenger, Drake, met the Union here during Psychomachia. There is no Mouse pack to deal with any more, but the boat still keeps a lamp lit for him.
u-rendezvous.brief: Turk’s broken riverboat on the Veterans Park shore has a spirit too: a sad old paddle-steamer that remembers excursions.

u-knot.name: The Knot
u-knot.html: The Penumbra shows the faint outlines of the streets and houses that were cleared for it. On the death side of the Shroud, the same place is a Nihil.
u-knot.brief: Where three freeways meet, the Weaver has tied an enormous knot of shining lanes. Pattern Spiders keep it tight, and Gridlock Jagglings graze its ramps at rush hour.

u-bridgenowhere.name: The Bridge to Nowhere
u-bridgenowhere.html: Its spirit still suspects it is unwanted. It is shy, melancholy and enormous, and it will carry anyone who tells it where they are going.
u-bridgenowhere.brief: For years the great lakefront bridge stood finished and unconnected while the city argued over its approaches, and Milwaukee called it the bridge to nowhere.

u-parkeast.name: The Park East Spur
u-parkeast.sub: A freeway that dreams of being torn down
u-parkeast.html: It spends its nights apologising to the neighbourhood beneath it.
u-parkeast.brief: A short, unloved elevated spur north of downtown. Its spirit is convinced it will be demolished one day and has made its peace with that.

u-tolls.name: The Zoo Interchange tollkeepers
u-tolls.html: Garou who refuse are re-routed into the Lawn Sea for a very long night.
u-tolls.brief: At the great western interchange, square Weaver spirits demand a token from every spirit crossing between city and suburb.

u-ninthinning.name: The Ninth Inning
u-ninthinning.html: Gnosis pours off it on a good night, and Theurges of every clan quietly come to drink.
u-ninthinning.brief: Fifty thousand hopes, every summer, for decades: the stadium’s spirit is a roaring, optimistic giant that wakes for home games and sleeps all winter.

u-hush.name: The Hush
u-hush.html: The excavation of the poor-farm graves has stirred it up badly.
u-hush.brief: Murmur, a Bane of despair, drifts through the old asylum wards like a grey mist. It feeds on every shout and every unanswered plea.

u-lantern.name: The Healers’ Lantern
u-lantern.html: It will help any Garou who comes to heal, and no Garou who comes to fight.
u-lantern.brief: A gentle spirit carrying a lamp through the wards: the remembered care of every nurse who sat up with a dying stranger.

u-embassy.name: The Embassy of Beasts
u-embassy.html: They receive Garou as ambassadors and trade news of faraway Umbral lands for news of the lake.
u-embassy.brief: Lion-spirits, bear-spirits, a very old elephant-spirit who chairs the council, and a hundred more, all keeping court behind the zoo walls.

u-greyamb.name: The Grey Ambassador
u-greyamb.html: Lupus-born Garou find it unbearable and come back anyway.
u-greyamb.brief: Wise, sad and patient, the spirit of the captive wolves speaks for every caged pack in the world.

u-spindle.name: The Departure Spindle
u-spindle.brief: A turning tower of light that spins flight paths into the sky. It is the most reliable way out of the city’s Umbra, and the Pattern Spiders keep a manifest of everything that leaves.

u-hive.name: The Southridge Hive
u-hive.html: Its Hive-Queen is half Weaver, half something hungrier, and is quietly expanding her territory into the woods.
u-hive.brief: The big southern mall glows in the Umbra like a honeycomb, full of drone-spirits of want and price-tags.

u-mowers.name: The Mowing Spiders
u-mowers.html: They are harmless unless you are a weed.
u-mowers.brief: Pale, flat, many-legged Weaver spirits that trim back everything Wyld in the suburbs each week.

u-marked.name: The Marked Threshold
u-marked.sub: Hrothulf’s house, as the spirits see it
u-marked.html: Hrothulf, the vampire, once married into the people Usla fought for and against. The Garou ancestors keep that debt, though no living Garou knows what it is.
u-marked.brief: The book says the Lupine avoid Hrothulf’s suburban house. In the Umbra the reason is plain: an old ancestor-mark of Usla’s band burns over the door.

u-coyotecaern.name: Caern of the Grinning Stone
u-coyotecaern.sub: The Coyote clan’s caern · limestone quarries
u-coyotecaern.html: Horatio’s sept of a dozen Red Talon wolves keeps it, and all but two of them have never worn a human face for more than an hour. The totem’s avatar sits on the rim of the quarry laughing. The moon bridge to the Granary broke this autumn, and the caern feels the break like an aching tooth.
u-coyotecaern.brief: A flooded quarry whose cliff-face is cut in the shape of a grin. The caern is small but strong, its Gnosis tasting of dust and lightning.

u-coyotebawn.name: The Bawn of Echoes
u-coyotebawn.brief: Woods and quarry roads that repeat every footstep three times. Intruders hear themselves surrounded long before the Coyote decide to show themselves.

u-oldfalls.name: Old Falls
u-oldfalls.sub: The spirit of the falls at Menomonee Falls
u-oldfalls.brief: A small waterfall that gave a town its name. Its spirit is an old friend of the Coyote and keeps their secrets in its roar.

u-grinavatar.name: Coyote’s Grin
u-grinavatar.html: It is cunning, generous, cruel, and very much wants its eye back.
u-grinavatar.brief: A lean, laughing coyote with one eye blind, the one Usla took. It is the totem’s avatar and the clan’s patron.

u-quarrylake.name: The Quarry Lake That Answers
u-quarrylake.html: The joke is always true; it just takes a while to understand.
u-quarrylake.brief: Throw a stone in and ask a question. The lake answers with a joke.

u-eaglecaern.name: Caern of the Bleeding Pine
u-eaglecaern.sub: The Eagle clan’s caern · Root River woods
u-eaglecaern.html: The caern is fierce, small and failing a little each year, and its eight Wendigo guard it with the bitterness of people who know they are losing. This autumn the blight reached its roots: the ward-stones around the pine are defiled, and the sap at its base has started to run black.
u-eaglecaern.brief: A huge white pine whose sap runs red. It has bled since the night Usla took the Talon.

u-aerie.name: The Talonless Aerie
u-aerie.html: Here too the pack settles business no mortal partner hears about: the Seven Fires casino, held through trusted people, pays for lawyers, land and scholarships, and its board are people Agnes would trust with her life.
u-aerie.brief: A ring of tall trees where the clan holds its councils and sings the Grudge, the long, unending list of wrongs done to the Eagle, starting with Usla and ending, for now, with the Kindred of Milwaukee and the Tremere who poisoned the woods.

u-woundedeagle.name: The Wounded Eagle
u-woundedeagle.html: Its cry carries for miles in the Umbra. It is proud, wounded and furious, and it has never forgiven anyone.
u-woundedeagle.brief: A white eagle the size of a barn, circling high over the southern woods with one foot clenched and empty.

u-boerner.name: The Gardeners’ Truce
u-boerner.html: Even the Eagle don’t fight here; they come to sit.
u-boerner.brief: Inside the big county park, the botanical gardens’ cultivated flower-spirits live in a strict, fragrant peace with the wild woods around them.

u-gnaw.name: Gnaw
u-gnaw.sub: The Bane that rides the Eagle’s rage
u-gnaw.html: It has grown fat this year on blood that isn’t Garou blood. Parovich is gone, but the feeding trough isn’t empty: the leftovers of Velez’s Sabbat bring the blood now, and in the blighted woods Gnaw finds food of its own. Brother Sparrow can hear it and thinks it is the Eagle speaking.
u-gnaw.brief: A thin, grinning rage-Bane that clings to the clan’s raiders like a tick and whispers to their Rage.

u-dotfarm.name: Brennan’s farm
u-dotfarm.html: Dot Brennan feeds the clan, hides its wounded and is the only person who can make Agnes Hightree laugh.
u-dotfarm.brief: A failing dairy farm where the Brennan family has quietly raised Eagle Kinfolk for four generations.

u-granary.name: The Granary Caern
u-granary.sub: The Mouse clan’s defiled urban caern
u-granary.html: Now it smells of rotten grain and copper. Jesselin and McKenzie defiled its heart with a blood rite, and Banes have bred in the lower cellars: grey, small, countless, gnawing sacks and spirits alike. The caern is dying. Grandmother Mouse still sleeps in its heart but no longer answers. Mercer keeps the last candles lit.

notes.title: Storyteller
notes.html: The caern can still be saved: the cleansing rite needs Garou of three clans in one cellar. Mercer doesn’t know it. Horatio suspects.

u-granary.brief: A caern hidden in the cellars of the old produce warehouses. It used to smell of grain, onions and candle-wax and fed on the city’s hunger the way a field feeds on rain.

u-grandmouse.name: Grandmother Mouse
u-grandmouse.html: She survived this too, barely. She lies curled in her thimble, weak and silent, her fur gone dull.
u-grandmouse.brief: A tiny, ancient, silver-furred mouse wearing a thimble for a hat. She was the most dangerous spirit in the Warrens because she had survived everything.

u-commission.name: Commission Row kin
u-commission.sub: The Wójcik family and the market workers
u-commission.html: They know the clan without quite knowing what it is, and they keep its doors.
u-commission.brief: Mouse Kinfolk families have worked the produce trade for generations: truckers, stall-holders, night watchmen.

u-ericasroom.name: Erica’s empty place
u-ericasroom.sub: Where Merik’s wife used to sleep · now a memorial room
u-ericasroom.html: Mira Kessler knew why Erica stopped coming, but Mira is dead and the secret died with her. Mercer has put candles here for all of them: Erica, Rosa, Teodor, Mira, and two unlit ones for Benny and Drake. Gunther, Erica’s old friend, sometimes sits here with him until dawn.
u-ericasroom.brief: A small cellar room in the Warrens kept exactly as Erica left it. She was a Gangrel the Mouse accepted as packmate, the rarest thing a vampire can earn.

u-hedgelords.name: The Hedgerow Lords
u-hedgelords.sub: Estate spirits of the North Shore
u-hedgelords.html: They have been known to hire Banes as watchmen.
u-hedgelords.brief: Proud, clipped spirits of old estates and their boundary hedges. They take trespass very seriously and everything else not at all.

u-doctorsravine.name: Doctors Park ravine
u-doctorsravine.sub: An old Wyld fold on the north shore
u-doctorsravine.brief: A steep, wild ravine to the lake where the Hedgerow Lords’ writ does not run. Mouse Garou go to ground here when the city is too much.

u-mousecave.name: The cave on Route 43
u-mousecave.html: A spirit of the cave, the Bone-Count, remembers every body ever brought in. Since Psychomachia it has been asking who will come to collect the Justicar’s.
u-mousecave.brief: In the Umbra the little cave is a hall of bones with a low door. The Justicar’s remains lay at the back.

u-thiensville.name: The mill-dam spirit
u-thiensville.brief: An old mill-dam spirit, slow and courteous, that keeps the northern river’s memory and trades it for news of the city.

u-lapham.name: Lapham’s Watcher
u-lapham.sub: The weather-spirit on the high hill
u-lapham.html: It is the best forecaster in the Umbra, and it will warn the clans of storms if asked politely.
u-lapham.brief: On the high hill at Delafield, where the state’s first weather observations were made, a careful spirit watches the sky and writes down everything it sees.

u-kettles.name: The Kettles
u-kettles.brief: Round glacial ponds that in the Umbra are eyes of the old ice, watching the sky. Garou Theurges come to read them.

u-bog.name: The Bog of First Waters
u-bog.brief: Mist and peat-light, and things too old to have shapes. Visiting is safe.

u-unnamed.name: The Unnamed
u-unnamed.sub: Something at the bottom of the bog
u-unnamed.html: Every clan has a story about the Garou who went down to ask it something and came back different.
u-unnamed.brief: A Wyld presence older than the bog. It does not speak; it changes those who listen.

u-holyhill.name: The sealed caern
u-holyhill.sub: The summit of the Hill of Two Prayers
u-holyhill.html: In the Umbra the hill wears a crown of stars and a basilica of light, and pilgrims of two faiths climb it side by side.

notes.title: Storyteller
notes.html: The seal was set by Usla’s band before their last battle. The Drowned Thief remembers the rite. An open caern could give Mercer a new home, or become the place where three clans finally make one sept.

u-holyhill.brief: A great caern, sealed with a rite nobody living remembers. Its moon bridges are cold.

u-edge.name: The Hunting Edge crossroads
u-edge.html: The Anubi and the Lupine both leave signs here for the other to read.
u-edge.brief: Claw-scored road and the ghosts of a hundred ambushes. Decker’s motel is a block south.

u-ancestors.name: The Ancestor Hollows
u-ancestors.sub: Forest Home, as the Garou see it
u-ancestors.html: They are not wraiths. They are the remembered strength of family. Kinfolk of all three clans lie here together.
u-ancestors.brief: The ancestor-spirits of three clans’ bloodlines gather among the old graves: grandmothers, great-uncles, a lupus elder who died in the 1918 snow.

u-domes.name: The Kept Wild
u-domes.html: The show garden changes sides depending on the season.
u-domes.brief: The jungle dome’s spirits are restless and want to go out into the Wisconsin winter. The desert dome’s spirits think they are mad.

u-northdam.name: The North Avenue Dam
u-northdam.html: It believes the dam will come down one day. It’s right, though nobody in 1991 would bet on it.
u-northdam.brief: A sullen, patient river-spirit pooled behind the old dam, remembering every word spoken over its water.

u-estabrook.name: Estabrook Falls
u-estabrook.brief: A short run of rapids where the river is loud and free. Garou who want to talk without being overheard by the Dammed Reach come here, below its reach.

u-soldiers.name: The Battle-Echo
u-soldiers.sub: The Soldiers Home, as war-spirits see it
u-soldiers.brief: Spirits of old battles gather around the veterans’ cemetery like crows on a fence. Ahroun of every clan come to sit with them before a fight.

u-crucible.name: The Crucible’s hunger
u-crucible.html: Garou who know what they are looking at can tell how many vampires fed there last night.
u-crucible.brief: The Kindred’s central hunting ground shows in the Umbra as a dim, sticky patch where small Banes collect like flies.

g-pangaea.name: The path to Pangaea
g-pangaea.html: Those who come back describe mammoth-spirits, and the smell of the first rain.
g-pangaea.brief: At the bottom of the bog a path opens into the Realm of Pangaea, the world as it was before people.

g-cyber.name: The Data-Sky
g-cyber.sub: Gate to the Weaver’s Cyber Realm
g-cyber.brief: From the top of the Spire, a thread leads up into the Cyber Realm: a city of pure pattern, lit by phosphor and paperwork.

g-malfeas.name: The Rendering Pit
g-malfeas.html: Parovich does not know it exists. He would be very interested.
g-malfeas.brief: Deep in the valley a pit of boiling tallow opens downward toward the Wyrm’s own realm. Tallow guards it.

g-aether.name: The Lunar Stair
g-aether.html: She does it once a year, for a price nobody has yet agreed to pay.
g-aether.brief: The Moonkeeper can open a silver stair from the clock face to the Aetherial Realm, where the stars live.

g-battle.name: The War-Field gate
g-battle.html: Ahroun go there to train, and some do not come back.
g-battle.brief: At the heart of the veterans’ cemetery a road leads into the Battleground, the realm of endless war.

g-legend.name: The Legendary Way
g-legend.brief: Behind the sealed caern a dim road leads to the Legendary Realm, where every story ever told about the Garou is true.

g-fork.name: Where the Silver Path forks
g-fork.html: No local Garou has found the fork. The fae, on their own side of things, would say the Dreaming is not the Umbra, and they would be right.
g-fork.brief: Lunes whisper that far out over Greatwater the moon’s road splits in two, and that one branch leads toward Arcadia.

u-wardstone.name: The defiled ward-stone
u-wardstone.sub: A guardian stone turned against the forest
u-wardstone.html: The House Goratrix rite turned the ward inside out: the stone no longer holds Banes back but calls them, and the Gauntlet around it has worn to a rag. Brother Sparrow has tried to cleanse it twice and twice retreated with burns.

notes.title: Storyteller
notes.html: Burned into the stone’s underside are sigils Mercer would recognise: the same as in the Granary’s defiled heart. This is Jesselin’s hand; McKenzie only paid in blood.

u-wardstone.brief: A boulder carved with Wendigo signs, which held the forest’s Gauntlet for a hundred years, split in two, the crack filled with caked blood.

u-banenest.name: The Bane nest
u-banenest.sub: A rotting hollow where they breed
u-banenest.html: The Eagle burn the nest out every week. Every week it grows back.
u-banenest.brief: A hollow where a spring used to rise, now choked with oily fog. In the Penumbra the trunks are covered with blisters, and Banes hatch from the blisters: small biting things like flayed ferrets, and larger things Coal-Eye won’t talk about.

u-blackcreek.name: The poisoned creek
u-blackcreek.sub: Water carrying the blight toward people
u-blackcreek.html: Mortals see only dead fish and sick cattle; Dot Brennan sees more.
u-blackcreek.brief: A creek running out of the blighted wood toward the Franklin farms. Its spirit is sick and raving, and in the Umbra its water is the colour of rust.

gp-grand.name: The Well Hall
gp-grand.html: The Nosferatu decide here what the rest of the city will be told, and what it will pay. A guest follows the guide and asks no questions about faces.
gp-grand.aliasText: The Nosferatu have a hall somewhere under downtown where they decide what the city knows. You will not be invited.
gp-grand.brief: The Well Hall: the huge round chamber of an old storm-water well under the west bank, turned into an assembly hall. Mother Agatha receives petitioners here.

gp-archive.name: The rumour archive
gp-archive.html: Cricket keeps the file and listens to the telephone lines from here. Mother Agatha decides who may read it.
gp-archive.alias: A vault under the Journal building
gp-archive.brief: The Milwaukee Journal's old pneumatic-post vault: rows of drawers with a card on every resident of the city, by night and by day.

gp-ratking.name: The Rat King
gp-ratking.html: It guards the western approaches to the Warrens and squeaks to Agatha about everyone who comes.
gp-ratking.alias: Something that squeaks in the western tunnels
gp-ratking.brief: The Rat King: a thousand rats fed on Nosferatu blood, their tails knotted into a single creature.

gp-market.name: The Rat Market
gp-market.html: The only place underground where the Nosferatu are glad to see strangers. A neonate who wants a forged licence, a clean car or the name of whoever is following them comes here. Since the invasion trade has halved, because everyone is afraid of the tunnels.
gp-market.brief: The Rat Market: the Nosferatu's neutral bazaar in the cellars of the old Commission Row warehouses under the Third Ward. Stalls of crates, lanterns on hooks, hooded traders: information, papers, weapons, bagged blood.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Trade, don't fight. Troublemakers are handed to the Council.

gp-parovich.name: Parovich’s abandoned rooms
gp-parovich.html: The Council's seals are intact. The bricks of the old passage to the Warrens have been broken out from inside.

notes.title: Who came back
notes.html: The vozhd came here. The Parovich inside it wanted to see his home.

gp-parovich.brief: Parovich's den under his Concordia mansion. The Council searched and sealed it.

gp-pocketdoor.name: The harbour lock
gp-pocketdoor.sub: Where the way under the lake begins
gp-pocketdoor.html: A passage slopes down from here under the lake.
gp-pocketdoor.brief: An old lock at the edge of the harbour. A grate is held by a Nosferatu padlock and a second seal nobody else recognises. Brother Dust keeps watch.

notes.title: Where it goes
notes.html: The passage leads to the Michigan Pocket. The second seal is a sluagh's.

gp-akawa.name: The cell under MECCA
gp-akawa.html: The Blood Brothers do not know where it is. The Nosferatu do.
gp-akawa.brief: A concrete boiler room in the Council's steam tunnels under MECCA, turned into a cell. Gracis's ghouls guard it.

notes.title: The prisoner
notes.html: Akawa is held here under a Blood Bond.

gp-pocketdoor2.name: The Undersea Door
gp-pocketdoor2.sub: The Pocket’s entrance from the Warrens’ side
gp-pocketdoor2.alias: A vault door in a cave wall
gp-pocketdoor2.brief: A door from an old bank vault set into a cave wall. On this side hangs a sign in Gaelic: "Closed until forgiven."

gp-gas.name: The Robinson gas station
gp-gas.alias: A gas station under the lake
gp-gas.brief: A gas station with a faded logo and working neon. The pumps still give fuel nobody ever delivered. Ivory took it from Highway 41 when the building was condemned. Jamie Robinson came here once, and left without a word.

gp-diner.name: The diner
gp-diner.brief: A chrome 1940s dining car with a DINER sign. The sluagh gather here to whisper. There is always a pie in the fridge that nobody baked.

gp-gazebo.name: The gazebo
gp-gazebo.brief: An octagonal bandstand from a demolished city park, where an orchestra played in the 1920s. Some nights there is music in it.

gp-houses.name: The street of forgotten houses
gp-houses.brief: Frame houses from the north side, torn down for the freeway and carried off by the sluagh with their wallpaper, the photographs on the walls and the smell of supper. The doors aren't locked.

gp-pens.name: The pens
gp-pens.brief: Wooden pens from the valley's old stockyards. Empty. The sluagh brought them so the city wouldn't forget what was killed in the valley.

gp-boxcar.name: The boxcar
gp-boxcar.brief: A rusted boxcar from an abandoned spur. Inside is a storeroom of signs, shop fronts, lamps and door handles: the small things that don't fit in buildings.

gp-truss.name: The bridge truss
gp-truss.sub: A span of a demolished railroad bridge
gp-truss.alias: A bridge truss over a crack
gp-truss.brief: A span of a demolished railroad bridge lies on the rocks over a black crack. They say that if you cross it you come out somewhere other than where you went in.

gp-angels.name: The angels
gp-angels.brief: Stone angels from moved and demolished cemeteries stand along the road, facing the way out. The Nosferatu set them up; that was their share of the work.

gp-lion.name: The stone lion and the memorials
gp-lion.brief: A lion from the façade of a demolished bank, a nameless obelisk, an abstract sculpture the city council declared "ugly". The Pocket keeps even what nobody liked.

gp-spire.name: The spire
gp-spire.sub: The steeple of a demolished church
gp-spire.brief: The white wooden steeple of a demolished church lies on a heap of brick. The bell inside sometimes rings by itself, at the death of another building above.

gp-gallery.name: The Gallery of Two Peoples
gp-gallery.sub: The shared place of the sluagh and the Nosferatu
gp-gallery.html: The last Nosferatu entry is from 1990. After it there is only Ivory's handwriting.
gp-gallery.brief: The Gallery of Two Peoples: a cave wall covered with drawings, names and dates. For generations the Nosferatu and the sluagh recorded here which building was saved, and by whom.

gp-ivory.name: Ivory’s lookout
gp-ivory.sub: Where she watches over the Pocket
gp-ivory.brief: A wooden fire tower from a hill outside town. Ivory sits at the top in her school uniform doing homework while the stolen city sleeps below her.

gp-wide.name: The gate of Warehouse No. 7
gp-wide.sub: The mouth of Dragos’s wide tunnel
gp-wide.html: The grate has been bent from inside twice already.
gp-wide.aliasText: There is a grate in Cudahy that the Council guards with ghouls. Something has bent it from below.
gp-wide.brief: The back wall of Warehouse No. 7 in Cudahy hides a gentle ramp a truck wide: the mouth of the Sabbat's wide tunnel. The Camarilla has put a grate and two ghouls here.

gp-shaft-ji.name: The Jones Island shaft
gp-shaft-ji.html: A single watchman is on duty at night. He has twice been found asleep at the bottom of the shaft, and does not remember going down.
gp-shaft-ji.alias: A Deep Tunnel shaft on Jones Island
gp-shaft-ji.aliasText: The city is digging an enormous tunnel three hundred feet under the river. The night watchmen do not like it.
gp-shaft-ji.brief: A vertical shaft of the Deep Tunnel, the storage tunnel under construction since 1986, beside the Jones Island treatment plant.

gp-shaft-n.name: The North Avenue shaft
gp-shaft-n.html: Gunther goes down here when he wants to cross the city unseen.
gp-shaft-n.alias: A shaft by the North Avenue dam
gp-shaft-n.brief: The northern shaft of the Deep Tunnel, by the North Avenue dam.

gp-shaft-v.name: The valley shaft
gp-shaft-v.html: The workers left after a night shift did not come back up.
gp-shaft-v.brief: An abandoned Deep Tunnel construction shaft in the middle of the Menomonee Valley.

gp-miller.name: The Miller caves
gp-miller.html: Leave something cold for the cellars' keeper. Nobody remembers who started the custom.
gp-miller.aliasText: There are cold cellars in Miller Valley where the Nosferatu and the Gangrel meet. They give tours by day.
gp-miller.brief: The Miller caves, 1850s lagering cellars dug into the hillside: a tour stop by day and a neutral waystation of the Nosferatu and the Gangrel by night.

notes.title: The custom
notes.html: Neutral ground. Leave something cold.

gp-chestnut.name: The Chestnut Street cellars
gp-chestnut.html: From here you can reach the Spine, the trunk sewer under Wisconsin Avenue, without going up to the street.
gp-chestnut.alias: Cellars under the Pabst brewery hill
gp-chestnut.brief: Vaulted cellars under the Pabst brewery where ice for the lager was stored.

gp-bridge.name: The door under the bridge
gp-bridge.html: Nobody forces it. That is the whole agreement.
gp-bridge.brief: The service door under the Wisconsin Avenue bridge, seen from inside: a short brick passage straight into the Spine.

gp-usla.name: Usla’s burial
gp-usla.sub: Under St. Joan of Arc Chapel
gp-usla.html: Haberman would give a year of his unlife to get in here.
gp-usla.brief: A narrow crack in the dolomite directly under St. Joan of Arc Chapel. The stone is warm to the touch, and no spell works.

notes.title: The totems
notes.html: Here Usla hid the Talon of the Eagle and the Eye of the Coyote, reshaped as his own hand and eye.

gp-ossuary.name: The bone workshop
gp-ossuary.html: Dragos Dalca sculpted his creatures here. Castor lives here now and carries on his master's work.
gp-ossuary.brief: A tannery basement under the Menomonee Valley: tables of fused bone, walls laced with sinew, jars of eyes on the shelves.

gp-hounds.name: Dragos’s hounds
gp-hounds.html: Dragos made them from dogs and from the homeless. Castor feeds them.
gp-hounds.alias: Something that hunts the valley sewers
gp-hounds.brief: Six, or by now five, things the size of calves, with human hands for forepaws. They hunt as a pack in the valley sewers and can smell vampire blood.

gp-choir.name: The Choir
gp-choir.html: The Black Water pack's priest gives the same name to something much larger.
gp-choir.brief: The Choir: prisoners from the viaduct camp, sewn into one crawling body with a dozen mouths. It sings the hymns its parts remember and weeps when it is fed.

gp-gills.name: The Gills
gp-gills.sub: Fish-men from the sewers by the fish plant
gp-gills.html: Cold, slippery, and sometimes they climb out onto the piers.
gp-gills.aliasText: Dockworkers say something climbs out onto the piers on foggy nights.
gp-gills.brief: The Gills: what the Sabbat made of fish and people on the fish plant's conveyor. A few survived and went down into the harbour sewers.

gp-wall.name: The living wall
gp-wall.brief: A partition of flesh grown across the wide tunnel to slow pursuit. It still breathes and grabs at anything that comes too close.

gp-stalker.name: The Faceless
gp-stalker.sub: A loner in the southern galleries
gp-stalker.html: It lures hunters and the homeless with the voices of their families.
gp-stalker.alias: A voice in the southern galleries
gp-stalker.brief: The Faceless: a tall thing without a face that repeats the voices it hears.

gp-shovel.name: The shovelhead dugout
gp-shovel.html: Noemí Santana visits them with blood once a week and calls them "the reserves".
gp-shovel.brief: A side gallery where three Sabbat shovelheads, dug out of their graves too late to fight, have learned to live like animals.

gp-vozd.name: The vozhd
gp-vozd.html: It is a vozhd, a Tzimisce war-ghoul, the last great work of Dragos Dalca.
gp-vozd.brief: A colossal thing of dozens of fused bodies fills an abandoned drift of the Deep Tunnel from wall to wall. It sleeps until disturbed.

notes.title: His face
notes.html: One of the faces in its flank is Parovich. He never sleeps.

gp-drake.name: The spiral den
gp-drake.html: Drake, the Lupine who killed Victor, sleeps in a concrete pipe here and sometimes goes up into the spirit world.
gp-drake.brief: A storm culvert under the concrete Kinnickinnic, its walls scored with clawed spirals.

gp-cistern.name: The Black Water cistern
gp-cistern.html: The last Sabbat pack in the city, the Black Water, sleeps on the island in sleeping bags. Hieronymus performs the Vaulderie here.
gp-cistern.alias: A flooded cistern under Walker’s Point
gp-cistern.brief: The Black Water cistern: a flooded brick hall under Walker's Point with a single dry island in the middle.

notes.title: Velez
notes.html: Guillem Velez comes here when the yacht is not safe.

gp-maxcache.name: Maximus’s cache
gp-maxcache.sub: In a sewer under Bay View
gp-maxcache.html: Maximus McKenzie comes back here once a week.
gp-maxcache.alias: A niche behind a sewer grate
gp-maxcache.brief: A niche behind a sewer grate under Bay View: boxes of totem blanks, blood in ampoules, a list of buyers.

t-lupine.name: Lupine lands
t-lupine.html: Even Shorewood, the North Shore and their lakefront parks fall outside any Kindred patrol. The highways are watched. Sensible Kindred who must leave arrange a sealed daylight truck or a night flight.
t-lupine.brief: Everything past the Anubi patrol line belongs to the Werewolves. Roads, railways and the suburbs beyond are their hunting ground. Few Kindred cross them alive, and none do it by choice.

t-anubi.name: The Outlands (Anubi patrol zone)
t-anubi.html: The border drawn here is their outermost patrol route; Good Hope Road marks its northern limit. If you want to talk to Decker, drive Good Hope Road after dark and wait.
t-anubi.src: Milwaukee by Night, War Map p. 21; Geography p. 18; Kindred p. 35
t-anubi.brief: The Outlands: the no-man's-land of suburbs between the city and the wilds. Mark Decker's Anubi patrol its outer edge every night and ambush Lupine raiders before they reach the Barrens.

t-bb.name: Blood Brothers territory
t-bb.html: The Brothers used to leave quiet travellers alone. Since Akawa disappeared the gang is in turmoil, Wrecker and Ethan Stone are holding it together, and nobody can vouch for its streets.
t-bb.src: Milwaukee by Night, War Map p. 21; West-Downtown p. 22
t-bb.brief: Blood Brothers territory: the largest slice of the Barrens, from West Downtown out to the Zoo Freeway. Most Anarch rumbles happen here, because downtown is too well watched by the Elders.

t-union.name: Union turf: East Downtown & the lakeshore
t-union.html: Travel in groups. Turk has killed few Kindred, but many more have limped home much worse for meeting him. The gang is bleeding members and losing ground to the Blood Brothers.
t-union.src: Milwaukee by Night, War Map p. 21; East Downtown p. 26
t-union.brief: Union turf: the narrow lakeside strip east of the Milwaukee River, from the UWM end of the East Side down through the Lower East Side and the I-794 corridor into Bay View. The Union leaves Elders alone but mauls neonates who wander in alone.

notes.title: Why it is weak
notes.html: The Union lost face, and members, because the late Prince had been Dominating and Blood Bonding its key figures for five years.

t-elders-dt.name: Elder control: downtown core
t-elders-dt.html: The Anarchs fight elsewhere; the Elders watch from the penthouses. Since the Prince's death the downtown blocks are held by the Council as a body, which means by whoever can get three votes.
t-elders-dt.src: Milwaukee by Night, War Map p. 21; pp. 22–24
t-elders-dt.brief: The glass-and-steel heart of Kindred Milwaukee, spanning the river around MECCA, the Hyatt and City Hall. The Council meets here, the oldest havens are here, and heavy police patrols keep the street-level riff-raff away.

t-elders-air.name: Elder control: General Mitchell Field
t-elders-air.html: Gracis's spies log every arrival. Parovich's people used to do the same.
t-elders-air.src: Milwaukee by Night, War Map p. 21; Geography p. 18
t-elders-air.brief: General Mitchell Field: with every road and railway running through Lupine country, the airport is the city's real front door. The Council holds it tightly.

t-null.name: The Marquette null zone
t-null.html: Blood magic risks a painful backlash inside the zone, while Auspex and Protean grow stronger. The Tremere and several independent Kindred study it. So do the Lupine.
t-null.src: Milwaukee by Night, History p. 13; Geography p. 20; Tremere p. 50
t-null.aliasText: Magic does not work at Marquette. Tremere talk about it when they think you are not listening.
t-null.brief: A "magic-dead" zone covering the Marquette campus: north past Mount Sinai Medical Center, west to the old Children's Hospital, south almost to the Menomonee. Thaumaturgy fails here.

notes.title: The cause
notes.html: The cause lies under St. Joan of Arc Chapel: Usla's buried totems.

t-crucible.name: The Crucible
t-crucible.html: Many Kindred hunt here every night: Missing Persons, Arabian Nights, Deadman's Party, Peaches and Cream, Soldier Boy, Howler and Starscape. With the Prince dead, somebody will try to claim it soon.
t-crucible.src: Milwaukee by Night, Things to Do, pp. 23–24
t-crucible.brief: The Crucible: Milwaukee's central hunting grounds, a West Downtown knot of bars and dance clubs. No faction has tried to claim it yet.

t-coyote.name: Range of the Coyote pack
t-coyote.html: This autumn his wolves are also helping the Eagle burn Banes out of the southern woods.
t-coyote.src: Milwaukee by Night, Lupine p. 69; placement is Storyteller discretion
t-coyote.brief: The range of the Coyote, the principal Lupine pack: just under a dozen strong, every one a Red Talon, a born wolf. It is led by the coolly rational Horatio Sims.

notes.title: What Horatio wants
notes.html: The Kindred off balance long enough for him to hold Marquette and dig up the totems.

t-eagle.name: Range of the Eagle pack
t-eagle.html: They blame the Coyote for the theft of their totem's Talon. This autumn the raids have mostly stopped.
t-eagle.src: Milwaukee by Night, Lupine p. 70; placement is Storyteller discretion
t-eagle.brief: The range of the Eagle pack along the southern approaches, astride I-94: about eight Garou, almost all Wendigo, who raid the city roughly once a week regardless of the odds.

notes.title: Why the raids stopped
notes.html: House Goratrix poisoned their woods with Banes.

notes.title: Seven Fires
notes.html: The pack secretly owns the Seven Fires casino.

t-mouse.name: Range of the Mouse pack
t-mouse.html: Merik's Gangrel wife ran with them. This autumn they ambushed a group of Kindred on Route 43 north. Since then the pack has almost disappeared.
t-mouse.src: Milwaukee by Night, Lupine p. 70; A Midnight Moon
t-mouse.brief: The range of the Mouse pack: the northern woods and the North Shore lakefront. Once fifteen Garou, mostly Glass Walkers, who lived in the city in human form and hated Vampires even by Lupine standards.

notes.title: What happened to them
notes.html: The Sabbat and House Goratrix all but wiped out and corrupted the pack. Of the old Mouse only Mercer remains, and Drake belongs to the Wyrm.

t-dz-cudahy.name: Danger: the Cudahy warehouse yards
t-dz-cudahy.html: A Camarilla grate and two ghouls now guard the wide ramp behind Warehouse No. 7. The grate has twice been bent from below.
t-dz-cudahy.brief: Danger: the Cudahy warehouse yards. The Sabbat's creatures came up into the city here during the invasion. Stray dogs will not enter the yards, and night-shift workers have stopped taking the shortcut along the tracks.

t-dz-valley.name: Danger: Tannery Row
t-dz-valley.html: Dragos's hounds, and worse. The Blood Brothers cross the valley in pairs now.
t-dz-valley.aliasText: Blood Brothers cross the Menomonee Valley in pairs now, and never on foot after three in the morning.
t-dz-valley.brief: Danger: Tannery Row, the old tanneries and packing houses of the Menomonee Valley. At night things come up through the drains to hunt.

t-dz-harbor.name: Danger: the fish-plant cordon
t-dz-harbor.html: Under the piers live the Gills, things made of fish and men on the plant's conveyors. They climb out onto the docks on foggy nights.
t-dz-harbor.brief: Danger: the fish-plant cordon. Police tape, a security trailer and the smell of burnt ammonia around the plant where Jade Riley killed Dragos.

t-dz-blight.name: Danger: the blighted Root River woods
t-dz-blight.html: The Eagle pack of Lupines fights them every night. Anyone else who wanders in is either a target or a meal.
t-dz-blight.brief: Danger: the blighted Root River woods. The forest is dying, and things pour out of the poisoned groves every night.

notes.title: Who did it
notes.html: House Goratrix poisoned the forest to keep the Garou busy while the Sabbat moved in.

r-ruins.name: The distant ruins
r-ruins.brief: The distant ruins of the Crownless Ward.

r-wolf.name: The Country of the Wolf’s Eye
r-wolf.brief: The Country of the Wolf's Eye, over the Marquette zone.

r-index.name: The Unfinished Index
r-index.brief: The Unfinished Index, under the Central Library.

r-orchard.name: The Glass Orchard
r-orchard.brief: The Glass Orchard, over the Mitchell Park Domes.

r-seat.name: The Far Guest’s Seat
r-seat.brief: The Far Guest's Seat, far out on the lake.

uz-thicket.name: The Glass Thicket
uz-thicket.sub: Downtown, as the Weaver sees it
uz-thicket.html: Pattern Spiders the size of buses walk the parapets, reinforcing the Gauntlet strand by strand. The few Wyld spirits left live in the cracks and pay rent to clerks. Kindred havens show here as cold, rotten spots that the spiders refuse to touch.

facts.v: Weaver

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Everything must be counted. A spirit that cannot give its number is unmade and filed. Garou who step sideways here must name themselves aloud before the Pattern Spiders let them move.

uz-thicket.brief: Downtown’s Umbral reflection is a forest of crystal: towers grown from spun glass, skywalks thick with web, and bank vaults ringing like bells.

uz-claw.name: The Clawed Sky
uz-claw.sub: Over Marquette and the buried relics
uz-claw.html: Joan of Arc Chapel. Each yearns for its owner so hard that the sky above Marquette is torn open in long red scratches. A great eye watches from the clouds on one side and a talon rakes them on the other. The Gauntlet slams shut and swings open like a door in wind.

facts.v: 2–9, flickering
Totemic storm

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Everything happens twice. Every Gift, rite and spirit summoned here arrives doubled: one answer from the Eagle’s side and one from the Coyote’s. The two answers never agree.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: Horatio’s pack and the Eagle both have a Theurge camped at the storm’s edge. Neither has noticed that Dr. Mortius has strung wards along the zone’s north side, and those wards are starting to hum.

uz-claw.brief: The book’s “magic-dead” zone is, in the Umbra, a permanent storm. Two halves of two totems, the Talon of the Eagle and the Eye of the Coyote, lie under St.

uz-gambrinus.name: Gambrinus Hill
uz-gambrinus.html: His halls are a smoky Bavarian banquet that never ends. He is ailing: the brewery is losing money, and in the Umbra the vats are running low.

facts.v: Genius loci

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Hospitality must be accepted. Refuse an offered drink and you have declared a feud; accept it and you may not raise a claw until you leave the hill.

uz-gambrinus.brief: Beer has been brewed on this hill since the 1840s, and its spirit has grown into a crowned old king of copper, foam and civic pride who calls himself Gambrinus.

uz-copper.name: The Copper Queen’s Valley
uz-copper.html: She and Gambrinus are old rivals and occasional lovers. Her court is the busiest in the Penumbra: a beer hall where spirits of every allegiance drink side by side because no one dares break her peace.

facts.v: Genius loci

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Every guest pays in a story. The Queen collects them in barrels, and a story told here becomes common knowledge in every tavern spirit in the city by morning.

uz-copper.brief: The biggest brewery left in town has a spirit to match: a vast, bright Copper Queen in a crown of hop-vines, healthy, rich and expanding.

uz-dryvats.name: The Dry Vats
uz-dryvats.sub: The closed brewery on the river bluff
uz-dryvats.html: Weaver salvage-spirits are already measuring the walls for offices.

facts.v: Fading genius

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Nothing new may be started. Gifts of creation and new pacts fail here; only endings, inventories and farewells hold.

uz-dryvats.brief: The big brewery on the bluff closed in 1982, and its spirit is dying slowly. The Widow of the Vats walks empty fermenting rooms, still polishing kettles nobody will fill.

uz-ironhorse.name: The Iron Horse Run
uz-ironhorse.html: Their lord is the Iron Horse: half engine, half stallion, loud enough to crack the Gauntlet. The Blood Brothers ride its children without knowing it. The spirits have decided that Akawa, who rides in wolf shape, is a strange kind of Garou.

facts.v: Weaver–Wyld

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Speed is truth. Whoever arrives first is believed; whoever is passed on the road must concede the argument.

uz-ironhorse.brief: Next door to the Copper Queen, the motorcycle works breeds chrome Jagglings that run in howling packs.

uz-rendering.name: The Rendering
uz-rendering.sub: The Menomonee Valley tanneries and packing houses
uz-rendering.html: The ghosts of slaughtered beasts run in terrified herds through the smoke. The Garou should hate it, and do, but nobody has ever been strong enough to cleanse it.

facts.v: Wyrm

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Everything is reduced. Spirits that linger here are boiled down into simpler and hungrier things, and wounds taken in the valley don’t heal until you leave it.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: The stockyard herd-spirits have started stampeding out of the valley at dusk. Something new is driving them, and it smells of the Sabbat.

uz-rendering.brief: A century of stockyards, tanneries and rendering vats has left a spirit-landscape of boiling pits, hide-curtains and rivers of tallow.

uz-works.name: The Transmuting Works
uz-works.sub: Jones Island and the sewage-to-fertiliser plant
uz-works.html: Grandmother Compost presides, ancient and patient. Wyrm, Weaver and Wyld all claim the Works, and none of them is wrong.

facts.v: Contested

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Everything given becomes useful. Leave a thing here and the Works will turn it into something else. You don’t choose what.

uz-works.brief: The great plant on Jones Island turns the city’s waste into fertiliser, and its Umbral reflection is a cathedral of alchemy where Wyrm-filth goes in and Wyld-green comes out.

uz-chained.name: The Chained River
uz-chained.html: The Concrete Warden patrols the banks and reinforces the chains each night. Freeing the river would flood the South Side’s Penumbra with Wyld water, and some of the spirits who live here like their dry cellars.

facts.v: Weaver over Wyld

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Nothing may stop moving. Stand still in the channel and the current, or the Concrete Warden, carries you to the lake.

uz-chained.brief: In the 1960s the Kinnickinnic was poured into a concrete trough to control its floods. In the Umbra the river spirit lies bound in grey bands, still alive and thrashing.

uz-polishmoon.name: The Ward of the Polish Moon
uz-polishmoon.sub: The South Side under the great clock
uz-polishmoon.html: Lunes love it: a second moon that never wanes. They have built a silver court around it, and moon-folk dance there whether Luna is full or dark. The Mouse pack’s Galliards come here to learn the old songs, and Garou of any clan can swear oaths under it that the Lunes will enforce.

facts.v: Lunar

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Under the Polish Moon the hour is whatever the clock says, and a promise made beneath its face binds until it strikes midnight. After that it binds forever.

uz-polishmoon.brief: The four-faced Allen-Bradley clock rises over the South Side, and the neighbourhood calls it the Polish Moon.

uz-accord.name: Olmsted’s Accord
uz-accord.html: Wyld and Weaver live here by agreement. That agreement made the Accord the one place where the three feuding clans can meet without killing each other, under the Lake Park Truce.

facts.v: Balance

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Paths must be kept. Spirits that leave the designed paths lose their names until dawn, and blood spilled on the Treaty Green is carried by the Lake Breeze to every caern in the city.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: The Truce was last invoked in 1983. Horatio wants to call a moot here before the first snow, not for peace this time but for war on the Banes in the poisoned forest. The Eagle have not said whether they will come. From the Mouse, only Mercer can.

uz-accord.brief: A landscape architect laid out these ravines and lawns as a city’s idea of nature, and the spirits took the design seriously.

uz-lake.name: Greatwater
uz-lake.html: Wreck-spirits, fish swarms, ice-memories and storms all live in it. Greatwater, the lake’s own vast spirit, is neither friendly nor hostile. It is simply bigger than every quarrel on the shore. Usla went into the lake to die, and Greatwater has kept him.

facts.v: Wyld

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: The lake keeps what it takes. What drowns or is thrown into Greatwater belongs to it, and getting anything back requires a gift of equal weight.

uz-lake.brief: The Umbral lake is a living inland sea, deep blue and lit from below by currents of spirit-light.

uz-breeze.name: The Lake Breeze Strand
uz-breeze.html: The book’s Lupines swim the lake and come ashore here to reach the Union. In the Umbra, this is the road they take.

facts.v: Air

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: It is always cooler by the lake. Rage gathers slowly here and frenzy is hard to reach, which is why Lupine raiders use the shore to approach unseen and why they must fight elsewhere.

uz-breeze.brief: A long ribbon of wind, beach and bluff, ruled by the Lake Breeze, the spirit every Milwaukeean knows from the weather report.

uz-stitch.name: The Stitchwork
uz-stitch.html: Where they were cut through neighbourhoods, the Penumbra still shows the outlines of streets that were erased, like scar tissue under the stitches. Gridlock Jagglings graze on the slowdowns.

facts.v: Weaver

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Keep to your lane. A spirit that crosses the Stitchwork anywhere but at a ramp is thrown back where it came from, and the spiders remember who tried.

uz-stitch.brief: The freeways are the Weaver’s sutures, pulling the city’s spirit-flesh tight along their lines.

uz-hush.name: The Hush
uz-hush.html: On the death side of the Shroud, the poor-farm graves are being opened. The spirits feel it as an earthquake.

facts.v: Wyrm & healing

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: No one may raise their voice. Shouted words become Banes of despair. Whispered ones are heard by the healing spirits and sometimes answered.
