uz-hush.brief: Asylums, poor farms and hospitals, a century of them, on one stretch of county land. The Umbra here is soft, grey and quiet, haunted by Murmur, a Bane of despair, and tended by the Healers’ Lantern, a gentle spirit that walks the wards.

uz-zoo.name: The Embassy of Beasts
uz-zoo.html: The zoo’s wolves have a spirit of their own, the Grey Ambassador, who speaks for every captive pack.

facts.v: Gaia

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Captivity is honoured as truce. No hunting inside the walls, and any creature here may ask any other for news of its homeland.

uz-zoo.brief: Animal-spirits from every continent are kept here, homesick and dignified. They treat the zoo as a court in exile, receive Garou as visiting diplomats, and trade news of distant Umbral lands for news of the lake.

uz-spindle.name: The Departure Spindle
uz-spindle.html: It is the most reliable way out of the city’s Umbra and the most watched. The Pattern Spiders keep a manifest of every spirit that departs.

facts.v: Weaver

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Everything must leave. Spirits can only stay at the airport by holding a ticket for somewhere else; Garou who linger feel an overwhelming urge to go.

uz-spindle.brief: A great Weaver spindle spins flight paths into the sky: shining threads to Chicago and everywhere beyond.

uz-lawn.name: The Lawn Sea
uz-lawn.html: This is where Decker’s Anubi ride and where the Lupine raiders cross. The Weaver keeps it tidy. Underneath, the old prairie is still waiting.

facts.v: Weaver

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Nothing may grow above the fence line. Wyld spirits in the suburbs are trimmed back each week, and a Garou who loses her temper on a lawn draws every Mowing Spider in the township.

uz-lawn.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The outline follows the waking map’s range for this territory.
uz-lawn.brief: Mile after mile of neat, quiet, spirit-poor suburb: hedge-spirits trimmed into shape, lawn-spirits mown flat, malls glowing like hives.

uz-coyote.name: Coyote Country
uz-coyote.sub: The quarries and the north-western woods
uz-coyote.html: Every one of them is a Red Talon, a wolf born, and to them the human city is a festering wound on Gaia’s body; they go near its lights only when they must. The Penumbra here is ochre and dusty, full of echoes. Coyote’s Grin, the totem’s avatar, can be glimpsed on any ridge, laughing at something nobody else heard.

facts.v: Garou (Coyote · Red Talons)

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Every bargain hides a trick, and the truth may only be spoken as a joke. Spirits here answer a straight question with a riddle, and the Coyote expect you to laugh.

uz-coyote.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The outline follows the waking map’s range for this territory.
uz-coyote.brief: Limestone quarries, flooded pits and second-growth woods west and north-west of the city, held by Horatio Sims’s Clan of the Coyote.

uz-eagle.name: Eagle Height
uz-eagle.sub: The Root River woods and the southern approaches
uz-eagle.html: They are fewer than the Coyote, angrier, and they raid the city every week. The sky is white and enormous here, and the Wounded Eagle circles overhead missing one talon, crying for it.

facts.v: Garou (Eagle · Wendigo)

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Nothing is forgiven. Every debt is remembered, and spirits here will repeat to you every wrong you have ever done to an Eagle.

uz-eagle.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The outline follows the waking map’s range for this territory.
uz-eagle.brief: Tall pines, river bottoms and farm country south and south-west of the city, held by the Clan of the Eagle.

uz-warrens.name: The Mouse Warrens
uz-warrens.sub: Commission Row, the Third Ward cellars
uz-warrens.html: The Umbra here is a maze of grain-sacks, crates and tunnels lit by candle-stubs, and most of the candles have gone out. During the failed Sabbat invasion the House Goratrix Tremere Jesselin and Maximus McKenzie hunted the pack down with the Sabbat: Rosa, Little Teodor and Mira Kessler were killed, Benny and Drake were broken and given to the Wyrm. Of the Mouse’s Glass Walkers only Mercer survives. Erica, Merik’s Gangrel wife, used to run here; hers is no longer the only empty room.

facts.v: Garou (Mouse), failing

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: The small may pass and the large must ask. Any spirit or Garou in a smaller shape used to move freely, and anything bigger than a dog needed a Mouse to vouch for it. Only one Mouse is left to vouch now, and the Banes in the cellars take advantage: they get in because they are small.

uz-warrens.brief: Beneath the Glass Thicket’s southern edge, under the old produce warehouses of Commission Row, the Clan of the Mouse kept its urban caern.

uz-hedgerow.name: The Hedgerow Lands
uz-hedgerow.sub: The North Shore and the northern woods
uz-hedgerow.html: The Mouse range here when they leave the city.

facts.v: Weaver & old Wyld

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Trespass is the only sin. Crossing a property line without leave is a crime the spirits punish; everything else is forgivable.

uz-hedgerow.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The outline follows the waking map’s range for this territory.
uz-hedgerow.brief: The wealthy North Shore and the river ravines beyond it: estates guarded by proud Hedgerow Lords, ravines full of old Wyld, and the north road where the Mouse pack ambushed the Mask on Merik’s orders.

uz-moraine.name: The Moraine
uz-moraine.sub: The Kettle Moraine country, far west

facts.v: Deep Wyld

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: The old ice remembers. Weaver things fail here: watches stop, engines stall, and fetishes made in factories go quiet.

uz-moraine.brief: Glacial hills, kettle ponds and kames left by the last ice sheet. In the Umbra the ice has not entirely left: blue-white spirits move under the hills and the ponds look back.

uz-bog.name: The Bog of First Waters
uz-bog.sub: The great bog, north of the city
uz-bog.html: The Penumbra is mist and peat-light, with things too old to have shapes, and somewhere in the middle there is a path to Pangaea.

facts.v: Deep Wyld

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Names dissolve. Stay longer than a night and you forget your own; spirits here have none and want none.

uz-bog.brief: An old bog that the Weaver never got its threads into. The Gauntlet is almost nothing here.

uz-holyhill.name: The Hill of Two Prayers
uz-holyhill.html: Christian pilgrims and Gaian spirits both pray here and, unusually, neither minds. Whoever reopens the caern could found a true sept for Milwaukee. The three clans would have to agree on who that is.

facts.v: Sealed caern

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Climb only on foot. No shapeshifting, no step sideways and no flight carries you up the hill; it must be walked.

uz-holyhill.brief: The highest ground for miles carries a basilica on its summit and, in the Umbra, a great caern that has been sealed since before any living Garou was born.

uz-edge.name: The Hunting Edge
uz-edge.html: Spirits of battle gather here like crows. Decker’s Anubi patrol it every night.

facts.v: War

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: No truce after sunset. Any pact made on Good Hope Road ends when the sun goes down. The Anubi and the Garou both know it, and both use it.

uz-edge.brief: The northern boundary of Kindred territory is a raw wound in the Penumbra: claw-scored asphalt, the ghosts of ambushes, and country-club woods full of eyes.

uz-ancestors.name: The Ancestor Hollows
uz-ancestors.sub: Forest Home and the old cemeteries
uz-ancestors.html: They are memory made spirit, the remembered strength of bloodlines. Kinfolk of all three clans are buried here, side by side, the only place they lie together.

facts.v: Gaia

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Speak of the dead with respect or not at all. Ancestor-spirits answer Garou who honour them, and they turn their backs, for a year, on anyone who mocks them.

uz-ancestors.brief: Garou ancestor-spirits gather where the city keeps its dead. They are not wraiths, which live on the far side of the Shroud.

uz-climates.name: The Three Climates
uz-climates.html: Here they are the rare thing, a working partnership. The jungle-spirits are restless and want out.

facts.v: Wyld under glass

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Each climate keeps its own season. Weather-Gifts work only in the dome whose season matches them.

uz-climates.brief: Three domes hold three kept Wylds: a jungle, a desert and a show garden. The Weaver built the glass and the Wyld filled it.

uz-dammed.name: The Dammed Reach
uz-dammed.sub: The Milwaukee River above the North Avenue dam
uz-dammed.html: It is waiting for the dam to come down, and it believes, without any evidence, that it will.

facts.v: Weaver over Wyld

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Still water keeps secrets. Anything spoken over the impounded river is remembered by it and can be called back up by anyone who knows the right question.

uz-dammed.brief: The old North Avenue dam holds the river in a long, slow pool. The river spirit is sullen and patient behind it, collecting every word spoken over its water.

uz-blight.name: The Blighted Wood
uz-blight.sub: The poisoned forests of Franklin and the Root River
uz-blight.html: Their blood magic lanced them like boils, and the Banes came through. The plan was simple: while the Garou cleaned their forest, they would have no time for the city. It worked. The pines weep black, the creeks smell of copper, and the Eagle, and sometimes the Coyote with them, have been fighting for weeks.

facts.v: Wyrm

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Everything that guarded now bites. Wards, ward-stones and tree-signs are turned against their makers: a Gift called here answers a Bane twice as readily as a Garou, and every drop of spilled Gnosis draws more.

uz-blight.brief: In late autumn 1991, while the Sabbat came into the city, the House Goratrix Tremere Jesselin and Maximus McKenzie walked the southern woods and defiled the protected places: the ward-stones, springs and sacred trees around the Bleeding Pine.

gz-grand.name: The Grand Warrens
gz-grand.sub: The Nosferatu’s main refuge under downtown
gz-grand.html: Clean, dry halls, maps on the walls, a market in rumours. Outsiders come in only with a guide.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: A guest follows the guide and asks no questions about faces.

gz-grand.aliasText: Most of the city's Nosferatu live in tunnels under the west bank. You go in only with a guide.
gz-grand.brief: The Grand Warrens: old storm drains, the cellars of demolished buildings and abandoned pneumatic-post channels under the river's west bank. Most of the city's Nosferatu live here.

gz-market.name: The Rat Market
gz-market.sub: An underground bazaar beneath the Third Ward
gz-market.html: Information, papers, weapons, bagged blood. Since the invasion trade has halved.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Trade, don't fight. Troublemakers are handed to the Council.

gz-market.brief: The Rat Market: knocked-through cellars of the old Commission Row warehouses under the Third Ward, where the Nosferatu keep a neutral market.

gz-steam.name: The steam tunnels

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: The tunnels belong to the Council.

notes.title: The cell
notes.html: The cell where Akawa is held is down here.

gz-steam.aliasText: The Elders move between MECCA and the Hyatt without ever going outside.
gz-steam.brief: The steam tunnels: hot, cramped passages lined with district-heating pipes, joining the basements of MECCA, the Hyatt and the government buildings. The Elders use them to move between Elysia unseen.

gz-null.name: The Hush under the chapel
gz-null.sub: The null zone reaches down as well
gz-null.html: At the very bottom is the place where Usla buried the halves of two totems.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Spells fall silent. You will have to rely on your hands.

gz-null.brief: The Hush: under the Marquette campus magic fails below ground as well as above. The sewers are strangely quiet; the rats do not squeak and the water runs without a sound.

gz-brew.name: The Miller caves
gz-brew.html: The Nosferatu and the Gangrel use them as a waystation.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Leave something cold for the cellars' keeper.

gz-brew.brief: The Miller caves: cold 1850s lagering cellars dug into the hillside of Miller Valley. A tour stop by day and a neutral meeting place by night.

gz-flesh.name: The flesh tunnels
gz-flesh.sub: Dragos’s workshops under the Menomonee Valley
gz-flesh.html: Dragos set up his workshops here. Most of his army died, but the surviving creatures came back here as to a nest, and Castor feeds them. The Nosferatu give these tunnels a wide berth.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Here, you are what is hunted.

gz-flesh.brief: The flesh tunnels under the old tanneries and slaughterhouses of the Menomonee Valley. In places the walls are alive: meat and bone grown into the brick.

gz-southnest.name: The southern nests
gz-southnest.html: The Sabbat's creatures marched to the city along it. Loners and small packs that nobody finished off live in its side galleries.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Move fast and don't answer the voices.

gz-southnest.brief: The southern nests along the wide tunnel that runs north from the Cudahy warehouses.

gz-sabbat.name: The Black Water cistern
gz-sabbat.sub: The last Sabbat lair · Walker’s Point
gz-sabbat.html: Guillem Velez comes here when his yacht is not safe. In the cistern's dark a Lasombra is at his strongest.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: The shadows here look back.

gz-sabbat.brief: The Black Water cistern: a flooded old cistern under Walker's Point, the last Sabbat lair in the city.

gz-drake.name: Drake’s den
gz-drake.html: Drake hides here: once a go-between for the late Prince's killers, now a creature of the Wyrm.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Never walk in a spiral.

gz-drake.brief: A forgotten stretch of the storm culverts under the concrete-lined Kinnickinnic. The walls are scratched with spirals.

gz-vozd.name: The vozhd’s lair
gz-vozd.sub: Construction drifts of the Deep Tunnel

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Say nothing. It listens with voices.

notes.title: Parovich
notes.html: Parovich's face is in its flank.

gz-vozd.alias: A drift of the Deep Tunnel
gz-vozd.brief: An abandoned side drift of the Deep Tunnel, three hundred feet underground.

gz-flood.name: The drowned galleries
gz-flood.sub: Old sewers under the East Side
gz-flood.html: The Nosferatu go through only on rafts.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Never put your hands in the water.

gz-flood.brief: Old brick sewers under the East Side, flooded when the new ones came into service. The water stands chest-deep, and something swims in it.

gz-pocket.name: The Michigan Pocket
gz-pocket.sub: An impossible cave under the lake
gz-pocket.html: For generations the local sluagh carried condemned buildings and the debris of crumbling architecture here: a diner, a gas station, houses, a gazebo, a boxcar, a bridge truss, a church spire, cemetery angels. The Pocket was once a place shared by the sluagh and the Nosferatu. Since Parovich went over to the Sabbat the door has been shut. Ivory is the last changeling who looks after it.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Take nothing away. The Pocket takes, and does not give back.

gz-pocket.brief: The Michigan Pocket: a cave that cannot exist, a vast vault of dark stone under the bed of Lake Michigan, full of buildings the city decided to forget.

kd-gracis.name: Kilbourntown
kd-gracis.html: His villa, the north-side Mafia contacts and the right to feed in the Avenue bars are his by long custom.
kd-gracis.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-gracis.brief: Kilbourntown: the old west-bank town Gracis ruled before the cities merged, and still treats as his.

kd-lucina.name: The Theatre District
kd-lucina.html: Hers by right of taste and by Gracis's indulgence. Louis Detonas has the run of the galleries on her sufferance.
kd-lucina.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-lucina.brief: The Theatre District: the Performing Arts Center, the Pabst Theater, the Auditorium and the Hyatt. Lucina's domain; feed here only with her leave.

kd-louis.name: East Town galleries
kd-louis.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-louis.brief: East Town galleries: a few blocks of galleries, studios and expensive apartments around Louis Detonas's own. Toreador neonates come here to be noticed.

kd-jason.name: Walker’s Point
kd-jason.html: Embarrassingly for the Council's swing vote, the Sabbat ran its invasion from a church in his streets.
kd-jason.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

notes.title: Still here
notes.html: The last Sabbat pack still hides in a cistern beneath his streets.

kd-hrothulf.name: Hrothulf’s Outlands acre
kd-hrothulf.html: Nobody has ever contested it, and the Lupine avoid it for reasons of their own.
kd-hrothulf.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-hrothulf.brief: Hrothulf's house and the cleared yards around it, deep in the Outlands.

kd-chapel.name: The Chapel grounds
kd-chapel.html: Since Victor's death Newman has extended the wards a block in every direction, and the neighbours have started sleeping badly.
kd-chapel.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-chapel.brief: The Highland Boulevard blocks around the Chapel, the Tremere chantry. Do not hunt here.

kd-mortius.name: The haunted block
kd-mortius.html: Its wards fail on the eastern side, where the null zone begins.
kd-mortius.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-mortius.brief: Dr. Mortius's own house at the edge of the null zone, which mortals swear is haunted.

kd-jade.name: Jade’s tower
kd-jade.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-jade.brief: The Brujah Primogen's official domain: her tower on East Michigan Street and the blocks around it, granted by the Council with a show of reluctance.

kd-jade2.name: Jade’s reserve haven
kd-jade2.html: Decker has let it stand. He has not said why.
kd-jade2.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-jade2.brief: Macy Carver's street in Wauwatosa, technically inside the Anubi patrol zone.

notes.title: Jade’s real haven
notes.html: The Brujah Primogen sleeps here.

kd-scott.name: The Black Prince’s lakeshore (vacant)
kd-scott.html: Jade could claim it as Brujah Primogen; she has not. Turk's Union is quietly moving in.
kd-scott.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-scott.brief: The Black Prince's lakeshore: Sir Edward Scott's domain on the Lower East Side, vacant since his death.

kd-parovich.name: Parovich’s Concordia (vacant)
kd-parovich.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-parovich.brief: Concordia: the decaying mansion blocks of the Nosferatu traitor Parovich, vacant since his exposure. Mother Agatha claims the streets for the Warrens and nobody argues, because nobody wants to go there.

kd-merik.name: The Prince’s block (sealed)
kd-merik.html: Every Council member pretends not to want it.
kd-merik.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-merik.brief: The late Prince's block, sealed. Nobody holds the Prince's domain, which used to be the whole city.

kd-gunther.name: The river above the dam
kd-gunther.html: Nobody has had the nerve to ask whether the grant died with Merik.
kd-gunther.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-gunther.brief: The banks and the pond above the North Avenue dam: Gunther's domain since the 1930s, by Merik's grant.

kd-soraya.name: The folded blocks
kd-soraya.html: The Council has never formally granted them, because the Council has never formally noticed them.
kd-soraya.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-soraya.alias: A few strange blocks on Yankee Hill
kd-soraya.brief: A few blocks on Yankee Hill that are slightly further away than they should be.

kd-ethan.name: Ethan’s firing lanes
kd-ethan.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-ethan.brief: The valley rooftops Ethan Stone can cover from his grain elevator, inside Blood Brother turf.

kd-decker.name: The Good Hope motel strip
kd-decker.html: Decker keeps no real haven. His people eat at the all-night diners and listen to the police scanner.
kd-decker.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-decker.brief: The Good Hope motel strip: the motels and diners along Good Hope Road are Anubi ground by any measure.

kd-turk.name: Turk’s riverboat & the War Memorial
kd-turk.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-turk.brief: The Veterans Park shore and the Art Museum steps: the heart of Union turf and Turk's own ground.

kd-agatha.name: The Warrens
kd-agatha.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-agatha.brief: The Warrens: everything from the Grand Warrens to the harbour lock is Nosferatu ground, by a right older than the Council. Mother Agatha governs it.

kd-steam.name: The Council’s steam tunnels
kd-steam.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-steam.brief: The service tunnels between MECCA, the Hyatt and the government buildings, held for the Council. Gracis's ghouls guard them.

notes.title: The prisoner
notes.html: Akawa is held somewhere inside.

kd-castor.name: Castor’s flesh tunnels
kd-castor.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-castor.brief: Castor's flesh tunnels. The Tzimisce claim nothing on paper. In practice nobody else walks here.

kd-blackwater.name: The Black Water cistern
kd-blackwater.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.
kd-blackwater.brief: The Black Water cistern, the last Sabbat lair in the city, right under Jason's domain.

l-goodhope.name: Good Hope Road patrol
l-goodhope.html: Anarchs dare each other to drive its length. "Done Good Hope" five times and you are an Ace.
l-goodhope.brief: Good Hope Road: the northern edge of Kindred territory and a favourite Anubi patrol route. Country clubs along it make perfect Lupine ambush cover.

l-harbor.name: North Harbor Drive patrol
l-harbor.html: He suspects Lupines are swimming the lake and slipping through the shore parks.
l-harbor.alias: A new Anubi patrol on the lakefront
l-harbor.brief: North Harbor Drive. Decker has recently stretched his patrols down to the lakefront here.

notes.title: Why
notes.html: Lupines have been using the lakefront to meet the Union.

l-lakeN.name: Lakefront parks: northern Lupine run
l-lakeN.brief: The chain of lakeshore parks runs far to the north. The Werewolves have used it as cover to reach the heart of the city, sometimes swimming the lake first.

l-lakeS.name: Lakefront parks: southern Lupine run
l-lakeS.brief: South Shore, Sheridan and Grant parks give the Lupine a wooded corridor from the southern Outlands nearly to Bay View.

l-i94s.name: I-94 to Chicago (Lupine-watched)
l-i94s.html: Sensible Kindred arrange a sealed daylight truck, or fly.
l-i94s.src: Milwaukee by Night, Traveling to Milwaukee, p. 8
l-i94s.brief: I-94 to Chicago: one of three highways into town, and all are said to be watched by the Lupine. Only the desperate drive them at night.

l-i43n.name: I-43 north / Route 43 (Lupine-watched)
l-i43n.html: This autumn a Kindred car was shot to pieces on Route 43 by the Mouse pack.
l-i43n.src: Milwaukee by Night, p. 8; A Midnight Moon
l-i43n.brief: I-43 north and Route 43: the northern highway out of town, watched by the Lupine.

notes.title: On whose orders
notes.html: Merik told the Mouse pack which car to expect.

l-i894.name: I-894 bypass (Lupine-watched)
l-i894.brief: The I-894 bypass, the third major road out of town. Its south-western run crosses deep into Lupine country.

l-skywalk.name: The sky-walk
l-skywalk.brief: The sky-walk: catwalks linking the Hyatt Regency, MECCA, the Arena, the Auditorium and the Reuss Federal Plaza. An Elder can cross the whole complex without touching the street or seeing it.

l-bridgewar.name: Bridge War line (1840s)
l-bridgewar.html: In 1845 Gracis staged a riot and the bridges were destroyed.
l-bridgewar.brief: The Bridge War line at the Chestnut Street crossing. In the 1840s Gracis and Hrothulf fought their war through mortal pawns, who thought the quarrel was about who paid for the river bridges.

l-ritual.name: The ring of the four anchors
l-ritual.html: The far anchors, west and north, stand about twice as far out as their partners, the proportion the Chapel's geometry calls a "lever". When all four are tuned, their fields close over Marquette.
l-ritual.brief: The ring of the four anchors: four antennae on the city's edges, aimed at the null zone. Their diagonals cross over St. Joan of Arc Chapel.

l-ritual2.name: The ring of the four anchors · north–south axis
l-ritual2.brief: The second diagonal of the Chapel's ritual, from the Hotel Warszawa through the chapel to the Lincoln Creek mast.

l-chase.name: The dragon’s chase
l-chase.html: The chase began at the Cudahy warehouses.
l-chase.brief: The dragon's chase: the path of the "Milwaukee Dragon" over Bay View, where the news cameras caught it, to the fish plant where Jade Riley killed it.

tr-white.name: The White Flag Crossing

facts.v: Cross with a small white cloth openly displayed and name someone on the far bank you mean to meet peacefully.
About twenty minutes, usually.

The Tollman can dispute who counts as a resident of either bank. The road reads intention, not justice: an armed traveller with a peaceful purpose may pass, and someone hiding a planned attack is refused.
A failed crossing returns you to your starting bank.

tr-white.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, p. 22. Entry customs negotiate with a particular road; performing one does not give anyone access to the Dreaming.
tr-white.brief: The White Flag Crossing: from the Counterweight to the eastern downtown echoes, about twenty minutes. Cross with a small white cloth openly displayed and name someone on the far bank you mean to meet peacefully.
tr-white.html: A remnant of the Bridge War and the most reliable cross-river trod. It lets an armed traveller pass who has declared a peaceful purpose, and turns back anyone hiding a planned attack. A failed crossing returns you to the bank you started from.

tr-borrow.name: The Borrower’s Stair

facts.v: In the dreaming basement stacks, return an unfinished work of your own to the shelf where it belongs and state the question that stopped you. A ladder descends from above, although you are underground.
Ten minutes to the reception desk; unpredictable beyond.
Follow a shelf because it holds the answer you want rather than the work you borrowed, and companions split into separate lines of inquiry. Agree on a meeting question first.
Mrs. Quire keeps a return slip for every admitted visitor and wants a better explanation each time she has to fetch one.

tr-borrow.sub: Ten minutes to the reception desk; unpredictable beyond.
tr-borrow.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, p. 22. Entry customs negotiate with a particular road; performing one does not give anyone access to the Dreaming.
tr-borrow.brief: The Borrower's Stair: from the Central Library's dreaming vestibule to the Unfinished Index. Offer unfinished work and its honest question. Ten minutes to the reception desk; unpredictable beyond.

tr-unbuilt.name: The Unbuilt Stair

facts.v: Climb a staircase while describing a specific thing you intend to build, teach or repair.
About half an hour.
Declare grander plans than you really intend and doors to much larger responsibilities open for you.
Return down the same stair carrying a tangible record of a small step already completed. This is why Kit carries so many receipts.

tr-unbuilt.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, p. 22. Entry customs negotiate with a particular road; performing one does not give anyone access to the Dreaming.
tr-unbuilt.brief: The Unbuilt Stair: from the old Pabst site to the Crownless Ward, about half an hour. Climb while describing something specific you intend to build, teach or repair.
tr-unbuilt.html: Declaring grander plans than you mean attracts doors to much larger responsibilities. The safe return is by the same stair, carrying a record of a small step already completed, which is why Kit carries so many receipts.

tr-lantern.name: The Lantern Wake

facts.v: Carry a properly kindled scale-light lantern in an enchanted vessel, with a chart from Ruth or the Ashen Usher.
One long night, even when the mountain looks close.
Follow the lantern’s reflection, not the star you most want to reach. A wind that blows the wake ahead of the bow is the clear warning to turn back.
Keep one full charge for the way home. Bjorn has the only known working lantern.

tr-lantern.sub: One long night, even when the mountain looks close.
tr-lantern.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, pp. 16, 22–23. Entry customs negotiate with a particular road; performing one does not give anyone access to the Dreaming.
tr-lantern.brief: The Lantern Wake: one long night across the lake to the Far Guest's Seat, in an enchanted boat carrying a kindled scale-light lantern, with a chart from Ruth or the Ashen Usher.
tr-lantern.html: Follow the lantern's reflection, not the star you most want to reach. If the wind blows the wake ahead of the bow, turn back. Keep one full charge for the way home.

tr-line.name: The Third Shift Line

facts.v: Leon’s consent, and a ticket punched with the date you expect to return.
Planned at fifteen minutes. Currently unsafe for passengers.
The Glass shard recognises old wartime destinations as unserved stops. The fix is to replace it with an honest mechanism, not to learn to exploit it.
If restored, one short reliable municipal route; the repaired Bell can call a ticketed passenger back.

tr-line.sub: Planned at fifteen minutes. Currently unsafe for passengers.
tr-line.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, pp. 8, 23. Entry customs negotiate with a particular road; performing one does not give anyone access to the Dreaming.
tr-line.brief: The Third Shift Line: Leon's surviving section of dream-rail from his workshop, eventually to the Counterweight. Planned at fifteen minutes; currently unsafe for passengers.

tr-candle.name: The Low Candle Way

facts.v: Ivory’s invitation, and the correct physical approach through the warrens.
Short, when she opens it.
Being seen at its mortal entrance can expose your movements to Nosferatu observation, though that gives no access to the freehold. The outer court has no sign of anything beyond it.
Only as Ivory permits.

tr-candle.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, p. 23. Entry customs negotiate with a particular road; performing one does not give anyone access to the Dreaming.
tr-candle.brief: The Low Candle Way: the old sluagh approach beneath the city to the outer court of the Gloaming Keep. Short, when Ivory opens it.
tr-candle.html: Being seen at its mortal entrance can expose someone's movements to the Nosferatu. It does not give anyone a way into the Keep.

tr-platform.name: To the Waiting Platform

facts.v: An actual invitation from a named destination outside Milwaukee.
The platform is reachable; onward service is not dependable.
The timetable shows persuasive departures that cannot carry a living traveller home.
Walk back up into the Ward. Ordinary buses and trains still leave town in daylight.

tr-platform.sub: The platform is reachable; onward service is not dependable.
tr-platform.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, p. 23. Entry customs negotiate with a particular road; performing one does not give anyone access to the Dreaming.
tr-platform.brief: From the outer Crownless Ward to the Waiting Platform.

tr-chicago.name: The old Chicago road

facts.v: None that works.
Every departing train carries the name of someone who abandoned Milwaukee.
It ends at the Waiting Platform. Reopening one trustworthy outward trod is Ruth’s project.

tr-chicago.sub: Every departing train carries the name of someone who abandoned Milwaukee.
tr-chicago.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, p. 9. Entry customs negotiate with a particular road; performing one does not give anyone access to the Dreaming.
tr-chicago.brief: The old Chicago road. It now ends at a station where every departing train carries the name of someone who abandoned Milwaukee.

tr-depart.name: The Far Guest’s road

facts.v: None.
The route the dragon used to leave Earth.
Severed. It cannot currently be followed, and it isn’t this chronicle’s inevitable destination.

tr-depart.sub: The route the dragon used to leave Earth.
tr-depart.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, p. 17. Entry customs negotiate with a particular road; performing one does not give anyone access to the Dreaming.
tr-depart.brief: The Far Guest's road, the way the dragon left. Severed.

facts.v: The Hierarchy’s procession route from the Citadel to the registry at Forest Home, following the line of old funeral corteges. Legionnaires keep it lit with corpse-candles.
Renegades ambush prisoner details where the road crosses the valley.
The Grim Legion’s marching road along Wisconsin Avenue and Bluemound. The Ninth Watch patrols the eastern half.
Dawn wind through the Marquette anomaly can blow travellers off the road and into strange Shroud weather.
The relic Milwaukee Road line south to the Chicago Necropolis. Sealed cars, Harbinger escorts, departures on the hour of a death.
Stowaways are Reaped on arrival in Chicago.
The drowned excursion steamer runs as a ferry across the Sea of Shadows toward Chicago. Centurion Dolan won’t take a passenger who can’t name someone waiting for them on the far shore.
Maelstrom weather. Spectres follow her wake, and some nights her own dead forget they are crew.
The Renegades’ route from Bay View into downtown along Kinnickinnic and the river, the way the strikers marched.
Hierarchy patrols watch the bridges, and the Newhall end is Spectre country.
A path of relic stairs and alleys from Walnut Street down to the lake that only the free wraiths keep. Lorraine’s people use it to reach the newly dead before the Reapers.
Where it crosses the Freeway the Hollow pulls at anyone who looks down.
A Tempest byway from the Interchange Hollow under the river and out beneath the lake. Smugglers use it to move what the Usurers won’t list.
Spectres. The Labyrinth lies somewhere below.
In hard winters the Sea of Shadows freezes along a line toward the Far Shores. Walkers who reach the end do not come back to say what is there.
It only exists while the living lake is frozen. Thaw while you are on it and you go into the Tempest.

up-cm.name: Moon bridge: Grinning Stone to the Granary
up-cm.html: On the night the Granary was defiled the span snapped in the middle, and now it hangs in the sky in two flickering stumps. Mercer can’t raise it alone, and Horatio’s Red Talons aren’t sure they want a bridge into the human city at all.
up-cm.brief: The last open moon bridge in the city, until this autumn. Horatio and Rosa kept it open as a courtesy, and they were the only two leaders who still talked.

up-em.name: Moon bridge: Bleeding Pine to the Granary
up-em.html: The span still hangs half-built in the sky, flickering.
up-em.brief: Broken in the 1930s, when Merik used Erica’s friendship with the Mouse to set them against the Eagle.

up-ce.name: The bridge that was never built
up-ce.html: Since both clans started fighting Banes in the same forest, the ghost glows a little brighter.
up-ce.brief: Coyote and Eagle have never opened a moon bridge between their caerns. The Lunes keep a ghost-span in the sky anyway, out of hope or mockery.

up-hh.name: The cold bridge to the Hill
up-hh.brief: A dead moon bridge to the sealed caern on Holy Hill. It would light up if the caern were reopened.

up-chi.name: The Chicago bridge
up-chi.html: The Glass Walkers of Chicago still don’t know the Mouse are gone.
up-chi.brief: Once the Mouse ran a moon bridge south to the Chicago caerns. The Weaver’s airport spindle cut it in the 1950s, and the Pattern Spiders have kept it cut.

up-usla.name: Usla’s Last Crawl
up-usla.html: Follow it and you feel his shame and his exhaustion. At the end Greatwater is waiting.
up-usla.brief: The track of the dying Usla from the buried relics to the lake, still glowing faintly in the Penumbra three centuries later.

up-fog.name: The Fog Road
up-fog.brief: When the Grey Coming rolls in, fog-spirits walk up the river from the harbor to the North Avenue dam, carrying Greatwater’s whispers into the heart of the city.

up-smelt.name: The Smelt Run
up-smelt.html: Their spirit is a silver road that small spirits ride north and south. In autumn it is only a faint shimmer.
up-smelt.brief: Every spring the smelt run along the shore by night, and the whole lakefront crowds with lanterns and nets.

up-decay.name: Riding the Winds of Decay
up-decay.html: Spirits see a vampire in wolf-shape running beside the packs, and they don’t know what to call it. Decker drinks Lupine Vitae in secret. The spirits have noticed even if the Garou haven’t.
up-decay.brief: The run the book’s Gangrel make when the full moon pulls them out to hunt with the wolves.

up-raid.name: The Eagle raid-road
up-raid.brief: The weekly route of the Eagle raids: east to the lake, north up the shore under the Lake Breeze, and into the city through the parks, just as the book says Lupines do.

up-iron.name: The Iron Horse’s road
up-iron.html: Now the Horse runs it every night, looking for Akawa.
up-iron.brief: The chrome pack’s favourite run: down Juneau Avenue to the Crucible, where the Blood Brothers drink.

gt-deep-mke.name: Deep Tunnel · Milwaukee branch
gt-deep-mke.html: Workers have seen tracks that were "too big" and abandoned one of the side drifts.
gt-deep-mke.src: The MMSD Deep Tunnel is real (built 1986–1993); the rest is improvised.
gt-deep-mke.brief: The Deep Tunnel, Milwaukee branch: an enormous storage tunnel under the river bed, under construction since 1986, three hundred feet down in the dolomite.

gt-deep-men.name: Deep Tunnel · Menomonee branch
gt-deep-men.html: Halfway along is the abandoned drift where the vozhd sleeps.
gt-deep-men.src: The MMSD Deep Tunnel is real (built 1986–1993); the rest is improvised.
gt-deep-men.brief: The western branch of the Deep Tunnel under the Menomonee Valley.

gt-deep-kk.name: Deep Tunnel · Kinnickinnic branch
gt-deep-kk.html: Its end breaks into the culverts where Drake hides.
gt-deep-kk.src: The MMSD Deep Tunnel is real (built 1986–1993); the rest is improvised.
gt-deep-kk.brief: The southern branch of the Deep Tunnel under the concrete Kinnickinnic.

gt-wis.name: The Wisconsin Avenue trunk sewer
gt-wis.brief: The Wisconsin Avenue trunk sewer: the main brick artery under the avenue. The Nosferatu call it the Spine.

gt-river.name: The riverbank interceptor
gt-river.brief: The riverbank interceptor along the west bank, from the North Avenue dam through the Grand Warrens to the Third Ward.

gt-valley.name: The valley interceptor
gt-valley.html: The eastern half is still passable; the western half belongs to the creatures.
gt-valley.brief: The valley interceptor under the Menomonee Valley.

gt-north.name: The North Avenue sewer
gt-north.brief: The old North Avenue sewer. Quiet, and nearly empty.

gt-kk.name: The Kinnickinnic Avenue sewer
gt-kk.brief: The Kinnickinnic Avenue sewer, south under Bay View.

gt-steam1.name: Steam passage · MECCA to the Hyatt
gt-steam1.brief: The Elders' steam passage between MECCA and the Hyatt.

gt-steam2.name: Steam passage · to City Hall
gt-steam2.brief: A service passage to the basements of City Hall and the Pfister.

gt-chestnut.name: The Chestnut Street cellars
gt-chestnut.brief: The Chestnut Street cellars under the Pabst brewery hill.

gt-parovich.name: Parovich’s old passage
gt-parovich.html: At the western end the bricks have been broken out from inside.
gt-parovich.brief: Parovich's private passage from the Warrens to his mansion, bricked up at both ends.

gt-harbor.name: The passage to the lock
gt-harbor.brief: A Nosferatu passage from the Grand Warrens to the old lock on the harbour shore.

gt-pocket.name: The way under the lake
gt-pocket.html: It ends at the Michigan Pocket's Undersea Door. Closed since Parovich went over to the Sabbat.
gt-pocket.brief: A stone passage on no engineer's drawings, sloping from the harbour lock down under the lake bed.

gt-wide.name: Dragos’s wide tunnel
gt-wide.html: Its southern mouth is hidden only by a warehouse wall.
gt-wide.aliasText: The Sabbat dug a tunnel big enough for a truck from Cudahy to somewhere under the valley.
gt-wide.brief: Dragos's wide tunnel: a tunnel a truck wide, dug (or grown) by the Sabbat's creatures from the Cudahy warehouses to the workshops under the valley.

merik.name: Terence Merik
merik.html:
Born in Kent in 1645, an earl Embraced by a nameless countess at Christmas 1683, he "died" in 1750 when the county began to wonder why he never aged. In the Civil War he met Erica, a Gangrel nursing Union soldiers on his plantation, Blood Bound her and brought her north. Her friends among the Lupine let him run liquor in the 1920s; liquor brought the Mafia, and the Mafia brought the throne.

He kept the peace by keeping the Anarchs leaderless: the dangerous ones always left town. He owned the mayor's office, the police commissioner and several precinct captains, and he read the Milwaukee Journal a day early. In his last weeks he appointed a handful of neonates as "the Mask" to protect the Masquerade and hunt the killer. The Mask destroyed him in his burning house, and they say he was the killer they had been sent to find.
merik.aliasText: The Prince is dead. Everyone says so, and no two people tell you how in the same way.
merik.brief:
Terence Merik, Ventrue, ruled Milwaukee from 1930 until this October. He took the city from Lyle Rickson on Canadian liquor money and Mafia muscle, and under him the Lupine raids grew fewer and weaker. People credit his Gangrel wife for that: she knew the packs.

He died this autumn, when his house on the hill above the Menomonee burned. The Council says a rogue Kindred had been leaving drained bodies for the newspapers and that the Prince fell while the matter was being settled. The throne is empty and the city is choosing a successor.

notes.title: Erica
notes.html: A month before the end he waited too long to feed, frenzied on his way home from a film, drained a couple on a park bench in Juneau Park and then killed Erica when she tried to stop him. He could not confess without inviting revolt, so he hid her body, and his mind split: one half ordered the hunt, the other kept killing.

notes.title: The Union was his
notes.html: For five years he had been bringing the East Side Anarchs Union under Domination and Blood Bonding its key figures. He sent them to kill the Mask with the Blood Brothers.

notes.title: He sold the Mask to the Lupine
notes.html: He told the Mouse pack exactly which car the Mask would be driving out on Route 43. The Justicar who should have come to judge the murders had already died in that same Lupine cave.

gracis.name: Gracis Nostinus
gracis.html:
A Roman Embraced by the general Marius in 412, he has hunted his blood-brother Hrothulf for fifteen hundred years to avenge their sire and, in his own mind, Rome. He was Prince of Kilbourntown in the 1830s and started the 1845 riot that brought the bridges down.

In Council he can usually count on Lucina and Carna, enough to force a three-to-three stalemate on anything. Mafia money pays for his bribes and for mortal hitmen whose job is to frighten rivals rather than kill them; his spies log every arrival at Mitchell Field. The other clans respect him and will not crown him: they know his interest is not the city but his vendetta.
gracis.aliasText: There is a little Roman on the Council who counts the votes before anyone else has finished speaking.
gracis.brief:
Gracis Nostinus, Ventrue, is the most powerful voice on the Council of Elders and the nearest thing it has to a chairman. He is soft, pink and barely five feet tall, dresses in stylish clothes a size too large, speaks through his nose and wipes his hands after every handshake.

He feeds Raoul and the armed guards who keep Anarchs out of MECCA, and he lives in a fine old house on the river north of downtown. Everyone knows two things about him: he wants the throne, and he hates Hrothulf.

notes.title: The seventh seat
notes.html: He backed Parovich's proposal to restore the Council's seventh seat for a second Ventrue and never saw that it was the Sabbat's plan to break the Council. Since Parovich's exposure he has been asking himself who else on the Council had the same idea.

notes.title: The detectives
notes.html: He meant to take the police detectives away from Parovich once the seat was won. With Parovich gone the detective bureau's Kindred leash is lying loose, and he is reaching for it before Lucina notices.

notes.title: He is afraid of Decker
notes.html: Of everyone in the city, the one he fears is Mark Decker. Decker's Anubi could seal the roads or walk into MECCA, and nothing Gracis owns could stop them.

notes.title: Playing him
notes.html: Hunch your shoulders, talk through your nose, keep a handkerchief to wipe your fingers. Fussy, precise, a little foolish on the surface.

hrothulf.name: Hrothulf
hrothulf.sub: Former Prince, recluse of the Outlands
hrothulf.html:
A Dane from 5th-century Britain, Embraced by Marius in 380 and kept as a Blood Bound slave for half a century. He came to the New World early, was Prince of Juneautown when Solomon Juneau founded it, and fought Gracis through the Bridge War until a Nosferatu Justicar forced a truce. As Prince again from 1906 he created the Council of Elders; he resigned in 1923, after a European assassin nearly killed him, rather than give Gracis a throne to aim at.

He controls the city's fire department. Years ago Gracis's men set his haven alight and the trucks took two hours to arrive; he has owned the brigade ever since. He does not want the throne, but if Gracis attacks him openly he will take it for as long as it takes to restore order. The Anarchs have no quarrel with him.
hrothulf.aliasText: They say the oldest Kindred in the city lives in a plain house out past the patrols, and that even the Lupine leave it alone.
hrothulf.brief:
Hrothulf is the oldest Ventrue in Milwaukee and has twice been its Prince. He is a huge man who looks barely twenty-five, with long unkempt blond hair, a deep scar from a Roman blade, poor grammar and a habit of mumbling in a language nobody else speaks. He rarely raises his voice; he rarely needs to.

He keeps out of Ventrue politics and lives alone in a suburban house beyond the Anubi line. He holds a season box at County Stadium. He and Gracis have been at war for longer than the city has existed.

notes.title: He drank his sire
notes.html: When he killed Marius he did not stop at killing. Hrothulf is a diablerist, and Gracis has never stopped saying so.

notes.title: Petre Dubois
notes.html: In 1674 he came through as a scout called Petre Dubois with Père Marquette's party, married into the Chippewa and Embraced his wife Chiclena. Her war against the Menominee brought the outcast Lupine Usla here. The siege of Milwaukee began with Hrothulf's marriage, and he knows it.

notes.title: The last resort
notes.html: If he is ever truly cornered he could make every hose in the city fail and let Milwaukee burn. He would probably not do it. Probably.

notes.title: Carna protects him
notes.html: The Tremere seat secretly favours him and has shielded him more than once.

notes.title: Playing him
notes.html: Speak quietly, as if shy. Bad grammar, the odd foreign word. Never get angry at insults: your size does the talking.

lucina.name: Lucina
lucina.html:
A Missouri farmer's daughter born in 1863 who danced at St. Louis socials. At sixteen a beautiful boy took her for six months, then left a note on the pillow: she would never be great, and he left her to her mediocrity for eternity. Her family drove her off with a shotgun. She still dances, and she has spent a century trying to prove him wrong.

She believes art can tame the Beast and wants to make the Toreador worthy of what they claim to love, which makes her a kill-joy and earns her respect. She fought Sir Edward Scott in Council on reflex, and she is working to take over the police administration so she can crush the street gangs. Several peace talks with Akawa at West Milwaukee Park came to nothing.
lucina.aliasText: The Toreador on the Council looks sixteen. People who treated her as sixteen are not on the Council.
lucina.brief:
Lucina leads the city's Toreador and sits on the Council. She looks like a girl of sixteen, red hair to her shoulders, dark brown eyes, always in the finest gown she can find. She is sweet and demure until someone argues with her on a point that matters, and then she is not.

She keeps a permanent suite on the 16th floor of the Hyatt Regency. Her ghouls guard the museums and concert halls against the Anarchs, whom she hates as a matter of principle. In Council she usually votes with Gracis.

notes.title: Scott loved her
notes.html: The Black Prince was in love with her, or something close to it, and an old Malkavian kept feeding the feeling. She never knew, or never let herself know.

notes.title: A kindly old gentleman
notes.html: A fatherly old Kindred has been advising her not to tolerate insults. She does not know that he is mad, or what else he is.

notes.title: Parovich’s friend
notes.html: She was Parovich’s ally in Council and supported his seventh seat. Since his exposure she has been very quiet about that.

scott.name: Sir Edward Scott
scott.html:
A Cornish knight born in 1399 and Embraced in 1432 by Sir Lorence, who killed his wife and son before his eyes. He spent five centuries protecting the young from the old. He saved Akawa from a blood hunt more than once and brawled with him in the dueling grounds just as often; Kindred laid bets on their bouts, and nobody ever collected. Decker was his friend.

He opposed giving the empty seventh seat to anyone but the Gangrel it was made for, and he would have preferred Hrothulf back on the throne. He kept a small, elegant flat on the east side near the lake, in the middle of Union turf, where the Anarchs still leave bottles and flowers by the door.
scott.aliasText: The Anarchs still drink to a dead Elder they called “the Prince”, just to annoy the living ones.
scott.brief:
Sir Edward Scott, "the Black Prince of Cornwall", was the Brujah Elder on the Council and the Anarchs' voice in it. He came to sessions in a bathrobe, a leather jacket or a bikini, mocked everyone including himself, and challenged Councillors to duels that none of them ever accepted.

He was destroyed in the chaos of the Sabbat invasion this autumn. Accounts of how differ, and no two agree. His seat now belongs to Jade Riley.

notes.title: He was Akawa’s sire
notes.html: In 1770, fleeing settlers who had caught him feeding, he Embraced a young Plains warrior and left him the next night. He never remembered. Akawa did.

jason.name: Jason
jason.html:
He was hanged in 1903 for killing a woman for the five dollars in her purse because a man called Talbot told him to, and was Embraced in his cell the night before. He is on the Council because he is the only Malkavian who would sit on it.

He holds the balance of power between Gracis and the Brujah, and both sides court him. He always voted against Parovich because he disliked the colour of his aura, and he was the only Elder who said so before the invasion. He feels responsible for the city's other Malkavians. He is trying to keep the police out of every Kindred's hands, his own included, and he is watching Jade Riley closely.
jason.aliasText: One of the Councillors is so forgettable that people forget he is on the Council.
jason.brief:
Jason holds the Malkavian seat on the Council. He is a short, quiet man in clothes twenty years out of date who keeps checking a pocket watch as if he were late for something. He rarely speaks; when he does, it tends to be the wisest thing said all night.

Any Kindred may bring him a question or a request about Council business, and he listens to all of them. He lives in a luxurious penthouse hidden inside a shabby tenement in Walker's Point.

notes.title: His sire
notes.html: His sire is Jacob. Jason serves both Jacob and Esau, and both of them tell him what to do.

notes.title: The frame
notes.html: The Sabbat meant to kill Parovich once he had broken the Council and make it look like Jason had done it.

parovich.name: Parovich
parovich.sub: Former Nosferatu Primogen, exposed Sabbat agent (destroyed)
parovich.html:
A Russian Embraced in 1467, in the city for ninety years. He was in New York when the Sabbat took it, decided they would win everywhere eventually, and joined the Black Hand. In Milwaukee he owned the police detectives, set Elders and Anarchs at each other's throats, pushed for a seventh Council seat so that Hrothulf and Gracis would sit at the same table and tear it apart, and searched the Anubi for someone weak enough to betray Decker.

He told the Council his runaway childer were dangerous psychotics to be killed on sight. He had already killed two of them himself.

notes.title: He is not gone
notes.html: Parovich was not destroyed. Dragos melted him into a Tzimisce war-ghoul, a vozhd, as punishment and as a spare brain. It hides in the Deep Tunnel drifts under the city, and one of the faces in its flank is his. He remembers every secret of the Warrens.

notes.title: The clan was watching
notes.html: The Nosferatu elders outside Milwaukee had already grown suspicious of him and sent spies to watch him before the invasion.

parovich.aliasText: The old Nosferatu on the Council turned out to be working for the Sabbat. Nobody on the Council likes to talk about how long it took them to notice.
parovich.brief:
Parovich sat on the Council for the Nosferatu for most of a century: enormous, kindly, drenched in a sickly sweet perfume to hide the stench, with a forked tongue. During the Sabbat invasion this autumn he was exposed as the Sabbat's agent inside the Council and destroyed.

His mansion in the Barrens has been searched and boarded up. Mother Agatha now speaks for the Nosferatu.

carna.name: Carna
carna.html:
A peasant girl Embraced in 1435 by a prince who made her as revenge on his own masters: the first woman in the Tremere tanks. She was once Prince of Marseille. Since 1903 only trusted elders and ancillae of her clan have been allowed in Milwaukee, and they are here for the Marquette anomaly, not politics.

She openly supports Gracis but votes for and against him to keep everything exactly as it is: if he wins he will leave her behind, and if he loses he cannot protect her. Officially she heads the city's Tremere. In practice she took her orders from Victor, who relayed what Dr. Mortius needed. Since Victor's death this autumn the Chapel works without Vienna's direct oversight.
carna.aliasText: The Tremere on the Council flirts like a debutante. People who know her avoid being flirted with.
carna.brief:
Carna represents the Tremere on the Council. She looks eighteen, with straight blond hair that hides half her face, and wears long dresses from eras nobody can place. She is flirtatious and seems perpetually tired, and those who know her treat her as a shark.

Her favourite haven is at the Hyatt. The Tremere keep a chantry, the Chapel, in an old brewer's mansion on Highland Boulevard, and no Tremere comes to Milwaukee without Vienna's leave.

notes.title: Her lovers
notes.html: She clings to her lovers until they want to leave, and then she kills them with a ritual of her own invention, the Curse of Clytaemnestra. She is coming unhinged.

notes.title: Hrothulf
notes.html: She secretly favours Hrothulf and has protected him more than once. When Hrothulf dies, Gracis will leave the city, and her power base goes with him.

notes.title: Doubts
notes.html: She has begun to question what the Tremere have done over the centuries. In her clan that is not a healthy thought.

notes.title: Playing her
notes.html: Very flirtatious with men, while planning how to dominate them. When it comes to a real confrontation, be as cold as you were sweet.

victor.name: Victor
victor.html:
A CIA assassin who was sent in 1950 to kill a Greek noble and was Embraced by him instead. Vienna sent him to Milwaukee to watch its own people: Carna took her orders from him, and he passed on what Dr. Mortius needed.

He was killed in his own laboratory by Drake, a Lupine of the Mouse pack corrupted by the Wyrm, who walked through the Chapel's wards as if they were not there. His havens were hidden in the city's richest districts; the Chapel cleaned out most of them.
victor.aliasText: A Tremere with a scar who never smiled died inside the Chapel this autumn. The Tremere are not discussing it.
victor.brief: Victor was a Tremere with a deep scar across his right cheek who wore loose black clothes like a karate gi and moved like a tiger. He never smiled and always seemed about to kill somebody. He was destroyed this autumn inside the Chapel, the Tremere chantry on Highland Boulevard.

notes.title: His real orders
notes.html: Vienna feared that whatever lies under the null zone might be strong enough to break a Blood Bond. Victor was to kill any Kindred who tried to control it, or perhaps take it himself.

notes.title: Who opened the door
notes.html: The wards were weakened from inside. Jesselin of House Goratrix found a way in through Haberman’s correspondence and gave Drake the key.

mortius.name: Dr. Mortius
mortius.html:
A 16th-century sorcerer whose rediscovery of magic as a mortal earned him the Embrace in 1566. His mentor is a clan Elder, and Carna is under orders to accommodate him. He studies the null zone at Marquette; his ghoul retainers are skilled fighters who die often defending him from the Lupine.

Very few Kindred know he is in the city at all. Before the invasion only Decker and Parovich did.
mortius.aliasText: There is a house near Marquette that mortals swear is haunted. Kindred who ask about it are told to stop asking.
mortius.brief:
Dr. Mortius is a Tremere scholar: a stooped, bearded old man with a hunchback and mottled skin, Embraced in his twilight years. He avoids other Kindred and their eyes, seems to drift off while you talk, and loves to show visitors magical gadgets that technology overtook long ago.

He lives in a house near Marquette that mortals believe is haunted, and he does not like to be disturbed.

notes.title: His dowsers
notes.html: He uses the witches of the Church of Isis to search the city for him without risking himself. The rest of the Tremere would be appalled. Kayla is his eyes inside the Brujah.

notes.title: The ritual
notes.html: The four antenna anchors around the city are his. With Victor dead nobody in Vienna checks his work.

notes.title: A forbidden ritual
notes.html: His house is protected by Haunted House, a ritual the Tremere banned as a danger to the Masquerade. He learned it before the ban.

louis.name: Louis Detonas
louis.html:
The son of French nobles who supported the Revolution and died by it, he was rescued from the guillotine in 1793 by Natasha, who wanted more of his sculpture. He came to America hoping for a land without war, fled the Civil War north, and has been in Milwaukee longer than almost any other Kindred. He knows much of what goes on and has gone on in the city.

He has never forgiven the lower classes for his parents' deaths. He thinks of Gracis and Lucina as nearly friends.
louis.aliasText: There is an Elder who makes everyone feel underdressed, including people in the middle of a fight.
louis.brief:
Louis Detonas is a Toreador Elder and sculptor: an extremely cultured gentleman with impeccably combed black hair and a hint of make-up on a pale face. He has a way of making everyone around him feel underdressed.

He lives in a spacious downtown apartment by Cathedral Square and stands at Lucina's side against the Anarchs.

notes.title: He lied for Gracis
notes.html: When the Mask came asking about Hrothulf during the Prince’s last weeks, Louis told them what Gracis wanted them to hear.

barth.name: Barth (“Derik Dark”)
barth.html:
A Louisiana storyteller Embraced in 1934 by Sondra, who promised he could tell stories forever. He has friends among the Blood Brothers and fears the Union, whose Caitiff could use an older generation's blood. He is looking for bodyguards.

He has taken Raul, Parovich's last childe, under his wing.
barth.aliasText: “Derik Dark, only after sundown and not for the faint of heart.” Half the Kindred in the city listen to him; the other half pretend not to.
barth.brief:
Every weeknight from 10 p.m. to 2 a.m. on WBIT, "Derik Dark" plays music and slips notices to listening Kindred: parties, rumbles, news dressed up as something else. The Elders keep telling him to be less obvious.

Off the air he is Barth, a skinny, geeky Toreador with a greasy mop of black hair and a voice far bigger than he is. He calls himself the only neutral in the Jyhad. He lives in a middle-class apartment in East Downtown.

notes.title: Not quite neutral
notes.html: He keeps Lucina warned about the Anarchs’ most destructive plans.

akawa.name: Akawa
akawa.html:
Embraced in 1770 in Missouri by a stranger fleeing white settlers, he stayed with his tribe until it was driven away, and learned to love the city as a harsher wilderness. His plan was to unite every gang, mortal and Kindred, control the city's vessels and starve the Elders until they crowned him Prince.

He attacked the Public Museum over its exhibit of Native American bones, and Lucina's Toreador retaliated without understanding why. Several peace talks with Lucina at West Milwaukee Park failed; he never showed his face and spoke through a Blood Brother.

notes.title: His sire
notes.html: His sire was Sir Edward Scott, who never remembered him. Akawa did, and meant it to be Scott’s undoing.

notes.title: Where he is
notes.html: The Council holds him, in a cell in the steam tunnels under MECCA. Raoul’s people guard it.

notes.title: Playing him
notes.html: Calm, observant, in control. You consider yourself a leader, and your plotting is worthy of an Elder.

akawa.aliasText: The Blood Brothers have a chief nobody ever sees, and a wolf that rides on the back of their lead bike.
akawa.brief:
Akawa leads the Blood Brothers, the strongest Anarch gang in the city. He is a big Plains warrior with ritual scars across his chest and black hair to the middle of his back. He speaks in a stiff, old style of "sunrises" and "the final sleep", keeps no haven and rides with his gang, often in the shape of a wolf.

During the Sabbat invasion he disappeared. The Brothers say he was taken, and they do not know by whom. The gang is in turmoil.

wrecker.name: Wrecker
wrecker.html: His name is Lewis, and only really stupid, soon-to-be-dead people use it. A Milwaukee ganger with no plan and no future, he was Embraced by Akawa in 1968 because Akawa needed muscle, and Akawa has looked out for him ever since. Cocky, violent and not bright. He respects anyone who loses to him in good spirit, frenzies if he is humiliated, and wants Turk dead.
wrecker.aliasText: If a Blood Brother on a flame-painted hog challenges you to chicken, say yes and lose gracefully.
wrecker.brief:
Wrecker is the Blood Brothers' muscle: black leather biker jacket, tight jeans, slicked-back hair, a lean cruel face and a cigarette even on the bike, a black hog with flames painted on the tank and a tire iron tied to it. He talks out of the corner of his mouth like a movie gangster and challenges strangers to games of chicken.

Since Akawa disappeared he and Ethan Stone are holding the gang together.

notes.title: Playing him
notes.html: Snide comments, mobster mumbling, a nuisance. You know you are cool.

turk.name: Turk
turk.html:
He has lived on the streets since 1967, when he was nine, and joined Zulu Nation the day it reached Milwaukee in 1972. When the gang was broken he was Embraced by one of the victors, the Chicago Anarch Gengis, who left him a Caitiff. He has killed few Kindred and crippled many. The park's homeless are the Union's herd, so it rarely fights short of blood. He fears fire beyond reason, and sleeps on the water because of it.

His lieutenant Lars runs most of the dangerous raids; Turk hopes they will kill him. The Prince forbade Turk to make the childer he needed.
turk.aliasText: Neonates crossing East Downtown travel in groups. The reason has a name.
turk.brief:
Turk leads the East Side Anarchs Union, the second Anarch gang. He is very strong and very fit and likes to intimidate with it: denim jacket, loose blue sweatpants, curly black hair sticking up after a ride. Sombre and bitter.

The Union holds East Downtown and the lakeshore from an old riverboat at Veterans Park. It rarely attacks Elders, but neonates on its turf are at risk. It has been losing to the Blood Brothers, and it lost face for its ties to the late Prince.

notes.title: Diablerist
notes.html: Turk is 12th generation because he drank the leader of a rival Anarch gang.

notes.title: The Prince’s pawn
notes.html: For five years Merik was bringing the Union under Domination and Blood Bonding its key figures. It was the Union that ambushed the Mask and the Blood Brothers.

notes.title: Esau
notes.html: A hairy old Malkavian called Esau has been whispering to him that every Kindred in the city is out to get him. Turk believes it, and calls him “the man”.

notes.title: Gengis
notes.html: His sire once came back for a single night, on the run from Chicago, and shared blood with him. If anything happened to Turk, Gengis would be here in an instant.

notes.title: New friends
notes.html: The Union has grown weak enough to find allies where it can. Lupines have swum the lake and used the lakefront parks to reach it.

decker.name: Mark Decker
decker.html:
A Revolutionary militiaman Embraced in 1777 by Lucian, who took him in his tent. He became a rich man in Alabama, fled north after the Civil War, and held off a Lupine siege of his country house for thirteen days. He warned the Council before the New Year's Eve attack of 1900 and has warned it ever since; his last report was so scathing that the Council decided the threat was imaginary.

He commands six to nine Kindred who would follow him into the noonday sun, and suburban police who think he runs a neighbourhood crime watch. He carries a shotgun loaded with silver buckshot. He could seal every road out of the city if he chose. The Sabbat meant to kill him first; it failed. Jade Riley now sleeps inside his patrol zone, and he has not decided what that means.
decker.aliasText: If you want to talk to the man who keeps the wolves out, drive Good Hope Road after dark and wait.
decker.brief:
Mark Decker commands the Anubi, the Gangrel-led guard that patrols the Outlands and fights the Lupine so that the rest of the city does not have to. He is tall and very pale, with jet-black hair, always in black or camouflage, and he seems the most honest vampire in Milwaukee. Whatever topic you raise, he will bring it back to the Lupine.

He never took his seat on the Council, and the Council thinks he is a madman. Good Hope Road is his patrol route.

notes.title: Werewolf vitae
notes.html: He loves the taste of Lupine blood. It is his secret and his alone.

notes.title: Julia
notes.html: Julia Calvin is his childe, Blood Bound and in love with him. He keeps it hidden so that no one can use her against him.

notes.title: Riding the Winds of Decay
notes.html: Some of his Gangrel run with Lupine packs under the full moon, in wolf form, and a few have been accepted. Hrothulf knows and calls it a necessary evil.

notes.title: Mortius
notes.html: He knows Dr. Mortius is in the city and suspects he is looking for the same thing the Lupine are.

notes.title: Playing him
notes.html: Be open and honest with the players. They will be shocked. Wander back to the Lupine whatever the subject.

thomas.name: Thomas Gerhieren
thomas.html:
Embraced in 1971 at sixteen by Wendy, the girl he loved, who was carried off by Werewolves soon after. Despair drove him into a frenzy that killed four people and then out into Lupine country, where Decker's ambush saved him. He joined the next night.

He sleeps in the homes of rich teenage girls from the Outlands high schools when their parents are travelling.
thomas.aliasText: One of Decker’s Anubi looks sixteen and has eyes that look straight through you.
thomas.brief: Thomas Gerhieren is an Anubi veteran: boyish, rumpled blond hair, soft pastel-blue eyes, wrinkled clothes. Look at his face and you see age that should not be there. He talks only when he must and is always busy with something, a knife or a magazine of silver rounds. After twenty years he would lead the Anubi if Decker fell.

notes.title: What Wendy wanted
notes.html: Wendy told him she knew where to find items of great power. The Werewolves came for her the same week.

julia.name: Julia Calvin
julia.html: Born on the street, raised by a homeless Korean War veteran, she begged, stole, sold herself and finally killed for money. In 1989 she took a contract on a pale man who appeared only at night. He caught her, kept her chained in his basement for a week, and Embraced her. Her contacts are criminals and prostitutes all over the city.
julia.aliasText: Decker’s guard has a woman who corrects your mistakes very loudly. Do not make any.
julia.brief: Julia Calvin rides with the Anubi: thin, gaunt and beautiful, dark hair tied up for a fight, moving with a cat's grace that some find attractive and many find frightening. She is rude, loud about other people's mistakes and respected as a warrior despite her few Disciplines.

notes.title: Bound
notes.html: She is Blood Bound to Decker and loves him with all her heart. If he dies she will understand what was done to her, and may be the only one who can stop the Anubi from going after his killer.

jacob.name: Jacob
jacob.html: Enslaved as a boy in Islamic lands, he learned that his only dignity was in how he carried himself, and he walks tall to this day. He was Embraced in 750 and is one of the oldest Kindred in the city. He recruits pawns against Esau and is very good at it: he does not start the city's feuds, but he pours oil on every one of them, and the people who fight in his war die quickly.
jacob.aliasText: A fatherly old Kindred seems to know everyone’s grievances and gives very good advice.
jacob.brief: Jacob is a distinguished, fatherly Malkavian who keeps a mansion at the very edge of Kindred territory in Greendale. He seems harmless and wise. He says there is no Jyhad, only predators who fight, and warns everyone he meets about his mad brother Esau.

notes.title: One Kindred
notes.html: Jacob and Esau are the same Kindred. He created the Esau personality when he was Embraced, and the two have been trying to destroy each other ever since. Each always seems to know what the other plans.

notes.title: Coax
notes.html: His Presence and Auspex go beyond anything taught in the city. He senses what people fear and want and brings it to the surface, and people find they cannot refuse what he asks.

notes.title: Mad ghouls
notes.html: Both of him have let insane ghouls loose in the city. When one is caught, the murders shake the Masquerade.

notes.title: Playing him
notes.html: Flatter, coax, threaten, anything to get them on your side. You are mad, and your talk can fall apart without warning.

milo.name: Milo
milo.html:
His sire fed on him in a Chicago asylum the night he had taken angel dust and purple microdots, and drank his nightmare. The Prince of Chicago spared Milo as an innocent victim, destroyed his sire and banished him. He came to Milwaukee for safety and slept in old drains and burned-out buildings until IT found him.

He distrusts Akawa and holds Kristian in contempt.
milo.alias: The man who talks about IT
milo.aliasText: Sooner or later every neonate meets the vagrant who says something in the lakeshore drains will eat us all.
milo.brief:
Milo is a Malkavian of Japanese descent who looks like a vagrant, in torn and dirty clothes, with an almost handsome voice. He never sleeps in the same place twice. He insists that something woke in a drain pipe by the lake and will eat every Kindred in the city, one by one. He tells the story differently every time.

Some nights he is perfectly normal, friendly and talks about ordinary things. It never lasts.

notes.title: IT is real
notes.html: Something really did follow him out of the lakeshore drains. The dead would call it a Spectre.

anastasia.name: Anastasia
anastasia.html: A car crash killed her parents and wrecked her face, and Parovich came to "help". She fled with Kristian when he discovered what their sire was. Her haven is a dry utility room in the steam tunnels under her old school. Kristian visits once a week and always brings her something nice.
anastasia.alias: A girl in a faded party dress
anastasia.aliasText: Parovich had childer who ran from him. One of them is said to keep a little zoo of stray cats.
anastasia.brief:
Anastasia is one of Parovich's runaway childer. She still looks young and still wears the frilly dress she had in high school, faded now to a dingy brown. She hides in empty cellars and storm drains with a little zoo of stray cats, drinks from them when she can, and asks handsome strangers whether they like her hair.

Parovich told the Council his childer were dangerous psychotics. Since his exposure nobody believes it.

notes.title: She doesn’t believe it
notes.html: She took the news of her sire’s destruction in silence. She does not believe it.

kristian.name: Kristian
kristian.html: He beat his abusive father to death with a baseball bat at sixteen, and Parovich took him from Juvenile Hall. He found out about the Black Hand by listening at doors, gathered his brother and sisters and told them to scatter; two are dead anyway. He sleeps in the basement of an elderly couple who never notice him. Scott and Jason have both used him for favours, and Jason owes him one.
kristian.aliasText: Parovich’s runaway childer had a leader, and the leader is still out there.
kristian.brief: Kristian led Parovich's childer into hiding when he found out what their sire was. Lean and compact, with a hard, almost noble face under the Nosferatu warts, young and cocky, he talks over people and does not take advice. He feels responsible for Anastasia.

notes.title: It doesn’t add up
notes.html: He met his sire’s fall without joy. No ash he saw, no witness he trusts. Too much about the story does not add up.

raul.name: Raul
raul.html: A grey-market car dealer who liked cocaine, Embraced in 1990. He gave Parovich all his money, defended him to Kristian and threatened to tell on him. Parovich made him drink often. Barth has taken him under his wing.

notes.title: The pull
notes.html: He is still Blood Bound. Some nights the bond drags him downward, toward the drains and the tunnels. He has not followed it yet.

raul.alias: A Nosferatu who sells street gossip
raul.aliasText: There is a Nosferatu who will tell you anything about the street for a price. Half of it is true.
raul.brief: Raul was Parovich's last childe: a short, whining weasel of a man, warts and no hair, who thinks he is as bad as they come. He sells street information, asks large bribes for trivial details and is wrong as often as right. He still hangs around his dead master's boarded-up mansion.

badr.name: Badr-al-Budur
badr.html:
She is paid in the blood of Kindred of the 9th generation or lower, shipped to her clan in Turkey. If she dies trying to fulfil a contract, no Assamite will ever take that target again. And she remembers everything about her employers, in case she is ever hired to kill them.

Embraced in 1867, she is descended in the blood from Fatimah, the woman who forced Alamut to accept women as assassins, and she fights her own clan's prejudice still.
badr.aliasText: Somebody in this city takes contracts from Elders and Anarchs alike and is paid in vitae. Everyone knows someone who knows how to reach her.
badr.brief: Badr-al-Budur is an Assamite assassin: a solidly built Arab woman in loose business suits, black hair tied up. She speaks very little. She travels the Northwest on contracts but always returns to her small condominium near the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee. Anarchs hire her to kill Elders, Elders hire her to kill Anarchs, and with the Prince dead business is about to boom.

raoul.name: Raoul
raoul.html: Gracis feeds him and considers him a wonderful deterrent against "undesirables".
raoul.brief: Raoul runs security at MECCA. He was a karate champion before he was given immortality; now he and a team of heavily armed mortal guards stop every Anarch raid just past the lobby.

notes.title: The cell
notes.html: His people guard a cell in the steam tunnels under MECCA. Its prisoner is Akawa.

vrasks.name: Vrasks
vrasks.html: Where he came from and what he is doing in Milwaukee nobody knows. What became of his master is uncertain; rumour says the master is still in the city and quietly backs him.
vrasks.aliasText: There is a bar on Townsend Street where you can buy a death, paid in vitae.
vrasks.brief: Vrasks owns Jungleman, a small dance bar on West Townsend Street beside Wanderers Rest Cemetery. He is a very powerful ghoul and a known assassin: he will kill anybody, or so he says, for enough Kindred blood to keep him immortal. He also buys blood from Anarchs who are short of cash.

venturi.name: Mr. Venturi
venturi.html: A Mafia tough born in 1903, he worked for Merik since the liquor days. Being a ghoul barely changed his life. He has grown very bored of it, and the kindness that was never in him seems to be coming out at last: he is surprised by anyone who looks out for him.
venturi.aliasText: The late Prince’s errand-man is still walking around. Nobody knows whose errands he runs now.
venturi.brief: Mr. Venturi was the late Prince's messenger: a big, heavy man in a tasteless suit and a tan hat, half his left ear missing, mouth always shut tight. He never looks at the person he is talking to.

notes.title: The last night
notes.html: If one of the Mask pulled him out of a burning car, he turned on the Prince at the end.

demetri.name: Demetri
demetri.html: He hid the ghoul ambush in Merik's penthouse with Obfuscate. As a young vampire he discovered a hallucinogen that opens Kindred to their own powers and wears away their minds; Merik used it on the Mask. Whether he survived the Prince is unknown.
demetri.brief: Demetri is an old Nosferatu who went mad over the centuries and was the late Prince's Dominated servant.

wilks.name: Lt. James Wilks
wilks.html: He chased the "Vampire Murderer" this autumn, was captured and held in the dungeon of the Prince's house, and escaped with the Mask while it burned. He ran to meet the fire trucks and kept his silence. He has an unusually strong will.
wilks.aliasText: A police lieutenant has been asking questions about the “Vampire Murderer” case long after it was closed.
