wilks.brief: Lieutenant James Wilks of Milwaukee Police homicide is a no-nonsense cop in his mid-thirties from a small Midwestern town, unmarried and likely to stay that way. He is respected in the department and wants his captain's bars.

notes.title: He knows
notes.html: Wilks knows what Kindred are. He promised silence and may come to the Mask for help on hard cases. If provoked he could turn a small, dangerous wing of the police against the Kindred.

urgen.name: Lisa Urgen
urgen.html: She was eighteen with twin babies in the ruins of postwar Germany when a starving vampire came to her house and drained her husband and children before her eyes. She has hunted Kindred across two continents since. She works with the Society of Leopold when it suits her, rarely by its methods. This autumn she trapped the Mask on the roof of a burnt-out lakeside hotel ten minutes before dawn.
urgen.aliasText: The Anarchs say an Inquisitor is hunting in Milwaukee: a German woman who works alone.
urgen.brief: Lisa Urgen is an Inquisitor who hunts Kindred alone. German, rumoured to have destroyed the Prince of Hamburg, she was in New York and then Chicago before Milwaukee. She has been seen with a flamethrower.

notes.title: Untouchable
notes.html: Dominate and Presence simply do not work on her.

horatio.name: Horatio Sims
horatio.html: He is a wolf born, of the Red Talons, with exactly as much humanity as the job requires. This autumn he freed the Mask from the Mouse pack's cave on Route 43, because a broken Masquerade would expose the Lupine next. He wants to hold Marquette long enough to dig, burn the Banes out of the southern woods and do it without a war he cannot win.

notes.title: Under Marquette
notes.html: What he wants is buried under St. Joan of Arc Chapel: the Eye of the Coyote and the Talon of the Eagle, stolen by Usla three centuries ago.

notes.title: One partner
notes.html: He has begun to suspect the totems cannot be taken back by one clan alone, and that the Eagle are the only partner he has. The Mouse pack’s fate showed him the Wyrm came in through the city, and that frightens him.

horatio.aliasText: Decker says the biggest pack out there has a leader who thinks before he bites. He says that is the bad news.
horatio.brief: Horatio Sims leads the Coyote, the largest Lupine pack around Milwaukee: just under a dozen strong. In human shape, which he takes only to negotiate, he is short and square-jawed. He is the most rational of the Lupine leaders, and therefore the most dangerous.

drake.name: Drake
drake.sub: A Lupine of the Mouse pack
drake.html: He carried messages between the late Prince's killers and his pack leader this autumn. During the Sabbat invasion he was broken and given to the Wyrm. He got inside the Chapel and killed Victor, then vanished. They say he hides in the tunnels under the city.

notes.title: He opened the door himself
notes.html: The corruption was not forced on him: Jesselin whispered to him through his dreams for weeks, and he opened the Granary’s doors to her himself.

notes.title: His den
notes.html: He hides in the storm sewers under the concrete Kinnickinnic, and he is not alone down there.

drake.brief: Drake is a Lupine of the Mouse pack: usually a large wolf, otherwise a chubby, bald, middle-aged man. He hates the city's Kindred and has lost friends to the Anubi.

marta.name: Marta Kaczmarek
marta.html:
Her Glamour comes from people making something useful together and recognising each other's skill: the teenager who learns a difficult seam sustains her longer than a roomful of satisfied diners. She survived 1981 because she had gone back for a mortal kitchen helper. She remembers the old court kindly until anyone suggests restoring its privileges.

Her authority is only that people accept a room she keeps warm is hers to govern. She likes Celia and will defend her from mockery, and rejects every proposal for a standing council. Nina brings young performers to her suppers; Oren distrusts the strangers Nina invites.

facts.v: Late fifties, compact, flour on her sleeves, a laugh that interrupts her own complaints.
Skin warm brown like baked crust, copper-bright eyes, curls escaping every pin.

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: Enough rent money and helpers to keep the storefront through winter. The absentee landlord is weighing a better-paying tenant; he is an ordinary man.

notes.title: The weak fire
notes.html: The Hearth's balefire falters when Marta tries to do every task herself, and she has been hiding how weak it is. She fears everyone will leave if refuge starts to sound conditional.

notes.title: What she wants
notes.html: Her old guilt: she wants rest more than another heroic responsibility.

notes.title: Playing her
notes.html: Interrupt an argument to put food in someone's hand, then return to it exactly where it stopped. "You may be right. You still have to dry the dishes."

marta.aliasText: A woman who does alterations near Mitchell Street cooks a supper for anyone who turns up once a month.
marta.brief: Marta Kaczmarek, a boggan, keeps the Last Hearth: a rented alterations shop near Mitchell Street that becomes, in the Dreaming, a long brick bakehouse with a copper stove. Once a month she hosts the Spare Chair Supper, with an empty chair for anyone not yet found.

leon.name: Leon Mercer
leon.sub: Builder of things that might work
leon.html:
He finds Glamour in stubborn, inventive problem-solving; repetitive work exhausts him. He wants to restore a short, reliable stretch of the old chimerical street railway, so that a childling never has to beg an elder for permission to visit a friend across town. His workshop becomes the Third Shift in the Dreaming, a place of power only while people are inventing.

Celia sees public transport as a way to rebuild civic trust; Ruth insists one successful trip proves nothing. Both are right about different risks, which irritates him.

facts.v: Late twenties, thin, bespectacled, work shirt, a plastic box of mismatched parts.
Porcelain face patterned with soot-black whorls, tiny sparking eyes, copper-stained fingers.

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: A stable test route, Oren's permission to use the Counterweight as one terminus, and a patron who will not claim the finished line.

notes.title: The shard
notes.html: His prototype works because it contains a shard of the Glass of the Second Door, the treasure the Ravnos used in 1981. He bought it as salvage without knowing what it was.

notes.title: Passengers he cannot see
notes.html: The tram's bell sometimes rings for passengers nobody can see. He has stopped carrying passengers, but will not give up the machine before he understands it.

notes.title: Playing him
notes.html: Relentless technical detail, then unexpected patience with beginners. "No, it isn't temperamental. It is doing exactly the wrong thing every time."

leon.alias: A repairman in the Menomonee Valley
leon.aliasText: There is a repairman in the valley who can make anything run, including things that shouldn't.
leon.brief: Leon Mercer, a nocker, repairs audio gear and industrial controls in a rented bay in the Menomonee Valley. His Chrysalis came in 1988 while he was getting a "useless" machine to run. He is building a tram.

ruth.name: Ruth Bell
ruth.kicker: Eshu · grump · Seelie when promises are involved
ruth.sub: The woman who gets you there
ruth.html:
She earns Glamour by helping people make journeys that matter to them: an audition, a reunion, a first trip alone. She cannot simply be wherever she is needed, and she does not guarantee happy endings. Her maps describe conditions, witnesses and dependable exits. The old road toward Chicago now ends at a station where every departing train carries the name of someone who abandoned Milwaukee.

Oren trusts her judgement on roads and resents her refusal to discuss the last retreat.

facts.v: Around fifty, charcoal coat, worn road atlas, pocketful of bus transfers.
Midnight skin faintly dotted with stars, boots dusted with road that never wears off, a scarf moving in wind nobody else feels.

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: To reopen one trustworthy outward trod, so that the city's fae can travel without choosing between total dependence and leaving their magical lives behind.

notes.title: The voices
notes.html: In 1981 Ruth cut the Copper Hart's return route to stop a false-door incursion. There were voices calling beyond it. She believes everyone she heard died, and she has never told Marta.

notes.title: Playing her
notes.html: Ask what someone plans to do on arrival before naming the fare. "Getting out is a direction. Where are you going?"

ruth.alias: A courier with a road atlas
ruth.aliasText: There is a courier in Sherman Park who will drive anyone anywhere, as long as they can tell her why.
ruth.brief: Ruth Bell, an eshu, works irregular courier and driving jobs from a kitchen table in Sherman Park. She knows more of the city's Dreaming roads than anyone, and gives map lessons to anyone willing to argue about the best route to a real destination.

oren.name: Oren Voss
oren.html: In 1981 he held the retreat long enough for Ruth and Marta to get out. He draws Glamour from people keeping difficult commitments, especially commitments nobody is watching, and has no patience for spectacular vows that replace practical preparation. Kit is the one local who makes him laugh, and also keeps bringing uninvited passengers.

facts.v: Broad, middle-aged maintenance man, stiff knee, quiet voice, an immaculate thermos.
Blue-grey skin, horn tips worn smooth, old bronze plates beneath a wool coat.

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: To repair the dream-bridge's counterweight before the autumn storms turn a manageable defect into a closed route.

notes.title: His oath
notes.html: His oath is to provide a return passage for anyone he personally admits. He has stretched it into a duty to save all Milwaukee, which is his own reading, and it makes him slow to welcome strangers.

notes.title: Playing him
notes.html: Offer practical help before affection. "I cannot promise that" is an act of respect.

oren.aliasText: One of the bridge maintenance men on the river works nights nobody scheduled.
oren.brief: Oren Voss, a troll, keeps the Counterweight: a small refuge beside the machinery of the Juneau Avenue bascule bridge, which in the Dreaming is a stone gatehouse hung on chains over a channel full of discarded destinations. He was the Copper Hart's dependable defender, never its commander.

celia.name: Celia Ashdown
celia.html: She draws Glamour from ensembles learning to listen to one another. She sincerely believes institutions can protect weak people from arbitrary favours, and finds it hard to see how her own inherited assumptions make them arbitrary. Marta likes her; Nina suspects her; Leon wants it in writing that no restored lord will own his tram, and Celia is beginning to think that is reasonable.

facts.v: Late twenties, red-haired, teaches beginner cello, patches her own secondhand coats.
Spring-green eyes, a narrow golden circlet she seldom wears, an elegance that makes cheap rooms look briefly intentional.

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: To relight one chamber of the Crownless Ward, the Hall of Borrowed Voices, as a public rehearsal and meeting hall open to every kith and allegiance.

notes.title: The list
notes.html: Her sponsor outside Milwaukee will advance resources only if she sends a list of the local residents and their sworn obligations. She keeps not sending it, and is paying rent with the last of her savings.

notes.title: The petition
notes.html: She once drafted a private petition to the absent dragon of the Far Guest's Seat, asking it to take responsibility for the city. She never sent it. The mountain has it anyway.

notes.title: Playing her
notes.html: Formal until someone asks a practical question she can answer. "Yes, I know the proper ceremony. We could also start by repairing the roof."

rows.b: Suspects her; arranges songs with her

celia.alias: A cello teacher on the Lower East Side
celia.brief: Celia Ashdown, a sidhe of House Gwydion, teaches beginner cello lessons and patches her own secondhand coats. She arrived in 1989 with a credible but unenforceable claim to oversee the properties of the old Copper Hart, and found people exhausted by titles.

kit.name: Kit Navarro
kit.sub: Collector of things nearly thrown away
kit.html: Kit collects the futures people abandon casually (an instrument sold after two bad lessons, an unfinished costume, a child's outdated map) and gains Glamour when someone unexpectedly uses one again. Nina finds them paid work; Oren quietly repairs their bicycle; Kit finds the cast-off parts Leon needs and always understates the trouble.

facts.v: Seventeen, bicycle courier, patched jacket, an inexhaustible supply of useless keys.
Ringed tail, dark mask, bright ears, hands that cannot leave a strange fastening alone.

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: To get a bag of mislaid objects back from the Unfinished Index before it is classified as a permanent acquisition. It holds a living chimerical mouse Kit promised to return to a child.

notes.title: Custodian, not owner
notes.html: Kit's claim ticket for a blue-lit room in the Crownless Ward names them custodian, not owner. They pretend not to understand the difference, because ownership sounds like finally having a place nobody can take away.

notes.title: Playing them
notes.html: Indirect truths and flamboyantly implausible denials. A bad lie is often a plea to be asked a kinder question.

kit.alias: A bicycle courier with too many keys
kit.brief: Kit Navarro, a raccoon pooka, is a seventeen-year-old bicycle courier and flea-market regular with a patched jacket and an inexhaustible supply of useless keys. Chrysalis in 1990.

nina.name: Nina Salazar
nina.sub: Insists there will be another song
nina.html: Her Glamour comes from a crowd that stops being an audience and becomes collaborators. She is very good with shy amateurs, and believes the survivors sometimes confuse safety with giving up. She and Celia argue about whose name goes on the invitation, then spend hours arranging the same song.

facts.v: Mid-twenties Mexican American percussionist and part-time waitress; strong forearms, battered boots.
Dark curling horns, amber eyes, shaggy legs, the smell of warm wood after rain.

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: A public neighbourhood performance before winter, with Celia's musicians, Leon's repaired sound equipment and the people Marta has brought together.

notes.title: The Encore
notes.html: A chimera called the Encore answers to her music and will not let a good night end. She dismissed the first warning as nerves and has now cancelled two rehearsals trying to understand it.

notes.title: Playing her
notes.html: Generous attention, then sudden impatience when someone turns a person's desire into a moral lesson. "Let her be bad at it. She only started yesterday."

rows.b: Respects her; wary of rescue stories

nina.brief: Nina Salazar, a satyr, is a percussionist and part-time waitress who plays small Milwaukee venues and community events. Her Chrysalis came in 1987 during a disastrous show the audience saved by joining in.

bjorn.name: Bjorn Halvorsen
bjorn.html: His dream travel uses learned magic and a dream-anchor called the Pillow Sail. Eating something in a dream may change that dream; it does not erase its real counterpart, steal knowledge or cure the dreamer. He asks consent for repeat visits, though his curiosity sometimes gets ahead of his manners. He carries the only working scale-light lantern anyone knows of.

facts.v: Heavily muscled Scandinavian in a fisherman’s sweater.
Slate-red skin, ice-pale eyes, teeth like broken white crockery, impossible crumbs in his beard.

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: To taste the last fruit of the Far Guest's Winter Orchard, which ripens only for someone who has found a hunger they cannot name.

notes.title: The bell
notes.html: He once bit through a bell in the mountain's vestibule. He now hears a faint note when someone promises what they have no right to give. It is imperfect, not infallible, and the mountain's keeper wants the bell restored.

notes.title: Other inhabitants
notes.html: He has noticed signs that more people live in Ivory's Keep than she admits. He has not got past the wards.

notes.title: Playing him
notes.html: Calm, literal, startlingly discriminating. "No. A nightmare can be excellent. That one was merely cruel."

bjorn.alias: A dock worker in a fisherman’s sweater
bjorn.brief: Bjorn Halvorsen, a redcap, does irregular dock work on the Inner Harbor. He arrived after the war. His private vocation is tasting dreams: the brass apple from a schoolboy's invented planet, the banquet nobody attends.

ivory.name: Ivory
ivory.sub: Custodian of the Gloaming Keep; overseer of the Michigan Pocket
ivory.html:
She leans on the routines and Banality of school to stay steady. Exploring the Dreaming remains of the Pabst Building after her Chrysalis in 1986, she joined the broken Copper Hart to the unclaimed sluagh holdings and made the Gloaming Keep, whose approach lies inside the Nosferatu warrens. She also looks after the Michigan Pocket, the cave of rescued buildings under the lake, alone since the Nosferatu stopped coming.

She trains a few young mortal monster-hunters with chimera of her own invention: the Knock-under-the-Bridge, the Coat on the Last Bus, the Lantern in the Drain. Her contact with the Nosferatu is limited to individuals and to a door nobody forces.

facts.v: A grumpy schoolgirl.
The only sluagh left in Milwaukee; she remembers being a sidhe patron of heroes.

notes.title: Patron of heroes
notes.html: She remembers being a sidhe patron of heroes, and she knows the Secret of the sluagh.

notes.title: The patients
notes.html: She secretly shelters eight changelings in Bedlam, survivors of the 1981 war, in the private wards of the Keep, and hopes to heal them. She will not accept death and reincarnation as a treatment.

notes.title: The hunters
notes.html: She quietly helps Wolfgang, Rudeus Frost and Doctor Fire. Rudeus has faerie blood, and she sees kin in him.

ivory.brief: Ivory looks like a grumpy north-side schoolgirl who dislikes school and attends it anyway. She is the last sluagh in Milwaukee.

lola.name: Dolores “Lola” Wendt
lola.html: She is kinain: she knows that certain visitors see an extra Milwaukee, helps them selectively and expects consent before anything leaves its community. A basement leak threatens years of work, and she needs boxes and two people with a car.
lola.alias: A retired printer with a lot of paper
lola.brief: Dolores "Lola" Wendt, a retired printing worker, keeps playbills, neighbourhood newsletters and the small publications nobody else thinks to preserve.

notes.title: The invitation
notes.html: She owns a duplicated 1980 supper invitation that puts two supposedly unrelated incidents of the War of False Doors on the same night.

arthur.name: Arthur Saye
arthur.html: He has walked the Glass Orchard under temporary enchantment and understands it as a place visited under unusual conditions. He is weighing a better-paid job outside Milwaukee. His apprentice could carry on his work, differently, if anyone asked her.
arthur.brief: Arthur Saye tends plants at the Mitchell Park Domes and draws impossible gardens on the backs of discarded forms.

hester.name: Hester Ames
hester.html: She is interested in recurring dream geography and knows no fae by name. One of her research notebooks was lost at the edge of the Marquette zone.
hester.alias: A mature student at Mount Mary
hester.brief: Hester Ames, a mature student at Mount Mary College and a member of the Church of Isis: observant, politically stubborn, better at taking notes than at seeing who benefits from her curiosity.

notes.title: Her sponsor
notes.html: Her distant sponsor is Dr. Mortius, and she does not know he is a vampire. She recently asked a reference librarian about a building that appears on no map but matches the Crownless Ward, and Mortius heard about it.

eddie.name: Eddie Rusk
eddie.html: He has learned to help frightened people, check an exit and stop a companion panicking, and now mistakes that for understanding every monster. Another member has started publishing names and addresses without consent.
eddie.alias: A night-shift clerk who hunts ghosts
eddie.brief: Eddie Rusk, a night-shift stock clerk, belongs to a small amateur club that investigates hauntings over pitchers of beer in a bowling alley.

notes.title: His teacher
notes.html: Ivory has anonymously encouraged his better instincts.

quire.name: Mrs. Quire
quire.html: She wants every unfinished work to have a fair chance to finish, and can find a deposited manuscript by the question that created it. She cannot tell honest postponement from cowardice without talking to the person.
quire.brief: Mrs. Quire keeps the Unfinished Index: an elderly librarian assembled from card-catalogue drawers, ink-dark lace and a face nobody remembers clearly. She speaks softly, because a shouted question rearranges whole wings.

notes.title: Overclassifying
notes.html: She has begun filing unfinished lives as unfinished manuscripts. A neighbourhood carpenter dreams nightly of shelves being built around him. Releasing a dreamer means showing her that a life can stay worthwhile without finishing that work.

rent.name: The Rent Collector
rent.html: It wants rooms inhabited responsibly and can identify a valid custodial obligation on any door. It cannot create ownership or a deed. It accepts repairs, regular use or an orderly handover as payment, and turns threatening when someone hoards doors to keep others out. It carefully keeps tenants' hand-drawn nameplates long after their rooms are gone.
rent.alias: A porter with a key for a tongue
rent.brief: The Rent Collector, porter of the Crownless Ward: a lanky figure in a coat of old leases, with a key for a tongue and bells in its cuffs. It knocks before entering, even where a building has no wall left.

usher.name: The Ashen Usher
usher.sub: Attendant of the Far Guest’s Seat
usher.html: It wants to discharge its duties without admitting that nobody receives them. It opens the public chambers and interprets the audience customs, but cannot summon the dragon or leave while a petition is pending. A cassette case interests it more than a sword. It asks who requested a visit, and becomes almost hopeful when told nobody did.
usher.brief: The Ashen Usher attends the Far Guest's Seat: a tall figure of overlapping flakes like cooled ash, with empty sleeves and a bright coal for a mouth. Its shadow has wings its body never had.

notes.title: The petitions
notes.html: The mountain has begun accepting petitions in the absent dragon's name. Every unanswered petition adds a step to the Listening Stair and makes the road home longer.

tollman.name: The Tollman of Two Banks
tollman.html: It can delay a crossing, demand a hearing and remember bargains. Paying twice satisfies neither half. Introducing two people who really want to meet across the river can quiet it for weeks. Ruth thinks it is lonely; Oren thinks loneliness can still be extortion.
tollman.brief: The Tollman of Two Banks squats under the White Flag Crossing in two incompatible uniforms stitched down the middle. Each half insists it belongs to the lawful city.

tuesday.name: Miss Tuesday
tuesday.html: She follows the trail of any object genuinely missed by its maker, and refuses to fetch tools for anyone who blames them for his own cruelty. She follows Leon without belonging to him. Her lunchbox holds the last compliment she received, written on a napkin.
tuesday.brief: Miss Tuesday is a long-legged workshop hound made of gauges, rivets and a battered lunchbox, dreamed into being by workers looking forward to the part of the week when they might finish something of their own.

encore.name: The Encore
encore.html: It wants an exceptional night never to end, and makes an enchanted audience feel that leaving would destroy something precious. A satisfying ending freely accepted undoes it; a curtain call dedicated to someone else's next attempt could turn it into a useful stage-spirit. Nina has to take part in that choice.
encore.brief: The Encore is a gorgeous absence on a stage: footlights with nobody between them, applause without hands.

surveyor.name: The Surveyor of Necessary Losses
surveyor.html: It wants to prove that every settlement requires someone else's permanent loss, and consolidates chimerical buildings by consuming others. It honours narrow terms faithfully and cannot seize a responsibly occupied room. It was born from ordinary civic rationalisations.
surveyor.brief: The Surveyor of Necessary Losses: a courteous figure with rolled plans under one arm and a face that becomes a familiar official's whenever someone wants reassurance. Its measuring chain is always slightly too short.

notes.title: Its offer
notes.html: It has offered Celia a habitable rehearsal hall before Nina's concert. The price is three blue windows of the Crownless Ward, put out for ever.

alisande.name: Lady Alisande of the Copper Hart
alisande.sub: Former lady of the last court
alisande.html: Her court had beauty, useful hospitality and a habit of treating other people's labour as an inexhaustible resource. In 1981 she gathered the refugees at the Copper Hart; it seemed defensible, and it gave the attackers a predictable target.
alisande.alias: A lady in the private wards
alisande.brief: Lady Alisande of the Copper Hart, a sidhe, hosted the seasonal assemblies of 1969–79 in the Hall of the Copper Hart. Most people believe she died in 1981.

notes.title: Alive
notes.html: She survives in Bedlam in Ivory's private wards, rehearsing again and again an audience at which nobody has yet been hurt.

coil.name: Peter Coil
coil.alias: A nocker in the private wards
coil.brief: Peter Coil, a nocker, was presumed dead in 1981.

notes.title: Alive
notes.html: He survives in Bedlam in Ivory's wards, repairing a door that breaks whenever it opens.

june.name: June-of-the-Many-Ribbons
june.alias: A satyr in the private wards
june.brief: June-of-the-Many-Ribbons, a satyr, was presumed dead in 1981. Marta made her a ribbon before the war.

notes.title: Alive
notes.html: She survives in Bedlam in Ivory's wards, and greets every visitor as someone still expected at a long-cancelled celebration.

silas.name: Silas Vane & Ada Vale
silas.html: They stole the Glass of the Second Door and used it to turn familiar escape routes into prepared ambushes. Twenty-five of the thirty-eight resident Kithain died, including every sluagh but Ivory, who came later. Silas died with the sunrise on the mortal side of a compromised refuge; the survivors hunted Ada down soon after. No Ravnos remain in Milwaukee. They were two particular predators, not representatives of their clan.
silas.brief: Silas Vane and Ada Vale, two Ravnos, made war on the city's fae in 1980–81 with a small mortal network in property clearance, theatrical equipment and architectural salvage.

vollmer.name: Anacreon Konrad Vollmer
vollmer.html: He is precise, tired and proud of a city that rarely notices him. Milwaukee is a minor Citadel under the Chicago Necropolis, and Vollmer has spent ninety years keeping it too dull for Chicago to interfere.

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: Merik’s victims Reaped, registered and quiet before Chicago sends an inspector.

notes.title: Pressure & secret · Storyteller
notes.html: He has a long, cordial acquaintance with the Malkavian Jason, whose Auspex can hear him. Some of Jason’s famously wise remarks in Council were Vollmer’s. Neither has told anyone.

vollmer.brief: A brewery-ward alderman who died of old age in 1899 and has administered the dead ever since.

reinholt.name: Sergeant Otto Reinholt
reinholt.sub: Marshal of the Soldiers Home garrison

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: To find and Reap whoever is turning Juneau Park into a killing ground. He does not yet know the killer is already destroyed.

reinholt.brief: A Civil War veteran knifed in a tavern quarrel outside the Soldiers Home in 1898. He commands the garrison and the Ninth Watch, and believes in drill, rosters and the dignity of soldiers who are forgotten.

dolan.name: Centurion Thomas Dolan
dolan.html: He is cheerful, superstitious and very good on bad water.

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: A new crew. Too many of his drowned have forgotten their names.

dolan.brief: A Third Ward militiaman drowned with the Lady Elgin in 1860, who took her helm on this side because nobody else would.

anselm.name: Father Anselm
anselm.html: This autumn he has to enter strangers too: the homeless that Dragos Dalca took for his fleshcraft keep turning up as new, bewildered ghosts by the harbour and the fish plant.

notes.title: Pressure & secret · Storyteller
notes.html: He has been writing some of the newly dead into the book as “passed beyond” and letting them go to Walnut Street.

anselm.brief: A parish priest who died in the influenza of 1918. He keeps the Citadel’s book of the dead and pares back Shadows with Castigation, gently and without illusions.

grau.name: Matron Ilse Grau

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: A week’s delay, a list of names returned to the living, and the Anacreon’s permission for either.

grau.brief: A county poor-farm matron who died at her post in 1911. She knows the name of every unmarked grave and is watching the excavation unpick her charges one coffin at a time.

penny.name: Mr. Penny
penny.html: Everything has a price. He is honest about it, which most people find worse.
penny.brief: Edwin Pennington, a hotel accountant who died at his desk in 1931, still balances the ledgers of the dead.

brauer.name: Hilde Brauer
brauer.html: She is brilliant, pragmatic and very short of materials.

notes.title: Pressure & secret · Storyteller
notes.html: She wants Merik’s victims for the forge. The Anacreon has not said no.

brauer.brief: A tannery forewoman killed by a boiler in 1902. She forges the chains and coin the Citadel runs on.

duval.name: Colette Duval
duval.sub: Mistress of the Pabst Theater gallery
duval.brief: A touring actress who died onstage in 1924. She is the Citadel’s face for delicate errands and its best liar.

hollis.name: Lorraine Hollis
hollis.html: She has heard of the sluagh child, Ivory, and would like to meet her.

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: To bring Merik’s newly dead to Walnut Street before anyone forges them into coin.

notes.title: Pressure & secret · Storyteller
notes.html: Her neighbourhood exists because people remember it. In 1991 fewer living people do every year, and the edges are starting to fray.

hollis.brief: A jazz singer who died in 1959, a few years before the bulldozers came. She holds relic Bronzeville together with music, memory and a hard-won rule that nobody is Reaped on her street.

mazur.name: Joe Mazur
mazur.html: He is fierce, funny, and allergic to anyone who wears a Legion mask.

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: Merik’s newly dead, before the Hierarchy chains them.

notes.title: Pressure & secret · Storyteller
notes.html: His Shadow has more say in the Circle’s plans than he realises.

mazur.brief: He says he was a rolling-mill hand shot in the Bay View volley of 1886. His name is not on any list of the dead, and he says the list is wrong.

clotilde.name: Sister Clotilde
clotilde.brief: A teaching nun who died in 1949 and was led to the chapel by its cold stone. She is luminous and certain, and kind to strangers.

benchcouple.name: The bench couple
benchcouple.brief: Two ordinary people walking home from a movie. They are Enfants, days dead, Fettered to a park bench and to each other, and everyone in the Shadowlands wants them for something.

burningman.name: The Burning Man
burningman.sub: The fire in the Newhall ruin
burningman.brief: Whatever keeps the Newhall House burning. It wears the faces of the 1883 dead and offers to end their suffering.

drainthing.name: The Drain-Thing
drainthing.html: It talks to Milo because nobody listens to Milo.
drainthing.brief: Once a wraith, long since eaten by its own Shadow. It has learned that vampires are lonely in a way it can taste.

tworuiz.name: Two-Moons Ruiz
tworuiz.html: She almost never takes human shape: the human city disgusts her, but she knows its spirits better than anyone in the clan. She keeps a standing table at the Copper Queen’s court and an informant among the Storm-Crows.

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: An honest answer from the Drowned Thief.

notes.title: Pressure & secret · Storyteller
notes.html: She has already spoken to Usla once, and has not told Horatio what he said.

tworuiz.brief: A quiet grey she-wolf Theurge. The quarry workers who saw her on the rim of the pit named her “Ruiz”, and she tolerates the name with distaste.

patience.name: Patience Vey
patience.sub: Keeper of the Grudge-Song (the Coyote version)
patience.html: She swears oaths under the Polish Moon because she trusts nothing else, and travels to the clock over rooftops so as not to touch the asphalt.
patience.brief: The Coyote’s memory. A rust-coloured she-wolf who knows the clan’s history back to Usla as a long comic epic that changes a little every time she tells it, and there isn’t a single human word in it: only howls, growls and laughter.

oldquarry.name: Old Quarry
oldquarry.html: He remembers the last time the Coyote and the Eagle almost made peace.
oldquarry.brief: A grey wolf who has never worn a human face for more than an hour. He judges disputes for the clan by staring at both parties until one of them laughs.

lark.name: Lark
lark.sub: A young she-wolf who wants the feud to end
lark.html: She has been secretly meeting Tamsin Rook of the Eagle on the Treaty Green, and they are close to doing something brave and stupid. Since they fought Banes side by side in the blighted woods, they are harder to separate.
lark.brief: First Changed a year ago; in human shape she looks like an awkward girl of sixteen, and she hates it.

agnes.name: Agnes Hightree, Sky-Rends
agnes.html: Through trusted people the pack secretly owns the Seven Fires casino; Agnes never sets foot in its halls, but its money pays for lawyers, buys land and puts children through school. She hates the Kindred with a pure, practised hatred, and the Coyote only slightly less. She is not stupid. She knows the raids will kill her people one day, and now that the Tremere have poisoned her forest, she cannot see how to save even that.

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: To clear the Banes from her woods, and proof that the Coyote stole the Talon, or that they didn’t.

notes.title: Pressure & secret · Storyteller
notes.html: She has felt Gnaw riding her raiders and thinks it is the Eagle’s anger. It isn’t.

agnes.brief: A big, grey-haired woman, a farmer by day and leader of the raids by night. Her family has lived on this land longer than the city has existed, and she knows every elder in Milwaukee’s Native communities.

coaleye.name: Coal-Eye
coaleye.html: This autumn he is drawing a different map, of the Bane nests in his own forest, and it grows faster than he can draw.
coaleye.brief: A lean metis with one black eye and one burned one. He has scouted every Kindred haven on the east side through the Umbra’s taint, and he can draw you a map.

sparrow.name: Brother Sparrow
sparrow.html: He hears the Wounded Eagle’s voice in the wind. Lately it has been telling him to hate harder.

notes.title: Pressure & secret · Storyteller
notes.html: What he hears is Gnaw. Parovich fed it first; now the remnants of Velez’s Sabbat do.

sparrow.brief: A gentle former seminarian who could never choose between his grandfather’s prayers and the mission’s, and finally kept both.

tamsin.name: Tamsin Rook
tamsin.kicker: Garou · Eagle · Child of Gaia Galliard
tamsin.html: She sings the Grudge better than anyone in the clan and has started, privately, to doubt it. She is meeting Lark of the Coyote.
tamsin.brief: Seventeen and fierce. The only member of the clan who isn’t Wendigo: a Child of Gaia whom Agnes took in when her own pack died.

rosa.name: Rosa “Granary” Wójcik
rosa.sub: Former leader of the Mouse clan
rosa.html: She died in the Granary’s cellars on the night the Sabbat and the Tremere came, last, at the door the others would have escaped through.

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: To learn why part of her pack helped Merik, and who ordered it. Now she never will.

notes.title: Pressure & secret · Storyteller
notes.html: She suspected Erica was dead but not how. A week before she died she smelled strange blood in the Warrens and put it down to Merik’s Kindred.

rosa.brief: Fifty, a produce wholesaler’s widow with a voice that carried across a warehouse floor. She held fifteen difficult Garou together by feeding them, scolding them and never forgetting a favour, and kept the moon bridge to the Coyote open because she believed the clans would need each other.

benny.name: Benny Two-Shoes
benny.kicker: Garou · Mouse · Glass Walker Ragabash · fallen
benny.sub: Union man (the other kind), now missing
benny.html: He thought the Kindred were hilarious and dangerous, in that order. The Sabbat got to him through debts and anger; on the night of the massacre he was seen in the cellars on the wrong side. Nobody has seen him since, and the Bazaar’s traders say his tracks smell of the Wyrm.
benny.brief: A dockworkers’ union steward and full-time trickster who knew every cellar, loading dock and back door in the Third Ward.

teodor.name: Little Teodor
teodor.html: On the night of the massacre he decided wrong: Jesselin came small.
teodor.brief: Born of two Mouse Garou, small, misshapen and very clever. He kept the doors of the Warrens and decided who counted as “large”.

mira.name: Mira Kessler
mira.html: She died covering the pack’s retreat and took two shovelheads with her.

notes.title: Pressure & secret · Storyteller
notes.html: She tracked Erica’s scent to Merik’s penthouse the night she died and knew the Prince had killed her. She told no one, and the secret died with her.

mira.brief: A former boxer who ran beside Erica the Gangrel for ten years and loved her like a sister.

wojciks.name: The Wójcik family
wojciks.html: Now they have buried Rosa, and they ask no questions of Mercer, who comes to Sunday dinner.
wojciks.brief: Three generations of Rosa’s in-laws. They fed the pack, hid its wounded and were fiercely uncurious.

dot.name: Dot Brennan
dot.html: This autumn her cattle are sick and so is the creek, and she was the first to understand the forest had been poisoned.
dot.brief: Practical, funny and tired: the Eagle clan’s quartermaster and conscience, who has buried two sons who Changed.

abe.name: Abe Lindqvist
abe.html: The Coyote’s wolves tolerate him, the only human they tolerate, because he keeps other humans away, and because an old wolf line smoulders in his blood through a Swedish great-grandmother. Abe thinks the wolves on the rim of the pit are just very bold coyotes.
abe.brief: An ordinary man who knows nothing: he keeps the mortal world away from the Grinning Stone with fences, paperwork and a shotgun he has never fired.

grin.name: Coyote’s Grin
grin.sub: The Coyote’s patron, one eye blind
grin.brief: Cunning, generous and cruel by turns. It wants its eye back, and it will happily trick its own children into getting it.

woundedeagle.name: The Wounded Eagle
woundedeagle.sub: The Eagle’s patron, one talon gone
woundedeagle.brief: Proud and furious, crying for its talon. It has never forgiven, and it does not understand why its children are dying.

grandmouse.name: Grandmother Mouse
grandmouse.html: Now she has one child left, and she is silent; Mercer can’t tell whether she is sleeping or dying.
grandmouse.brief: Tiny, silver and ancient, the survivor of everything. She taught her children to hide, to share and to bite only when it mattered.

drownedthief.name: The Drowned Thief
drownedthief.html: Greatwater keeps him. He is the only witness to the truth of the theft, and to the rite that sealed Holy Hill.
drownedthief.brief: An outcast Garou who stole two totems’ strength to save the Menominee from Chiclena’s brood, and then hid his theft in his own body.

greatwater.name: Greatwater
greatwater.brief: Vast, cold and indifferent. It speaks through fog, ice and storm, and it has never taken a side.

breeze.name: The Lake Breeze
breeze.sub: Witness of the Lake Park Truce
breeze.brief: Brisk, cheerful and smug. It cools tempers and carries the news of any broken truce to every caern in the city.

ravinekids.name: The Ravine Children
ravinekids.brief: Small, giggling and rule-breaking. They will lead you anywhere for a game.

unnamed.name: The Unnamed
unnamed.sub: The thing at the bottom of the bog
unnamed.brief: It changes those who listen to it.

icemother.name: Ice-Mother’s Remnant
icemother.sub: The ice that carved the lake
icemother.brief: Mostly asleep. She stirs in hard winters, and then the Ice Road on the death side freezes in sympathy.

lapham.name: Lapham’s Watcher
lapham.brief: Meticulous and kind. It will warn the clans of storms if asked politely and thanked afterwards.

alewives.name: The Thousand Alewives
alewives.brief: Silver, mournful and vengeful. It remembers every poison poured into the lake and who poured it.

kinnickinnic.name: Kinnickinnic
kinnickinnic.brief: It begs every passing Garou to break one band. Each band broken floods a few blocks of the South Side’s Penumbra.

northdam.name: The Dammed Reach
northdam.sub: The Milwaukee River behind the dam
northdam.brief: It remembers everything said over its water and waits for the dam to come down.

eightcount.name: Eight-Count
eightcount.brief: A crystalline spider the size of a bus that counts everything. It cannot imagine a thing it hasn’t counted, and it is beginning to notice the uncounted gap where the Pabst Building used to be.

tallest.name: The Tallest Thing
tallest.brief: A proud civil servant of a spirit that sees the whole Penumbra from its roof and trades what it sees for new compliments.

warden.name: The Concrete Warden
warden.brief: Square and tireless. It believes it saves lives, and it may be right.

spindle.name: The Departure Spindle
spindle.brief: It keeps the manifest of everything that leaves, and it cannot imagine why anyone would stay.

mowers.name: The Mowing Spiders
mowers.brief: Pale and flat, and harmless unless you are a weed.

inkwell.name: The Inkwell
inkwell.brief: Many-handed and always on deadline. It trades rumours with every spirit in town.

bridgenowhere.name: The Bridge to Nowhere
bridgenowhere.brief: Shy and enormous. It carries anyone who tells it where they are going.

parkeast.name: The Park East Spur
parkeast.brief: It expects to be torn down and spends its nights apologising to the neighbourhood beneath it.

gambrinus.name: Gambrinus
gambrinus.sub: Old king of the Pabst hill

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: A reason to believe he will last.

gambrinus.brief: Generous, sentimental and frightened of the end. His vats are running low.

copperqueen.name: The Copper Queen
copperqueen.sub: Spirit of the State Street brewery
copperqueen.brief: Bright, rich and expanding. Her peace is the strongest neutral law in the Penumbra, and she collects everyone’s stories.

widow.name: The Widow of the Vats
widow.brief: She polishes kettles nobody will fill and gives old recipes to anyone who promises to brew them.

ironhorse.name: The Iron Horse

notes.title: Pressure & secret · Storyteller
notes.html: It meant to offer Akawa a pact that would have made him, in spirit terms, a lesser totem of the Blood Brothers. Now it can smell Akawa’s trail, faint, reeking of old blood and stone, and it will serve anyone who leads it to its rider. Whoever helps will learn where the Council keeps its prisoner.

ironhorse.brief: Loud, proud and fast. It loved the wolf who rode with the Blood Brothers, and now that wolf has vanished and the Horse searches the whole city for him.

compost.name: Grandmother Compost
compost.brief: Immense and unhurried. The Wyrm, the Weaver and the Wyld all respect her, and she has outlived three septs.

reassembled.name: The Reassembled
reassembled.sub: Spirit of the South Side basilica
reassembled.brief: A patchwork giant built from another city’s stones. It shelters spirits who have lost their homes.

ambassador.name: The Grey Ambassador
ambassador.brief: Wise, sad and patient. Lupus Garou find it unbearable and come back anyway.

lantern.name: The Healers’ Lantern
lantern.brief: It helps any Garou who comes to heal and no Garou who comes to fight.

hedgelords.name: The Hedgerow Lords
hedgelords.sub: Proud spirits of the North Shore
hedgelords.brief: Trespass is the only crime they recognise. They have been known to hire Banes as watchmen.

moonkeeper.name: The Moonkeeper
moonkeeper.brief: A tall Lune in silver, with a clock face for a mirror. She enforces every oath sworn beneath her moon and opens the Lunar Stair once a year.

tallow.name: Tallow
tallow.brief: Slow, enormous and nearly unkillable while the valley feeds it.

tannintwins.name: The Tannin Twins
tannintwins.brief: Joined at the hip. They cure anything thrown in until it can never rot or grow again.

static.name: Static
static.brief: It feeds on panic and wrong addresses.

murmur.name: Murmur
murmur.brief: A grey mist that feeds on every shout and every unanswered plea.

hive.name: The Hive-Queen
hive.brief: Half Weaver, half something hungrier, and expanding into the woods.

gnaw.name: Gnaw
gnaw.html: Parovich used to feed it blood; now the leftovers of Guillem Velez’s Sabbat do, and in the blighted woods it finds plenty of its own food.
gnaw.brief: Thin and grinning. It whispers to the Eagle’s Rage.

jade.name: Jade Riley
jade.html:
Her grandsire is an old Methuselah who wants to steer the clan back to its philosopher-king roots, and her appointment is his work. She knows exactly how that looks and resents it. She wants to be reckoned with for what she has done, not for who sent her.

Her ghoul and oldest friend, Macy Carver, brings her everything the city's protest scene knows. Kayla, a sister of the Church of Isis, works for her as well.

notes.title: Where she sleeps
notes.html: The tower floor is a decoy with its lights on timers. She sleeps in Macy Carver’s house in Wauwatosa, inside the Anubi patrol zone, and Decker knows exactly who is staying there.

notes.title: What her grandsire wants
notes.html: He does not want victories from her. He wants her to found a school in Milwaukee and lecture. Jade does not want to be anyone’s project.

notes.title: Kayla
notes.html: Kayla also reports to Dr. Mortius, and tells each of them different things.

jade.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
jade.aliasText: The Brujah seat went to an outsider nobody voted for.
jade.brief:
Jade Riley took the Brujah seat on the Council after Sir Edward Scott's death, appointed over the heads of the local Brujah through the influence of her grandsire. She is educated, sharp-tongued and terrifying in a fight. During the invasion she killed the Sabbat's dragon, Dragos Dalca, with her bare hands at the fish plant.

Nobody takes her seriously anyway. To the Elders she is an upstart; to the Blood Brothers she was "sent from above". Her official haven is a whole floor of a glass tower on East Michigan Street. Her childe Jamie Robinson sings with the Rust Saints.

macy.name: Macy Carver
macy.html: She is Jade Riley's ghoul and oldest confidant, and everything she learns she brings to Jade. She wants Jade to finally do something truly radical.

notes.title: Her house
notes.html: The Brujah Primogen sleeps in Macy’s little blue house in Wauwatosa.

macy.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
macy.brief: Macy Carver is pushing forty and looks twenty: a trust-fund kid and rebel by vocation. Gulf War marches, squats, raves, eco-camps: wherever someone is protesting something, she is there.

jamie.name: Jamie Robinson
jamie.html: His family's gas station stood on Highway 41 for thirty years, until it was condemned for a widening. One morning the demolition crew found an empty pad: no foundations, no pumps, no fuel stains.

notes.title: The station
notes.html: Ivory carried the station off to the Michigan Pocket. Jamie has been there. The pumps still work, and he cannot decide whether he wants it back.

jamie.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
jamie.aliasText: The singer of the Rust Saints only plays after dark. People who have been to a show say that is not a coincidence.
jamie.brief: Jamie Robinson is the voice of the Rust Saints and one of the most recognisable faces in the city's punk scene; the band plays the Rusty Nail in Riverwest. He is Jade Riley's childe, Embraced for his fury and his ability to hold a room.

kayla.name: Kayla
kayla.sub: Ghoul, sister of the Church of Isis
kayla.html: She is a ghoul who works for Jade Riley and for Dr. Mortius at the same time, and each of them believes she is theirs first.

notes.title: Three masters
notes.html: She tells each of them different things and writes the truth down only for the Church.

kayla.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
kayla.brief: Kayla is calm, observant and never without a notebook; a sister of the inner circle of the Church of Isis.

arianna.name: Arianna
arianna.sub: Ghoul, student, sister of the Church of Isis
arianna.html: A ghoul trusted with too much, too soon, she sometimes deals with the Chapel directly, carrying books, blood and messages without the Church's go-betweens. Haberman finds her "charmingly useful".
arianna.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
arianna.brief: Arianna is an Egyptology student at UWM and a sister of the Church of Isis.

annalena.name: Annalena
annalena.html: She remembers the taste of real magic and looks for it in her flasks. She recently led an unsanctioned expedition into the Gloaming Keep, a changeling stronghold in the Dreaming, lost several valuable ghouls there and earned the anger of the fae. Her flight ended at a convenience store that no longer exists. She is on thin ice with the Chapel's council and the changelings alike.

notes.title: What she brought out
notes.html: She brought something out of the Keep. Ivory knows exactly what.

annalena.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
annalena.brief: Annalena is the Chapel's alchemist, one of the oldest Tremere in the city. She is said to have been a mage of House Tremere before it became a clan of vampires.

haberman.name: Benjamin Haberman
haberman.html: Embraced in Vienna in the 1890s, he has spent the century on blood genealogy, the bibliography of the forbidden and gossip. Without Vienna watching he has blossomed: he orders books he once had to hide and corresponds with half the occult booksellers of the Midwest. He is writing a history of the null zone and wants access to St. Joan of Arc Chapel before the ritual begins.

notes.title: His correspondent
notes.html: One of his society correspondents is Jesselin. He suspects her and thinks he is playing her. She thinks the same.

haberman.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
haberman.brief: Benjamin Haberman is a Tremere researcher and archivist at the Chapel: long hair, half-moon spectacles, rings in one ear, a pinstriped waistcoat and the smile of a man who knows where the right book is.

newman.name: Luke Newman
newman.sub: Chapel researcher, acting head of security
newman.html: A specialist in wards and boundaries, he was given security after Victor's death because he knows best how wards break. He rebuilt the Chapel's defences in three nights, started a visitors' log and vets even the Church of Isis ghouls. He also built the antenna rigs for the four anchors of the Chapel's ritual.

notes.title: He knows
notes.html: He already knows the leak ran through Haberman’s correspondence. He is keeping quiet to catch whoever is on the other end.

newman.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
newman.alias: A pale Tremere with pointed ears
newman.brief: Luke Newman is a Tremere researcher, acting head of security at the Chapel: bald, chalk-pale, with pointed ears and thick round spectacles, the mark of an old ritual gone wrong that he does not discuss. A pedant and a man of lists.

maximus.name: Maximus McKenzie
maximus.sub: Sabbat sorcerer, dealer in blood-magic totems
maximus.html: He is a Tremere of House Goratrix, the Sabbat's own sorcerers. He helped the infiltration, and with Jesselin he defiled the protected places in the Root River woods so that a plague of Banes would keep the Lupine busy while the Sabbat moved in. Every charm he sold was made with Sabbat blood and tied its owner to him a little.

notes.title: He never left
notes.html: He never left the city. His cache is in a sewer under Bay View, and every totem he sold is his ear and his eye.

maximus.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
maximus.aliasText: Before the invasion half the Caitiff in the city wore a charm from a tattoo parlour in Bay View. The tattooist has vanished.
maximus.brief: Maximus McKenzie is a charming Scot with tattooed forearms who ran Charms & Needles, a tattoo parlour in Bay View. Through the back door he sold Union Caitiff and Anarchs cheap, effective blood-magic charms: wards, silencers, "luck in a fight". He vanished when the Sabbat invasion failed, and the Council would like a word.

jesselin.name: Jesselin
jesselin.html: She is Jesselin, a sorceress of House Goratrix, the Sabbat's Tremere. She scries the Chapel to learn what it has found under the null zone, means to take it, and with Maximus she corrupted the Mouse pack and poisoned the forest's places of power. The Chapel does not know she exists.

notes.title: Victor
notes.html: She gave Drake the way through the Chapel’s wards. Victor’s death is her work.

notes.title: Drake
notes.html: She whispered to Drake through his dreams for weeks before the invasion, and he opened the Granary’s doors to her himself.

jesselin.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
jesselin.aliasText: A new patroness at the opera, “Miss Lascelles”, never seems to be seen at lunch.
jesselin.brief: As "Miss Lascelles" she is a patroness of charity balls and opera boxes who lives under another name in a suite at the Pfister and lunches with a city councilman's wife.

ethan.name: Ethan Stone
ethan.sub: Blood Brother, archer and urban-combat specialist
ethan.html: A Gangrel among Brujah, he roosts on the roof of a grain elevator above the Menomonee Valley with a clear shot over half the gang's turf, and sleeps in an empty grain bin. He bought "charmed" arrowheads from Maximus McKenzie before the invasion.

notes.title: He kept one
notes.html: He still has one of Maximus’s blood-magic totems, and he has not thrown it away.

ethan.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
ethan.aliasText: Somebody on the Blood Brothers’ rooftops puts wooden arrows through hearts at forty metres.
ethan.brief: Ethan Stone is a Blood Brother: quiet, lean, with bowstring calluses. He specialises in rooftop and alley fighting and is a remarkably gifted archer; a wooden shaft through the heart at forty metres is his signature. Since Akawa's capture he and Wrecker have kept the Brothers from splitting.

dominique.name: Dominique
dominique.sub: Blood Brothers ganger, candidate for the Embrace
dominique.html: He was made a ghoul and seriously discussed for the Embrace, but Akawa's capture and the political turmoil put everything on hold. He does not like waiting.
dominique.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
dominique.alias: A kid who runs errands for the Brothers
dominique.aliasText: A Camarilla Kindred went to check on a Blood Brothers errand-boy in Riverwest and never came back.
dominique.brief: Dominique is an ordinary kid from the block who ran errands for the Blood Brothers. When a Camarilla vampire came to his flat, Dominique burned him down with a lighter and a can of air freshener.

dragos.name: Dragos Dalca
dragos.sub: Sabbat elder, maker of the invasion army
dragos.html: He built an army of sculpted abominations from the homeless his servants trucked in from under the viaducts and from whatever came off the fish plant's conveyors. He kept his workshops in the Cudahy railside warehouses and in tunnels under the Menomonee Valley. Most of his creatures died in the fighting; nests and loners live on, especially underground.
dragos.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
dragos.aliasText: The thing on the late news really was a dragon. It is dead now.
dragos.brief: Dragos Dalca was the Sabbat elder behind this autumn's invasion, an old Carpathian master of flesh. He was the "Milwaukee Dragon" caught on the late news chasing three figures over the Kinnickinnic Avenue rooftops. Jade Riley killed him with her hands at the Lakeside fish plant, in front of hundreds of witnesses. Officially, an ammonia explosion.

notes.title: His apprentice
notes.html: His childe Castor survived and keeps the surviving creatures in the flesh tunnels.

notes.title: The vozhd
notes.html: Before he died he melted Parovich into a vozhd, a colossus of fused flesh that still lives in the Deep Tunnel drifts.

guillem.name: Guillem Velez
guillem.sub: Operational commander of the Sabbat in Milwaukee
guillem.html: He kept contact with the Sabbat's local collaborators (Parovich, Maximus, some Anarchs), recruited the shovelheads and ran the operation from a closed church in Walker's Point. The Camarilla found it empty: he left a day before the raid, and someone warned him.

notes.title: Where he hides
notes.html: A decommissioned yacht under a borrowed name in the McKinley marina, and the Black Water cistern under Walker’s Point. He never spends more than two nights running anywhere.

notes.title: Gnaw
notes.html: He keeps feeding a Bane called Gnaw with blood so that the Eagle Lupine keep raiding and the Garou and the Camarilla never make peace.

notes.title: What he waits for
notes.html: He is holding out for reinforcements from Detroit, or at least for a chance to take someone important with him. He knows where the vozhd is.

guillem.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
guillem.aliasText: The Camarilla has put a price on the Sabbat’s commander. Nobody has collected.
guillem.brief: Guillem Velez, a Lasombra, commanded the Sabbat's infiltration of Milwaukee: a Catalan with perfect manners and a soldier's bearing. When the invasion failed he went into the shadows with a handful of loyalists, and the Camarilla has put a price on his head.

castor.name: Castor
castor.sub: Dragos’s apprentice, keeper of the surviving creatures
castor.html: He hides in the flesh tunnels under the Menomonee Valley and feeds his master's surviving creatures. He thinks of them as his children.
castor.alias: A Tzimisce who keeps changing his face
castor.brief: Castor was Dragos's childe and journeyman: graceful, boneless, forever changing his face.

noemi.name: Noemí Santana
noemi.sub: Ductus of the Black Water pack
noemi.html: She guards Guillem Velez, though she does not like him.
noemi.brief: Noemí Santana leads the last true Sabbat pack in the city, the Black Water: three vampires and a couple of surviving shovelheads. Angry, funny, hungry.

hieronymus.name: Hieronymus
hieronymus.sub: Priest of the Black Water pack
hieronymus.html: He hears the vozhd through the stone and calls it "the Choir".
hieronymus.brief: Hieronymus is the priest of the Black Water pack. He performs the Vaulderie in a flooded cistern and preaches to the rats.

gunther.name: Gunther
gunther.html: He came in the 1840s, when the city was still Kilbourntown, and served Merik as a kind of gamekeeper: the man for errands beyond the city line. He was a friend of Erica, the Prince's wife, and through her of the Mouse pack of Lupines. He is the last Kindred the Mouse ever trusted.

notes.title: Mercer
notes.html: He still meets Mercer, the last Garou of the Mouse, at the boathouse.

notes.title: Erica
notes.html: He wants to know how Erica really died, and he suspects Merik. If it is true, he served her killer for half a century.

gunther.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
gunther.alias: An old Gangrel with a pipe
gunther.aliasText: There is a Gangrel who lives on the river above the dam and was in the city before it had a name.
gunther.brief: Gunther is red-bearded, with braids at his temples, a pipe that never leaves his hand and a leather coat that smells of smoke and lake. He lives in an old boathouse on the pond above the North Avenue dam and keeps to himself.

soraya.name: Soraya
soraya.sub: Recluse of the house that isn’t there
soraya.html: She cares for her sire, Lucretian Vane, who went mad studying the Malkavian madness, and she wants a way to give him back his mind.

notes.title: The voice
notes.html: In his ravings her sire sometimes speaks in the voice of the null zone.

soraya.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
soraya.brief: Soraya is tall, with eyes entirely black and a voice like turning pages. She keeps out of politics and rarely leaves her hidden mansion on Yankee Hill. She sometimes receives guests, the ones who manage to find the door, and pays for books with knowledge.

vane.name: Lucretian Vane
vane.html: He wanders the rooms of the house that isn't there, rearranging mirrors and talking to people who aren't present.
vane.brief: Lucretian Vane is Soraya's sire, a scholar who tried to dissect the Malkavian madness as a science and lost.

wolfgang.name: Wolfgang
wolfgang.html: He is one of a small group of vampire hunters. He builds their cars, traps and flamethrowers from spare parts in his two-bay garage, and started hunting after a customer vanished from his shop.
wolfgang.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
wolfgang.brief: Wolfgang is a taciturn auto mechanic in West Allis, oil to the elbows.

rudeus.name: Rudeus Frost
rudeus.html: He fights with a sword alongside Wolfgang and Doctor Fire. There is faerie blood in his family, so he sees more than he should and is not afraid of what he ought to fear.

notes.title: A well-wisher
notes.html: Ivory sees kin in him and quietly helps the group: hints, luck, sometimes a dream on the right night.

rudeus.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
rudeus.brief: Rudeus Frost is a huge, loud Scandinavian who laughs in a fight and thinks hunting is the best way to spend a night.

drfire.name: Doctor Fire
drfire.html: He found more in old expedition notes than he was looking for and taught himself to conjure fire. He is the hunters' brain. His magic is crude and dangerous, first of all to himself.
drfire.src: From the chronicle canon; details improvised.
drfire.brief: "Doctor Fire" is a professor of archaeology at UWM.

agatha.name: Mother Agatha
agatha.sub: Matriarch of the Warrens, acting Nosferatu voice on the Council
agatha.html: She wants the creatures Dragos left in the tunnels rooted out, and she wants the Warrens' old understanding with the people who lived under the lake restored. The Nosferatu archive under the Journal building and the Rat Market both answer to her.

notes.title: The smell
notes.html: Some nights she smells something in the deep tunnels that reminds her of Parovich. She tells herself it is memory.

notes.title: The Pocket
notes.html: For decades the Nosferatu shared an impossible place under Lake Michigan with the city’s last sluagh changelings. Parovich’s treachery closed that door, and she wants it open again.

agatha.aliasText: The Nosferatu have a new voice on the Council, and she is not interested in being liked.
agatha.brief:
Mother Agatha has spoken for the Nosferatu on the Council since Parovich's fall. She is hunched and enormous, with a shawl over her hump. She ruled the Warrens under the city while Parovich sat at the table, and she rules them again.

She is ashamed of his treachery and makes sure the Council remembers it: as far as she is concerned the Nosferatu owe nobody anything now.

cricket.name: Cricket
cricket.html: He keeps the Nosferatu rumour archive in the basements under the Milwaukee Journal building, and answers to Mother Agatha.
cricket.aliasText: At the Rat Market there is a fidgety Nosferatu who keeps a card on everyone in the city. Possibly including you.
cricket.brief: Cricket is a young, fidgety Nosferatu with a face like an insect's. He taps telephone lines and police frequencies, keeps a card file on everyone in Milwaukee and sells what he knows at the Rat Market.

dust.name: Brother Dust
dust.html: For decades he visited the Michigan Pocket, an impossible cave under the lake, as a guest of the sluagh changelings, and helped them "carry" condemned buildings into it. Since Parovich went over to the Sabbat the door has been shut. He keeps watch on this side and hopes Ivory will open it one day.
dust.alias: A Nosferatu covered in stone dust
dust.brief: Brother Dust is a quiet Nosferatu coated in stone dust who keeps watch over a sealed door deep in the Warrens.

vozd.name: The vozhd in the tunnels
vozd.html: It moves slowly and hides well. The Black Water pack can hear it through the stone.
vozd.alias: Something huge in the Deep Tunnel
vozd.aliasText: Workers on the Deep Tunnel project have stopped going into one of the drifts.
vozd.brief: A vast mass of flesh that Dragos sculpted from ghouls, shovelheads and prisoners lives in the construction drifts of the Deep Tunnel. There is a mind in it.

notes.title: Parovich
notes.html: One of the faces in its flank belongs to Parovich. The former Primogen was not destroyed: Dragos melted him into the vozhd as punishment and as a spare brain. He remembers everything and sometimes speaks through its mouths.

mercer.name: Mercer
mercer.sub: The last Garou of the Mouse clan
mercer.html: He says little, makes dry jokes at the wrong moment and drinks coffee by the litre. Every night he goes down into the dying Granary, lights the candle-stubs and talks to Grandmother Mouse, who doesn’t answer. He doesn’t trust Kindred, with one exception.

notes.title: Wants now
notes.html: To cleanse the Granary, wake Grandmother Mouse, and find out where Jesselin and Maximus McKenzie are now.

notes.title: Pressure & secret · Storyteller
notes.html: He meets the Gangrel Gunther, Erica’s old friend, in secret: Gunther brings him news of the Kindred world, Mercer brings news of the Umbra. He also knows Drake is hiding in the tunnels under the city and has twice left food for him at an old manhole. He can’t bring himself to kill him, or to tell Horatio.

mercer.brief: Around forty, wiry, bespectacled, a night technician at the telephone exchange. He ran phone lines into the Warrens while the others still used notes, and he survived only because on the night of the massacre he was up a pole on the far side of the city.

esau.name: Esau
esau.html: He coaches Turk and the Union against the Blood Brothers, and Turk calls him "the man". He visited Sir Edward Scott regularly and planted thoughts about Lucina. He treats Gracis as pretentious and Jason as untrustworthy.
esau.aliasText: There is an old Kindred with a lot of hair and a lot of opinions who seems to know where every Anarch grudge is buried.
esau.brief: Esau is an old Malkavian, hairy and threatening, with an expensive condo just north of downtown. He says the city's evils are the work of his brother Jacob, a liar mad for power, and that together you can bring him down.

notes.title: One Kindred
notes.html: Esau is Jacob. There is only one of them.

pg-invasion.title: This autumn
pg-invasion.html: You were Embraced into a city at war with itself. This is what everyone says happened; nobody tells it the same way twice.

pg-strife.title: What every neonate is told
pg-strife.html:
Some thirty or forty Kindred hold a city of 628,000 under a permanent Lupine siege. Every road and railway out of town runs through Werewolf country, so few Kindred come in and fewer leave. Since October there has been no Prince.

The rules you were taught. Keep the Masquerade, especially now. Never cross the Anubi line without Decker's say-so. Do not fight at the Zoo, at West Milwaukee Park or in Elysium. In Union turf, travel in groups. Leave Old St. Mary's alone. Stay away from the Army Reserve Center. Ask before you hunt in another Kindred's domain.

pg-outside.title: Outside pressure
pg-outside.html: Chicago is watching. Its Prince would like a friendlier ruler here, and some of his people are said to be buying influence already. Sheboygan and Green Bay covet the city, and the Anarchs of Madison would love to see it fall to the gangs.

pg-council.title: The Council of Elders
pg-council.html:
VentrueGracis NostinusWants the throne; hates Hrothulf
ToreadorLucinaUsually votes with Gracis
TremereCarnaOpenly supports Gracis
NosferatuMother AgathaSpeaks for the Warrens since Parovich's fall
BrujahJade RileyAppointed over the local Brujah; killed the dragon
MalkavianJasonThe swing vote; hears petitions from anyone
Gangrel(empty)Decker never took his seat
Before the invasion the Council was deadlocked three to three over Parovich's proposal to restore a seventh seat. Nobody knows yet how Mother Agatha and Jade Riley will vote, and every faction is counting.

pg-domains-note.title: Personal domains
pg-domains-note.html: Each Kindred’s own patch: where they sleep, hunt and expect to be asked first. Without a Prince nobody can grant a domain, so every claim here is held by habit, nerve or a Council member’s indulgence. Vacant and contested domains belonged to the dead. Toggle the Kindred domains layer (or press D) to see them on the map.

pg-pins.title: Reading the pins
pg-pins.html: Reading the pins. Colour shows who holds the site. Solid ring: a well-known address. Dashed: the area is known and the exact spot is a guess. Dotted: placed by rumour. Places you have only heard of appear as grey pins with "Unknown". Shift-click a category to show only that one.

pg-kindred-note.title: Names you know
pg-kindred-note.html: These are the Kindred, ghouls and mortals you have heard of. Some you know only as a rumour; the Storyteller will tell you more as you learn it. A † marks the destroyed.

pg-dream-near.title: Near and Deep
pg-dream-near.html: Near and Deep. The Near Dreaming keeps enough earthly geography for rivers and neighbourhoods to matter. Deep shows the inner stacks, the Ward’s distant ruins and the mountain’s upper rooms. Dotted threads tie a dreaming place to its mortal anchor.

pg-census.title: The census
pg-census.html: The census. Nine active local Kithain, and eight hidden survivors in Bedlam that only Ivory knows about. Visiting fae are rare individuals, not a second court waiting offstage.

pg-court.title: A community without a court
pg-court.html:
There is no baron, seneschal or council. Marta can refuse hospitality at her own hearth and Oren can refuse to lower his own bridge, but neither can tax the city or order anyone into battle. Once a month, whoever is willing meets for the Spare Chair Supper, with an empty chair for anyone not yet found. Nobody takes minutes. Three customs have taken hold:

  1. Ask before bringing anyone onto a trod.
  2. Never draw cold iron inside an offered refuge.
  3. Leave a newly found changeling’s mortal family out of disputes.

These are fragile agreements, not law. Breaking them costs you guides, repairs, invitations and shelter.

pg-fae-history.title: The history people disagree about
pg-fae-history.html: The fae still make things: they mend coats, rehearse bad first plays, build radios and teach children songs. What they have lost is the confidence that these acts add up to a future. Their great buildings survive in the Dreaming. Their institutions mostly do not.

pg-fae-next.title: What happens next if nobody intervenes

pg-fae-three.title: The city’s three disagreements
pg-fae-three.html: Who keeps the fire? The Hearth serves people who stay; the Counterweight helps people move through. Who owns something abandoned? Old promises still govern towers, roads and treasures whose keepers are dead. How much should be remembered? The survivors disagree about the war, and the chimera remember it vividly and often wrongly.

pg-shadow-note.title: Everything on this side is improvised
pg-shadow-note.html: Everything on this side is improvised. Real fires, massacres and demolitions anchor the haunts, and those are tagged History. Every named wraith, hall and byway is invented. Pale outlines are relics: buildings the living city has lost that still stand beneath the Shroud. Tempest shows the Nihils, the Sea of Shadows and the deep byways.

pg-citadel.title: A small Citadel
pg-citadel.html: A small Citadel. Milwaukee answers to the Chicago Necropolis across the lake. Four Legions keep a presence here, the guilds keep their halls, and the free wraiths of Walnut Street keep their own counsel. All improvised.

pg-legions.title: The Legions in Milwaukee
pg-legions.html:
IronThe CitadelThose who died of old age. Anacreon Vollmer’s own.
GrimSoldiers HomeThose who died by violence. Sergeant Reinholt and the Ninth Watch.
EmeraldHarbor mouthThose who died by accident. Centurion Dolan and the Lady Elgin.
PenitentCounty GroundsThose who died in madness or despair. Matron Grau.

pg-shroud.title: The Shroud
pg-shroud.html: Pale mist marks where the wall between the living and the dead is thin: cemeteries, fire sites, the harbor, Walnut Street, anywhere recently drenched in death. Darkness marks where it is thick: the airport, the malls, glass-and-concrete federal buildings. Wraiths act more easily where it is thin.

pg-touch.title: Where the worlds touch
pg-touch.html: The Everett Street depot is the Hearse Train’s station on this side and the fae’s Waiting Platform in the Dreaming. The Pabst Building’s False Floor is a scar from the War of False Doorsis a mystery the wraiths avoid. Lorraine Hollis has heard of a sluagh child named Ivory, and the sluagh have always been able to hear the dead. Milo’s drain is not empty. Merik’s Gangrel wife Erica left no wraith: nothing of a destroyed vampire crosses.

pg-dead.title: The city’s dead
pg-dead.html: Milwaukee has buried its disasters well. On this side of the Shroud the ship still sails, the hotel still burns and the neighbourhood the freeway erased is still lit up on a Saturday night.

pg-dead-autumn.title: What the dead are doing this autumn
pg-dead-autumn.html: The real events (the Lady Elgin, the Newhall House fire, the Bay View massacre, the 1917 bombing, the clearing of Bronzeville, the 1991 poor-farm excavation) are history. Treat them with the weight they carry. Everything said about their dead here is invented.

pg-umbra-note.title: Everything on this side is improvised
pg-umbra-note.html: Everything on this side is improvised, built on the book’s Lupine material: Usla’s theft, the three clans and the relics buried under Marquette. Each coloured field is a spirit zone with its own law, and its number is the Gauntlet there. Dark smudges are Kindred havens as the spirits see them. Gateways shows the paths out to the Realms.

pg-clans-note.title: Three clans, one feud
pg-clans-note.html: Three clans, one feud. The book’s Lupines are the Coyote (all Red Talons), the Eagle (almost all Wendigo) and the Mouse (Glass Walkers, all but wiped out: only Mercer is left). Horatio Sims and Drake are the book’s; everyone else here is improvised. The Kindred most tangled with the spirit side are , whom the spirits take for a strange kind of Garou, and , who drinks Lupine blood.

pg-gauntlet.title: Reading the Gauntlet
pg-gauntlet.html: The number is the Gauntlet’s strength: the difficulty of stepping sideways. It runs from 1 in the Bog of First Waters, where the wall is nearly gone, to 8 in the Glass Thicket and the airport, where the Weaver has spun it thick. Over Marquette it swings between 2 and 9 from minute to minute. Every zone also has a law: a rule the local spirits enforce and that Gifts, rites and visitors must respect.

pg-spirit-history.title: The spirit-history of the city
pg-spirit-history.html: Milwaukee’s Umbra was shaped by one theft. When Usla stole half of two totems and buried them in himself, he set the Coyote and the Eagle against each other for three hundred years. Everything since, breweries, freeways, Merik’s schemes, has been built on top of that wound.

pg-spirit-autumn.title: What the spirits and the clans are doing this autumn

pg-clans.title: The three clans
pg-clans.html:
ClanCaernLeadsGarou
CoyoteGrinning Stone (quarries, NW)Horatio Sims~12
The strongest clan: lupus wolves who despise the human city; rational and cunning, they want the Eye back without a war. Now helping the Eagle clean the woods. Optional tribe reading: Red Talons.
EagleBleeding Pine (Root River, S)Agnes Hightree~8
Fewest and angriest; used to raid weekly; blame the Coyote; ridden by Gnaw. Secretly own the Seven Fires casino. Their forest is poisoned with Banes. Optional tribe reading: Wendigo (plus one Child of Gaia).
MouseThe Granary (Third Ward cellars), defiledMercer (the last)1
City Garou in human form; Erica’s pack; some helped Merik. Nearly wiped out by the Sabbat and House Goratrix; the caern is dying. Optional tribe reading: Glass Walkers.
The book names its Garou only by totem. The tribe readings are one way to slot them into Werewolf: The Apocalypse; ignore them if you prefer the book’s vaguer Lupines. Real places anchor the zones (the breweries, the concrete Kinnickinnic, the Allen-Bradley clock, the Hoan Bridge, Cedarburg Bog, Holy Hill); every spirit in them is invented.

pg-under-note.title: The underground
pg-under-note.html: Under the city. The sewers, the old Miller and Pabst lagering cellars and the Deep Tunnel, still being dug three hundred feet under the river beds, are real. The Nosferatu live down here; everyone else needs a guide. A red dashed rim marks dangerous zones.

pg-below.title: Who walks under the city
pg-below.html: Who walks under the city. Mother Agatha rules the Warrens. Since the invasion the Nosferatu say the Sabbat left things behind in the southern and western tunnels.

pg-beneath.title: Beneath the pavement
pg-beneath.html: Under Milwaukee lie a century and a half of sewers, lagering cellars and the foundations of demolished buildings. The Nosferatu have always lived here. This autumn they got worse neighbours.

pg-pocket.title: The Michigan Pocket
pg-pocket.html: An impossible cave under the lake, where the sluagh carry the buildings the city has condemned. Two peoples the city didn’t want to see used to meet here. Now the door is shut, and Ivory watches over the Pocket alone.

pg-strife-st.title: A city of strife (Storyteller)
pg-strife-st.html: Some 30–40 Kindred hold a city of 628,000 under permanent Lupine siege. Few get in and none get out. Merik’s madness ended at the hands of the Mask, and every faction is now reaching for the throne.

pg-invasion-st.title: The Sabbat invasion · autumn 1991 (Storyteller)

pg-outside-st.title: Outside pressure (Storyteller)
pg-outside-st.html: Prince Lodin of Chicago wants a harsher ally on the throne, and his lieutenants Ballard and Capone are already buying in. Nicolai of the Chicago Tremere sends spies. Sheboygan and Green Bay covet the city, and the Council of Madison would make it an Anarch stronghold. The Nosferatu clan is sending agents to watch Parovich.

The seventh-seat vote stood at 3–3. Parovich wanted the seat to go to Hrothulf to shatter the Council and open the city to the Sabbat; the Sabbat came anyway and was beaten back. Now Mother Agatha sits for the Nosferatu and Jade Riley for the Brujah, and nobody knows how either will vote. These are Kindred dangers, not fae borders: a changeling can still ride a daytime bus out of town.

pg-below-st.html: Who walks under the city. Mother Agatha rules the Warrens; Ivory watches over the Michigan Pocket. Dragos’s creatures and the last Sabbat pack hide in the southern and western tunnels.
